(إذ) is an adverb of the past, attached to an implied (اذكر); the clause (تقول) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it; (للذي) is attached to (تقول); the clause (أنعم الله عليه) is the ṣila, and (أنعمت عليه) is conjoined to the ṣila. The clause (أمسك) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). (عليك) is either attached to an omitted ḥāl — as has been said about the lām in "سقيا لك" — or attached to (أمسك) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "keep to yourself"; (زوجك) is the mafʿūl bihi, and (اتق الله) is conjoined to (أمسك). (وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ): the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl), or of conjunction; (في نفسك) is attached to (تخفي); (ما) is the mafʿūl bihi; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (مبديه) its khabar, the clause being the ṣila of (ما). (وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ وَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشاهُ): the wāw is likewise circumstantial or a conjunction; (تخشى الناس) is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (أحق) its khabar; (أن) with what falls in its domain is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of a nominative as a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from the name of Allah. This i'rab has preceded in Sūrat al-Tawba, and we add here that it may be accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), attached to (أحق). Abū al-Baqāʾ chose a third view, namely that (أن تخشوه) [Translator's note: so in the source, citing the wording of al-Tawba 9:13; here the verse has «أن تخشاه»] is a mubtadaʾ and (أحق) its khabar fronted before it, the clause being the khabar of the name of Allah.
(فَلَمَّا قَضى زَيْدٌ مِنْها وَطَراً زَوَّجْناكَها): the fāʾ is resumptive; (لما) is a temporal adverb (ḥīniyya), or a linking particle including the sense of condition; (قضى زيد) is a verb and its fāʿil; (منها) is attached to (قضى); (وطرا) is the mafʿūl bihi. (زوجناكها) is a past verb and its fāʿil; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and the hāʾ the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position. "Fulfilling the waṭar" in the language is reaching the utmost of what the soul desires of a thing. (لِكَيْ لا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِي أَزْواجِ أَدْعِيائِهِمْ إِذا قَضَوْا مِنْهُنَّ وَطَراً): the lām is a preposition of cause; (كي) is a maṣdar-forming particle; (يكون) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (كي), and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by the lām; the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (زوجناكها), as a cause of the marrying. (على المؤمنين) is the fronted khabar of (يكون), (حرج) its delayed noun, and (في أزواج أدعيائهم) an adjective of (حرج). (وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا): (كان) with its noun and its khabar; the clause is parenthetical, or conjoined to what precedes.

* Benefits:
We promised you a full account of the story of the marriage of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha to Zaynab bint Jaḥsh. In fulfilment of the promise, and to refute the scaremongering stirred up by the doubters and those in whose hearts is disease and caprice, we say: the biography of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha has preceded, and that the Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jaḥsh to him. He had asked for her hand on his behalf, and ʿAbd Allāh and Zaynab disliked that, because they had previously thought the Prophet was asking for her for himself; then they consented, and he married her to him and paid her dower on his behalf: sixty dirhams, a headscarf, a wrap, a gown and a waist-wrapper, fifty mudds of food and thirty ṣāʿs of dates, as is related. It is worth noting that Zaynab was the daughter of the Prophet's paternal aunt; she was brought up under his eyes and enjoyed from his care what a daughter enjoys from her father. Had beauty held sway over his heart ﷺ, as the doubters claim, its strongest sway over him would have been the beauty of the virgin in her bloom and the freshness of her youth. He used to see her, there being no veil between him and her, and none of her outward charms was hidden from him; yet he did not desire her for himself, but desired her for his freedman. How then could her beauty captivate him and the arrow of love for her strike him after she had become the wife of a slave he had freed and favoured with freedom?
Moreover, it is not known in human nature that desire overcomes a person so that he falls passionately in love with one who is close to him, or with whom he lived in his childhood. How then can we allow ourselves to claim the existence of this desire in a man known for chastity and uprightness all his life, with the voice of Allah calling in his ear: «ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا»? Indeed, how would he allow himself to slide into this deep pit while he was preparing to spread a message and propagate the teachings of a new religion that differed from what his people were accustomed to and demolished the customs they were used to and the systems and rites they had laid down?
The fact is that he ﷺ paid no heed to Zaynab's refusal to be joined to Zayd and her aversion to him — and he knew full well that a marriage based on mutual repulsion lacks the natural harmony between spouses that is indispensable for concord to prevail between them and for married life to settle on the firmest foundations. But he wanted to carry out the command of Allah in erasing a bad custom of the Jāhiliyya that the Arabs followed at that time: giving the adopted son (al-daʿī) all the rights of a son and applying to him, against him and for him, all the rulings that hold for a son, even in inheritance and the prohibitions of lineage. His saying, the Exalted, has preceded on this matter, censuring the Arabs for what they held: «ما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم ذلكم قولكم بأفواهكم والله يقول الحق وهو يهدي السبيل». No one was more fitting than the Prophet for Allah to single out with this charge, which abolishes that custom and drives the Arabs to rid themselves of it. So, by revelation from Him, the Exalted, he set about breaking this custom and abolishing it: he compelled Zaynab to marry Zayd, his freedman and his chosen one, as a preparation for establishing a new law and carrying out a divine ruling from whose execution there was no escape. After Zaynab came to Zayd, she did not become docile and her pride did not soften; rather she was haughty towards him and held herself above him, and deliberately pained her husband's heart by holding herself above him in lineage and free birth. Zayd complained of this to the Prophet time after time, and the Prophet, in his tolerant character and pure qualities, would soothe Zayd's pain and say to him «أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله», until the command of Allah came and prevailed over all that, and He permitted Zayd to divorce her after the atmosphere of the house had turned into an unbearable hell — as the Exalted said: «لكيما يكون على المؤمنين من حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا وكان أمر الله مفعولا» [Translator's note: so quoted in the source; the verse reads «لِكَيْ لا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ»]. And He confirmed that, as will come, with His saying: «ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم ولكن رسول الله وخاتم النبيين وكان الله بكل شيء عليما».
In this way it can be said decisively that Allah the Exalted reminded His Prophet of what had occurred from him, to increase him in steadfastness upon the truth and to remove from him what had stirred in the breasts of the weak-minded. So He said: «وإذ تقول للذي أنعم الله عليه» — with Islam — «وأنعمت عليه» — with emancipation and freedom, with choosing him for your patronage and love, and with marrying him to your paternal aunt's daughter — and you exhort him when he complained to you of his wife's hurting him: «أمسك عليك زوجك واتق الله», and fear Him concerning her, for divorce will disgrace her and may hurt her heart; and observe Allah's right regarding yourself too, for perhaps you will not find anyone better than her after her. You say that while you know that divorce is inevitable, because Allah inspired you to carry out His command yourself, so that you would be a good example to those with you and those who come after you; but modesty overcame you in that, and the fear that they would say: "Muhammad has married the divorcée of his adopted son." So in this you «تخفي في نفسك ما الله مبديه» — of the ruling He inspired you with — «وتخشى الناس والله» — who commanded you to do all that — «أحق أن تخشاه». You should have proceeded with the matter from the first moment, hastening to carry out His word and establish His law. Then He made it clearer still with His saying: «فلما قضى زيد منها وطرا» — i.e. a need, through marriage — «زوجناكها لكيلا يكون على المؤمنين حرج في أزواج أدعيائهم إذا قضوا منهن وطرا», so that the unease would be lifted from the souls of the believers and they would find no constraint in themselves about marrying women who had previously been the wives of their adopted sons; «وكان أمر الله مفعولا».
This is the correct explanation and the sound interpretation of this story. As for what they related — that the Prophet passed by Zayd's house while he was away, saw Zaynab, something of her fell into his heart, and he said: "Glory be to the Turner of hearts", and Zaynab heard the glorification and passed it on to Zayd, so that it occurred to him to divorce her, and the rest of this nonsense from which the Prophet is far above — the verifying scholars have refuted it. Imam Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī said that it is not authentic, and that those who transmit it and argue by it for their claims in understanding the verse have not given the station of prophethood its due, and their minds have not grasped the essence of the meaning of authenticity. Ibn al-ʿArabī spoke at length on this, until he says:
«As for their saying that the Prophet ﷺ saw her and she fell into his heart, that is false. For he was with her at every time and place, and there was no veil at that time. How then could she grow up with him and he grow up with her, and he notice her every hour, and she not fall into his heart — except when she had a husband? She had offered herself to him and disliked anyone else, and that did not cross his mind; so how could a passion that had not existed arise anew? Far be that purified heart from this corrupt attachment! He, glory be to Him, has said: "ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم زهرة الحياة الدنيا لنفتنهم فيه" — and women are the most alluring of blossoms and the most fragrant of sweet herbs. He did not go against this regarding divorced women; how then regarding married women held in wedlock?» — until he says: «If it is said: for what reason did he say to him "أمسك عليك زوجك", when Allah had informed him that she would be his wife? We say: he wanted to test from him what Allah had not informed him of, namely his desire for her or his aversion to her; and Zayd showed him such repulsion from her and dislike for her as he had not known from him concerning her. If it is said: how can he command him to keep her when he knew that separation was inevitable — and this is a contradiction? I say: rather it is sound, for sound purposes, such as establishing the proof and knowing the outcome. Do you not see that Allah commands the servant to believe while He knows that he will not believe? So there is nothing, in the object of the command differing from the object of knowledge, that prevents commanding it, rationally or legally. This is among the precious points of knowledge, so accept it.»
Al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm said in Nawādir al-Uṣūl: «Allah reproached him only because He had informed him that "this woman will be one of your wives"; so how could he say after that to Zayd "أمسك عليك زوجك"? And fear of people took hold of you, lest they say "he married his son's wife", "والله أحق أن تخشاه".» Al-Naḥḥās said: «Some scholars said: this was not a sin on the part of the Prophet ﷺ. Do you not see that he was not commanded to repent or to seek forgiveness? A thing may not be a sin, yet something else is better than it. He concealed that in himself for fear that people would be tried by it.» It is related from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn that Allah had revealed to the Prophet ﷺ that Zayd would divorce Zaynab and that he would marry her by Allah's marrying her to him. So when Zayd complained to the Prophet ﷺ of Zaynab's character, and that she did not obey him, and informed him that he wanted to divorce her, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, by way of good manners and counsel: "Fear Allah in what you say, and keep your wife to yourself." This is what he concealed in himself; and the Messenger of Allah feared that some talk from people would attach to him concerning his marrying Zaynab after Zayd, who was his freedman, had he ordered him to divorce her. So Allah reproached him to this extent — that he feared people in something Allah the Exalted had made permissible — and informed him that Allah is more deserving of being feared.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark appears in the source although no opening mark precedes the report from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.]
The Master and Imam Muḥammad ʿAbduh said: «By Allah, were it not for the like of this report that the weak and the deceivers have introduced, nothing of what they aim at would have crossed the mind of anyone reading the noble verse. For the text of the verse is plain and clear; its meaning does not admit far-fetched interpretation, and nothing comes to mind from it except that the reproach was for delaying and lingering in the matter, and that what he was concealing in himself was that divine command issued to him to demolish that happiness [Translator's note: so in the source, «السعادة»; probably a misprint for «العادة», "custom"] deep-rooted in the souls of the Arabs, and to take up the pickaxe to demolish it himself — just as it was decreed for him to demolish their idols with his own hand for the first time at the conquest of Mecca, and as was his way in all the customs of theirs that he forbade. This which he was concealing in himself, Allah was going to disclose, by His command that He revealed to him in His Book and by marrying him to the wife of the one they used to call his son. Nothing prevented him [Translator's note: the source repeats «من»] from disclosing what Allah disclosed except the modesty of the noble and the deliberateness of the forbearing, while knowing that he would certainly do it — but with the help of time.»

dervis-irab:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(ما كانَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيما فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ): a resumption introduced to deny any constraint on him ﷺ in his marrying Zaynab, the wife of Zayd whom he had adopted. (ما) is negating; (كان) is a defective past verb; (على النبي) is the fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (حرج) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the delayed noun of (كان). (فيما) is an adjective of (حرج), and the clause (فرض الله) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قَدَراً مَقْدُوراً): (سنة الله) is a noun put in place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), because sunna means way and conduct; it also comes in the sense of nature, law, and manner, or its domain. This is what al-Zamakhsharī inclined to in his i'rab. Others chose that it is accusative as a maṣdar, or by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "like the way of Allah with the prophets who were before". More discussion on this point will come in the section on benefits. (في الذين) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "followed"; the clause (خلوا) is the ṣila of (الذين), and (من قبل) is attached to (خلوا). (وكان أمر الله): (كان) and its noun; (قدرا) is its khabar and (مقدورا) is an inherent adjective for emphasis, like يوم أيوم ("a most dire day"), ليل أليل ("a pitch-dark night") and ظل ظليل ("deep shade"). (الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ اللَّهِ): you may make (الذين) an adjective of the prophets, i.e. "among the prophets who passed away before, who conveyed the messages of Allah"; or you may cut it off and parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who…". The clause (يبلغون) is the ṣila, and (رسالات الله) is the object of (يبلغون).
(وَيَخْشَوْنَهُ وَلا يَخْشَوْنَ أَحَداً إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ حَسِيباً): (يخشونه) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لا) is negating; (يخشون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the Divine Name is the object of (يخشون). [Translator's note: the source does not parse (أحدا), which is the mafʿūl bihi, with the Divine Name excepted from it.] (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and (الله) is the fāʿil of (كفى) in position; (حسيبا) is a tamyīz (specification) or a ḥāl. (ما كانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجالِكُمْ): (ما) is negating; (كان محمد): (كان) and its noun; (أبا أحد) is its khabar, and (من رجالكم) is an adjective of (أحد). (وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً): the wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened. (رسول الله) is conjoined to (أبا أحد), or accusative by an implied (كان), indicated by the preceding (كان), i.e. "but he was the Messenger of Allah". (خاتم النبيين) is conjoined to (رسول الله). The khātam is the seal, with fatḥa or kasra on the tāʾ. (كان) with its noun and its khabar; (بكل شيء) is attached to (عليما).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم» — the verse — there is the device of al-talfīf (enfolding). In Muḥīṭ al-Muḥīṭ: talfīf among the rhetoricians is congruity (tanāsub); it consists in framing speech as teaching a ruling or a precept that the speaker did not intend to mention, his aim being only to mention a ruling included within the generality of the stated ruling whose teaching he made explicit. Clearer than this is to say that it is a general answer about one species of a genus all of whose species need to be explained; so the one answering turns from a specific answer to what he was asked about — explaining that species — to a general answer that includes clarification of the ruling asked about and of others that need explaining. For His saying «ما كان محمد ... etc.» is an answer to an implied question, namely someone's saying:
"Is not Muhammad the father of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha?" So the answer came, saying: "Muhammad is not the father of any of your men." What the answer required was to say "Muhammad is not the father of Zayd", and saying that would have sufficed; but He turned from it as a preparation (tarshīḥ) for reporting that Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, and this preparation is complete only by denying his fatherhood of any of the men; for he can be the Seal of the Prophets only on condition that he has no son who has reached manhood. So the objection does not arise that he had al-Ṭāhir, al-Ṭayyib and al-Qāsim, because they did not reach the age of men. Then He guarded that by His saying «من رجالكم», attributing the men to them and not to him. Thus the specific meaning was enfolded within the general meaning, conveying the total denial of fatherhood of any of their men, and within that was contained the denial of fatherhood of Zayd. Then there is another talfīf, namely His saying «ولكن رسول الله»: He turned from the word "prophet" to the word "messenger" for added praise, because every messenger is a prophet but not the reverse, according to one of the two views. So this is enfolding upon enfolding.

* Benefits:
The mafʿūl muṭlaq and the maṣdar:
The mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) is what is produced by the maṣdar, i.e. the effect, not the maṣdar that is the effecting. So applying the term maṣdar to the object involves a kind of leniency and a failure to distinguish between the effecting and the effect. To explain this: the forms of maṣdars are coined for the effect produced by the effecting of the agent, which is named by the word of the maṣdar, just as they are coined for bringing that effect about; otherwise figurative usage would be entailed in every mafʿūl muṭlaq, and there is no way to that, given the presence of the sign of literal usage, namely that its meaning comes to mind immediately without need of a contextual indication. And in not distinguishing between the effecting and the effect — even though Ibn Sīnā stated it explicitly — there is room for objection, because they belong to two different categories: the first to the category of action, the second to the category of being acted upon. Some of the verifying scholars said: the identity is an existent matter, but it does not preclude difference in concept; for the light produced from the sun in the house is one existent thing, but when it is attributed to the sun it is called "illuminating" (iḍāʾa), and when it is attributed to the house it is called "being illuminated" (istiḍāʾa).
[Translator's note: the I'rab section promises further discussion of (سنة الله) in the benefits; the benefits section addresses the mafʿūl muṭlaq and the maṣdar in general.]

dervis-irab:41-48.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْراً كَثِيراً): resumptive speech, introduced to show that remembrance (dhikr) has no limits at which it ends and stops; for there is no act of worship but that it has known limits and prescribed forms, except remembrance, which goes beyond the limits of time and place. (اذكروا الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ذكرا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and (كثيرا) an adjective. (وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا): an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (بكرة) is an adverb for the beginning of the day, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سبحوه); (أصيلا) is conjoined to (بكرة) and is an adverb for the end of the day. The secret of singling out these two, and of singling out glorification (tasbīḥ) for mention, will come in the section on rhetoric. (هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلائِكَتُهُ): a causal explanation of the preceding command to remember and glorify. (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate); the clause (يصلي) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (عليكم) is attached to (يصلي), and (ملائكته) is conjoined to the pronoun latent in (يصلي). (لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ وَكانَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيماً): the lām is of cause; (يخرجكم) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām of cause; the fāʿil is latent, the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (يخرجكم). (وكان): the wāw is parenthetical; (كان) and its latent noun; (بالمؤمنين) is attached to (رحيما), and (رحيما) is its khabar. The parenthesis serves to confirm the content of what precedes.
(تَحِيَّتُهُمْ يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ سَلامٌ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً كَرِيماً): a resumption introduced to set out what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter. (تحيتهم) is the mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is in construct with (تحية), as the annexation of a maṣdar to its object, i.e. they will be greeted, on the day of meeting Him, with "peace". The adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (يلقونه) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. (سلام) is the khabar of (تحيته) [Translator's note: so in the source, for (تحيتهم)]. The wāw is resumptive; (أعد) is a past verb with a latent fāʿil referring to Allah; (لهم) is attached to (أعد); (أجرا) is the mafʿūl bihi and (كريما) an adjective.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْناكَ شاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً): (إن) with its noun, and the clause (أرسلناك) is its khabar. (شاهدا) is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara); the anticipated ḥāl and its secret will be mentioned in the section on benefits [Translator's note: no section on benefits follows in this entry]. (مبشرا) and (نذيرا) are conjoined to (شاهدا). (وَداعِياً إِلَى اللَّهِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَسِراجاً مُنِيراً): (داعيا) is likewise conjoined to (شاهدا); (إلى الله) is attached to (داعيا), and (بإذنه) is a ḥāl. The secret of this metaphor will come in the section on rhetoric.
(سراجا منيرا) is likewise conjoined, and the expression is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) whose ruling will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ فَضْلًا كَبِيراً): conjoined to what precedes. (بشر) is an imperative verb and (المؤمنين) the mafʿūl bihi; (بأن) is attached to (بشر); (لهم) is the khabar of (أن); (من الله) is a ḥāl; (فضلا) is the delayed noun of (إن), and (كبيرا) is an adjective of (فضلا).
(وَلا تُطِعِ الْكافِرِينَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ وَدَعْ أَذاهُمْ): conjoined to what precedes. (لا) is the prohibiting lā; (تطع) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; (الكافرين) is the mafʿūl bihi and (المنافقين) is conjoined to (الكافرين). (دع أذاهم) is an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi, as the annexation of a maṣdar to its agent or to its object. On the first, the meaning is "leave their hurting you without retaliation"; on the second, "leave what they have hurt you with, and do not take them to task until you are commanded to" — and the command to fight came after that. (وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا): conjoined to what precedes; (على الله) is attached to (توكل). (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and (الله) is the fāʿil of (كفى) in position; (وكيلا) is a tamyīz (specification) or a ḥāl. Its like has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
Specification (al-takhṣīṣ):
He singled out the early morning and the late afternoon for mention in His saying «وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا» to show their merit and draw attention to them, because worship in them is more emphatically required of a person; just as He singled out glorification (tasbīḥ), which is one of the kinds of remembrance, to show its merit over the other remembrances. Al-Tirmidhī related, in his ﷺ address to Juwayriya, Mother of the Believers: «Shall I not teach you words to say: سبحان الله عدد خلقه، ورضا نفسه وزنة عرشه ومداد كلماته ("Glory be to Allah, as many times as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as much as the weight of His Throne and as much as the ink of His words").» Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī said in commenting on this ḥadīth: «I was asked long ago about the i'rab of these words and the reason for the accusative in them, and I answered that they are accusative as adverbs, by implying قَدْر ("to the measure of").» Sībawayh stated explicitly that among the maṣdars that are put in the accusative as adverbs is their saying زنة الجبال and وزن الجبل ("the weight of the mountains / of the mountain"). Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī composed a fine book on it called «رفع السنة عن نصب الزنة» ("Removing Drowsiness concerning the Accusative of al-Zina"). It is also said that they are parsed as accusative maṣdars; on this view some implied it as "I count His glorification by the number of His creation", and others implied it as "I glorify Him with a glorification equal to His creation when counted". Ibn Ḥajar said in [his commentary on] al-Mishkāt: «The first is clearer.» Others parsed it as accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). Further, al-Nawawī has a fine book on remembrances called «الأذكار المنتخبة من كلام سيد الأبرار»; so refer to it.
[Translator's note: the I'rab section promises discussion of the metaphor in (بإذنه) and of the simile in (سراجا منيرا) in the section on rhetoric; the rhetoric section here treats only the specification.]

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُظاهِرُونَ): the imperfect of ẓāhara, whose maṣdar (verbal noun) is al-ẓihār, with kasra on the ẓāʾ. It is — as in al-Qāmūs — a man's saying to his wife: "You are to me like my mother's back (ẓahr)"; and he has ẓāhara from her, taẓahhara and ẓahhara. They singled out the back rather than anything else because it is the place of riding, and the wife is the husband's mount. So in the saying of the one pronouncing ẓihār, "You are to me like my mother's back", there is an allusive metonymy (kināya talwīḥiyya), because one passes from the back to the mount, and from the mount to the woman, since she is the husband's mount. So it is as though the one pronouncing ẓihār says: "You are forbidden to me; you are not to be ridden, like the forbiddenness of riding my mother."
It is useful to quote what al-Zamakhsharī said on the meaning of "You are to me like my mother's back". He said: "They wanted to say 'You are forbidden to me like my mother's belly', but they alluded to the belly by the back so as not to mention the belly, the mention of which comes close to mentioning the private part. They made the allusion to the belly by the back only because it is the pillar of the belly; from that is the ḥadīth of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: 'One of them brings it on the pillar of his belly', meaning on his back. Another explanation is that approaching a woman with her back towards the sky was forbidden and prohibited among them; the people of Medina used to say: 'If you approach the woman with her face towards the ground, the child comes out cross-eyed.' So, in his aim of making the prohibition of his wife to him severe, the divorcing man among them likened her to the back; then he was not content with that until he made it his mother's back, so he did not leave [it at that] … the mother's back." [Translator's note: the end of the quotation appears truncated in the source.] The rulings of ẓihār are set out at length in the books of jurisprudence.
(أَدْعِياءَكُمْ): plural of daʿiyy, which is one who is ascribed to someone other than his father; faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle). But its plural on the pattern adʿiyāʾ is irregular, because afʿilāʾ is the plural only of a faʿīl whose final radical is weak when it is in the sense of fāʿil (active participle), e.g. taqiyy and atqiyāʾ, ghaniyy and aghniyāʾ. Although this is a faʿīl whose final radical is weak, it is in the sense of mafʿūl, so the regular plural would be faʿlā, like qatīl and qatlā, jarīḥ and jarḥā.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَلا تُطِعِ الْكافِرِينَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً): (يا) is the vocative particle; (أي) is a munādā (one addressed) that is a specified indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative [governed by] (يا); the hāʾ is for drawing attention; and (النبي) is a badal (substitute). (اتق) is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (ولا): the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is prohibitive; (تطع) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), the agent of (تطع) being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; (الكافرين) is the direct object; (المنافقين) is conjoined to (الكافرين). The clause (إن الله) gives the reason for the command and the prohibition and has no grammatical position; (إنّ) and its noun; the clause (كان) is its khabar (predicate); the noun of (كان) is latent, its implied form being "He"; (عليما) is the first predicate of (كان) and (حكيما) its second predicate.
(وَاتَّبِعْ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيراً): (واتبع) is conjoined to (اتق); (ما) is the direct object; the clause (يوحى) is the ṣila (relative clause), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent, its implied form being "it"; (إليك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يوحى); (من ربك) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause (إن الله) also gives the reason for the command — its i'rab has just preceded.
(وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا): conjoined to what precedes; (على الله) is attached to (توكل); (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (الله) is the agent of (كفى) in position; and (وكيلا) is a tamyīz (specification) — they have also allowed it to be parsed as a ḥāl.
(ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِنْ قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ): resumptive speech, introduced to answer the polytheists' claims that one of them had two hearts and so was more intelligent than Muḥammad; more of this discussion will come in the section on benefits. (ما) is negative; (جعل الله) is a verb and its agent; (لرجل) is attached to an omitted element that is the second object of (جعل), or to (جعل) itself; (قلبين) is the object of (جعل) in position, genitive in form by the redundant (من); and (في جوفه) is an adjective of (قلبين).
(وَما جَعَلَ أَزْواجَكُمُ اللَّائِي تُظاهِرُونَ مِنْهُنَّ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is negative; (جعل) is a past verb with a latent agent referring to Allah; (أزواجكم) is the first object of (جعل); (اللائي) is a relative noun, an adjective; the clause (تظاهرون) is the ṣila; (منهن) is attached to (تظاهرون) — it is made transitive with (من) only because it has been made to include the sense of distancing, as though it were said: distancing themselves from their wives by reason of the ẓihār; and (أمهاتكم) is the second object of (جعل).
(وَما جَعَلَ أَدْعِياءَكُمْ أَبْناءَكُمْ ذلِكُمْ قَوْلُكُمْ بِأَفْواهِكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes; (أدعياءكم) is the first object of (جعل) and (أبناءكم) the second object of (جعل) — the story of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha will come in the section on benefits. (ذلكم) is mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the [claimed] lineage; (قولكم) [the source prints «وقولم»] is the predicate; and (بأفواهكم) is a ḥāl, i.e. being in your mouths only, without having any reality.
(وَاللَّهُ يَقُولُ الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهْدِي السَّبِيلَ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (الله) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (يقول) predicate; (الحق) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "the true saying"; (هو) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (يهدي السبيل) predicate; (السبيل) is accusative by removal of the preposition, or a second object of (يهدي), as stated before.
(ادْعُوهُمْ لِآبائِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech, to show that ascribing every child to his father is more upright and more just. (ادعوهم) is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; (لآبائهم) is attached to (ادعوهم); (هو) is mubtadaʾ and (أقسط) predicate; and (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(فَإِنْ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا آباءَهُمْ فَإِخْوانُكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ وَمَوالِيكُمْ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, transformation [of tense] and the jussive; (تعلموا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم), the wāw its agent and (آباءهم) its object. (فإخوانكم): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and (إخوانكم) is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then they are your brothers"; (في الدين) is a ḥāl; and (مواليكم) is conjoined to (إخوانكم), i.e. your cousins — mawlā is applied to several meanings, among them the paternal cousin.
(وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ فِيما أَخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ليس) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (عليكم) is the fronted predicate of (ليس) and (جناح) its postponed noun; (فيما) is an adjective of (جناح); the clause (أخطأتم) is the ṣila; and (به) is attached to (أخطأتم).
(وَلكِنْ ما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً): the wāw is conjunctive; (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened; (ما) is conjoined to the (ما) in His saying (فيما), so its position is genitive. It may also be a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is omitted, i.e. "you are held accountable for it", or "there is blame upon you in it". The clause (كان الله) is circumstantial or resumptive.

* Benefits:
These verses contain many benefits, which we set out below briefly, referring whoever wants more of them to the extensive works.
1- The meaning of "and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites":
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Do not assist them in anything, do not accept any opinion or counsel from them, keep away from them and be on your guard against them, for they are enemies of Allah and enemies of the believers who want nothing but harm and opposition. It is related that when the Prophet ﷺ emigrated to Medina, he was eager for the Islam of the Jews — Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr and Banū Qaynuqāʿ — and some of them had pledged allegiance to him hypocritically; so he was gentle towards them, honoured their young and old, and when something ugly came from them he overlooked it, and he would listen to them; so [this verse] was revealed." It is also related that Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl and Abū al-Aʿwar al-Sulamī came to him and stayed with ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy, the head of the hypocrites, after the battle of Uḥud; the Prophet ﷺ had given them safe-conduct on condition that they speak with him. ʿAbdullāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ and Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stood up with them, and they said to the Prophet, while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was with him: "Give up mentioning our gods [with disparagement] and say that they have intercession for those who worship them, and we will leave you and your Lord." That was hard on the Prophet, and ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit us to kill them." He said: "I have given them safe-conduct." ʿUmar said: "Get out, under the curse and wrath of Allah." And the Prophet ordered them to leave Medina.
2- The meaning of combining two hearts:
The Prophet ﷺ stood one day praying, and a thought crossed his mind (khaṭara khaṭratan), so the hypocrites who were praying with him said: "Do you not see that he has two hearts: a heart with you and a heart with them?" Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from al-Ḥasan that he said: "There was a man of Quraysh called Dhū al-Qalbayn (the one with two hearts) who used to say: 'I have a soul that commands me and a soul that forbids me.' So Allah revealed concerning him what you hear." It is also related that there was among the polytheists one who claimed that he had two hearts, with each of which he understood — or that he reasoned better than Muḥammad's reason — and that he or someone else used to be called Dhū al-Qalbayn; and that the verse refuted this claim just as it invalidated the claims of adoption and ẓihār among the errors of the Arabs. In any case, the meaning of the fleshly heart is not intended.
Moreover, the word qalb (heart) is applied as a name for a lump of the fuʾād (heart) suspended by the aorta, or in the sense of the fuʾād absolutely. Some say that the qalb is the black clot inside this well-known pine-cone-shaped lump, as though meaning that this is the origin; then some made it a name for this lump, and some extended it and called this whole piece of flesh, even its fat and its membrane, qalb. It is also applied as a name for what is in the inside and interior of a thing, and as a name for an abstract thing, namely the human soul which reasons, perceives, understands, believes, disbelieves, is God-fearing, deviates, is at rest, softens, hardens, is in awe and fears; all these meanings have been attributed to it in the Qur'an. The basis of this is that the names of abstract things are taken from the names of concrete things. The thing by which a person lives and perceives intellectual matters and feelings — such as love and hate, fear and hope — has been given several names, among them al-qalb, al-rūḥ, al-nafs and al-lubb. There is another correspondence for the heart, namely that the heart of an animal is the manifestation and source of its animal life, and psychological feelings and emotions have an effect on the physical heart that a person feels. Whatever the correspondence that was the cause of the naming, the word qalb is used in the Qur'an in the sense of the perceiving soul and the reasoning spirit, by whose departure from him a person dies. Allah the Exalted said: «وبلغت القلوب الحناجر» (and the hearts reached the throats), i.e. the spirits, not these fleshly lumps that do not move from their place. And He said: «فتكون لهم قلوب فيعقلون بها» (so that they may have hearts with which to reason), i.e. souls and spirits; it is not meant that the physical heart is the organ of reason. And He said: «نزل به الروح الأمين على قلبك» (the Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon your heart), i.e. upon your rational soul and your perceiving spirit; the heart here does not mean the fleshly lump, nor the intellect, because ʿaql (intellect) in the language is a particular kind among the kinds of knowledge and perception, and it is not said that revelation descended upon it — although the reasoning soul may be called ʿaql just as it is called qalb. What belongs to the acts of the soul, or to its emotions that have an effect on the physical heart, may be ascribed and attributed to the heart, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم», and His saying: «ليجعل الله ذلك حسرة في قلوبهم», and His saying: «ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم».
The sura opened with the command to fear Allah, the prohibition of obeying the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and [the command] to follow the revealed revelation specifically; and after that came the saying of Allah the Exalted «ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين». What is meant by it is that a person cannot have two hearts with which he combines two opposites — seeking the pleasure of Allah and seeking the pleasure of the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Rather, he has one heart, which, if it is sincere in turning towards something, cannot turn towards its opposite with sincerity and devotion, so as to be at one and the same time devoted to Allah and devoted to the enemies of His religion. Of this kind is the saying of the poet, who gazed at the sky of this meaning:
لو كان لي قلبان عشت بواحد ... وتركت قلبا في هواك يعذب
(Had I two hearts, I would live with one and leave a heart to be tormented in love of you.)
In summary, the strongest of the interpretations mentioned about it is that they used to claim two hearts for Ibn Khaṭal [Translator's note: so in the source; other sources commonly name Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-Fihrī in this connection], so Allah denied the truth of that and joined it with the contradictory sayings they used to say, such as making adopted sons into sons and wives into mothers; and these three matters are mutually incompatible. As for the first, from the combination of two hearts it would follow that one of two meanings subsists in one of them and its opposite in the other — such as knowledge and ignorance, security and fear, and so on. As for the second, it is because the wife is in the position of service while the mother is in the place of honour, so it is incompatible for the wife to be a mother. As for the third, it is because sonship is rootedness and long descent in lineage, while adoption (al-daʿwa) is something attached and accidental to it, so the two are incompatible. He mentioned "the inside (jawf)" to depict thereby the image of the two hearts being combined within it, so that the hearer hastens to reject it.
Moreover, Allah the Exalted said here «ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه», and in another place He said: «رب إني نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا». He used jawf (inside) in the first and baṭn (belly) in the second, and did not use jawf in place of baṭn nor baṭn in place of jawf, although the two words are equal in signification, both are triliteral with the same number [of letters], and their pattern is also the same. So look at how the casting of words does its work!
3- The story of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha:
The exegetes are agreed that the saying of Allah the Exalted «وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم» was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Ḥāritha. His story, as related by Anas ibn Mālik and others, is that he was taken captive as a child, and Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām ibn Khuwaylid bought him and gave him to his paternal aunt Khadīja bint Khuwaylid; Khadīja gave him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who freed him and adopted him. He stayed with him for a time; then his father and his paternal uncle came to him to ransom him. The Messenger of Allah said to them: "Let him choose; if he chooses you, he is yours without ransom." Zayd chose bondage with the Messenger of Allah over his freedom. At that the Prophet said: "O company of Quraysh, bear witness that he is my son." When the Prophet married Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, who had been the wife of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha whom the Prophet had adopted, they said: "Muḥammad has married his son's wife." So Allah gave them the lie in that. The story, with a discussion of it, will come shortly in this sura.

dervis-irab:49-52.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا نَكَحْتُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتِ): (إذا) is a future adverb, and the clause (نكحتم المؤمنات) is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it. The meaning of (نكحتم المؤمنات) will come in the section on rhetoric. (ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ فَما لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ عِدَّةٍ تَعْتَدُّونَها): (ثم) is a conjunction denoting delay; (طلقتموهن) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural and the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma. (من قبل) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (طلقتموهن), and (أن تمسوهن), the interpreted maṣdar, is in construct with (قبل); what is meant by touching is intercourse. The fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذا); (ما) is negating; (لكم) is a fronted khabar (predicate); (عليهن) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (عدة); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (عدة) is genitive in form and a mubtadaʾ (subject) in position. The clause (تعتدونها) is an adjective of (عدة). (تعتدونها) is from counting (العدد), i.e. you complete its count — from your saying "he counted the dirhams, and he took them by count (فاعتدها)". (فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ وَسَرِّحُوهُنَّ سَراحاً جَمِيلًا): the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an implied condition); (متعوهن) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (سرحوهن) is conjoined to (متعوهن); (سراحا جميلا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The rulings on providing (tamtīʿ) are set out in the books of jurisprudence, so let whoever wishes refer to them there. The beautiful release is one in which there is no harm.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَحْلَلْنا لَكَ أَزْواجَكَ اللَّاتِي آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ): resumptive speech, introduced to single out the Prophet for what is best and purest, after he had given his wives the choice and they had chosen him. (إن) with its noun, and the clause (أحللنا) is its khabar; (لك) is attached to (أحللنا); (أزواجك) is the mafʿūl bihi; (اللاتي) is an adjective; the clause (آتيت) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (أجورهن), i.e. their dowers, is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَما مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ مِمَّا أَفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ): (وما) is conjoined to (أزواجك); the clause (ملكت) is the ṣila, and (يمينك) is the fāʿil of (ملكت). (مما) is a ḥāl explaining (ما ملكت); (أفاء الله) is a verb and its fāʿil — al-fayʾ is booty — and (عليك) is attached to (أفاء). What will make this clearer will come in the section on benefits. (وَبَناتِ عَمِّكَ وَبَناتِ عَمَّاتِكَ وَبَناتِ خالِكَ وَبَناتِ خالاتِكَ اللَّاتِي هاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ): conjoined to what precedes; (اللاتي) is an adjective, the clause (هاجرن) is the ṣila, and (معك) is an adverb attached to (هاجرن). These were singled out for mention to honour them, as the Exalted said: «فيهما فاكهة ونخل ورمان». (وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً إِنْ وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَها لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنْ أَرادَ النَّبِيُّ أَنْ يَسْتَنْكِحَها): (امرأة) is conjoined to the object of (أحللنا), i.e. "and We have made lawful for you a woman who offers herself to you without a dower"; as for a woman who is not a believer, she is not lawful for him if she offers herself to him. (إن) is conditional; (وهبت) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (نفسها) is the mafʿūl bihi; (للنبي) is attached to (وهبت); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "We have made lawful". (إن) is conditional, restricting the first; (أراد) is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis; (النبي) is the fāʿil, and (أن يستنكحها) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of (أراد). Istinkāḥ is like nikāḥ; one says نكحها and استنكحها. Al-Nābigha said:
وهم قتلوا الطائي بالحجر عنوة ... أبا جابر واستنكحوا أم جابر
(They killed the Ṭāʾī at al-Ḥijr by force — Abū Jābir — and married Umm Jābir.)
In the language it means joining and gathering; from it comes تناكحت الأشجار, when the trees lean and join one another. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
واستنكح النوم الذين نخافهم ... ورمى الكرى بوّابهم فتجدلا
(Sleep took possession of those we feared, and slumber struck their doorkeeper so that he fell to the ground.)
The second conditional clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, because the ḥāl is a restriction; for her offering herself to him does not make her lawful for him except by his wishing to marry her [Translator's note: the source repeats «نكاحها»]. It is as though He said: "We have made her lawful for you if she offers herself to you and you wish to marry her", because his wish is acceptance, and that by which it is completed. (خالِصَةً لَكَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): a maṣdar emphasising an omitted verb, i.e. "it is exclusively yours, an exclusiveness" (خلصت لك خالصة); the maṣdar has come on this pattern, as in العاقبة and الكاذبة. The agent of the maṣdar is latent, its implied form being "marriage by the word of gift"; and the al- is a substitute for the omitted pronoun, i.e. "marrying her being exclusively yours". Al-Zamakhsharī confined himself to this view. Al-Zajjāj and Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that it is a ḥāl from (امرأة), because it has been described and so become specific, in line with the well-known rule. It is also said to be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of (وهبت), i.e. "in the state of being exclusively yours, not anyone else's". It is not far-fetched that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "an exclusive gift". (لك) is attached to (خالصة), and (من دون المؤمنين) is a ḥāl. (قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما فَرَضْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِي أَزْواجِهِمْ وَما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ): the clause is parenthetical, confirming the content of what precedes it. (قد) is a particle of verification; (علمنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (ما) is the object of (علمنا); the clause (فرضنا) is the ṣila; (عليهم) is attached to (فرضنا); (في أزواجهم) is a ḥāl; (ما) is conjoined to (أزواجهم), and the clause (ملكت أيمانهم) is the ṣila. The meaning of this parenthetical clause is that Allah knows what must be imposed on the believers regarding wives and slave-women, and to what limit and in what manner it must be, so He imposed it; just as He knew the singling out of His Messenger with what fully serves the interest, so He singled him out with that.
(لِكَيْلا يَكُونَ عَلَيْكَ حَرَجٌ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً): (لكيلا) is attached to (أحللنا), or to (خالصة) in view of what it contains of the sense of the lawfulness being established and attained for him. (عليك) is the fronted khabar of (يكون) and (حرج) its delayed noun; (كان) with its noun and its two khabars. (تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشاءُ): resumptive speech, beginning the explanation of the ruling on his conjugal life with his wives after explaining their lawfulness to him.
(ترجي), i.e. "you defer", is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); it has also been read with hamza, (ترجئ). The fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you"; (من تشاء) is the mafʿūl bihi, and (منهن) is a ḥāl. (تؤوي), i.e. "you take to yourself", is conjoined to (ترجئ); (إليك) is attached to (تؤوي), and (من تشاء) is its object; i.e. the Prophet ﷺ was given the choice regarding his wives.
(وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكَ): the wāw is resumptive. (من) may be relative, in which case it is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause (ابتغيت) is the ṣila, the returning pronoun being omitted; the fāʾ is linking, as has preceded, because the relative noun has a scent of condition; and the clause (لا جناح عليك) is the khabar of (من). It may also be conditional, in which case it is in the position of an accusative as a fronted object of (ابتغيت), and His saying (فلا جناح عليك) is its apodosis. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (جناح) its noun and (عليك) its khabar.
(ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلا يَحْزَنَّ): (ذلك) is the mubtadaʾ — the reference being to the choice and to the leaving of the matter to his will ﷺ — and (أدنى) is the khabar. (أن) with what falls in its domain is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "nearer to their eyes being cooled", and it is attached to (أدنى). (أعينهن) is the fāʿil of (تقر), and (ولا يحزن) is conjoined to (تقر); i.e. "and nearer to the lessening of their grief, and nearer to the contentment of all of them", because he treated them equally in taking to himself, deferring, setting aside and seeking, so there was no preference or distinction among them in that. (وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِما آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَلِيماً): (يرضين) is conjoined to what precedes; (بما) is attached to (يرضين); the clause (آتيتهن) is the ṣila; (كلهن) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the nūn in (يرضين). (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يعلم) its khabar; (ما) is the object of (يعلم), and (في قلوبكم) is attached to an omitted ṣila of (ما), i.e. "what has settled in your hearts". (كان) with its noun and its two khabars. (لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّساءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ وَلا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْواجٍ): resumptive speech, introduced to explain what is lawful for him. (لا) is negating; (يحل) is an imperfect verb, nominative; (بك) [Translator's note: so in the source, for (لك)] is attached to (يحل), and (النساء) is the fāʿil. (من بعد) is a ḥāl; (بعد) is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, the meaning being "after the nine gathered in your marriage bond" — they are his full quota, just as four are the quota of his community. The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (أن تبدل) is an interpreted maṣdar conjoined to (النساء). The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (تبدل) [Translator's note: so in the source; تَبَدَّلَ is an active verb, and the latent pronoun is its fāʿil] is latent, its implied form being "you"; (بهن) is attached to (تبدل); (من) is a redundant preposition, and (أزواج) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the mafʿūl bihi. Ibn Zayd said: this is something the Arabs used to do — one of them would say: "Take my wife and give me your wife."
(وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكَ حُسْنُهُنَّ إِلَّا ما مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ رَقِيباً): the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (تبدل), i.e. "even supposing you were pleased with them". (لو) is conditional; (أعجبك حسنهن) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a delayed fāʿil. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «In this wording, "أعجبك حسنهن", there is evidence that a man may look at a woman he intends to marry.» (إلا ما ملكت يمينك): there are two views about this exception. The first is that it is excepted from (النساء), in which case two forms are permissible: the accusative as an exception, and the nominative as a badal (substitute) — which is preferable. The second is that it is excepted from (أزواج), in which case it may be accusative as an exception, or genitive as a badal from them according to the wording, or accusative according to the position. The clause (ملكت يمينك) is the ṣila of (ما); (كان) with its noun and its khabar; (على كل شيء) is attached to (رقيبا).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات ... etc.», calling the contract "nikāḥ" is a majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) whose relation is association, inasmuch as it is the way to it; similar to it is their calling wine "sin" (ithm), because it is a cause of committing sin [Translator's note: the source has «الاسم», a misprint for «الإثم»].
In His saying «تمسوهن» there is a kināya (metonymy) for intercourse. It is among the courtesies of the Qurʾān to refer to intercourse by metonymy with the words of touching (mulāmasa, mumāssa), approaching (qurbān), covering (taghashshī) and coming (ityān).
In His saying «إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين» there is iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person to the second person. The discussion of iltifāt has preceded in detail in more than one place. The secret of the iltifāt here is that it is a return to the original course of the speech: the speech began by addressing the Prophet with His saying «يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك» etc.; then it turned from address to the third person in His saying «إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها», to announce that this is something with which he was singled out and favoured, and that this distinction is an honour to him on account of prophethood. This is among the secrets of eloquence, so take note of it.

* Benefits:
On His saying «لا يحل لك النساء من بعد», we said in the section on i'rab that the adverb is indeclinable on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning. He meant "after the nine who chose you" and whom he left at his death. They are: ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, Ḥafṣa bint ʿUmar, Umm Ḥabība bint Abī Sufyān, Sawda bint Zamʿa, Umm Salama bint Abī Umayya, Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy bint [Translator's note: so in the source, for «بن»] Akhṭab of Khaybar, Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith al-Hilāliyya, Zaynab bint Jaḥsh al-Asadiyya, and Juwayriya [Translator's note: the source writes «جورية»] bint al-Ḥārith al-Muṣṭaliqiyya [Translator's note: the source writes «الصطلقية»] — may Allah be pleased with them. The meaning is that the nine in his case are like the four in ours.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ — (al-Farrāʾ said): Someone may ask: in what respect was the Prophet ﷺ commanded to have taqwā (fear of Allah)?
The occasion for it was that Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl and Abū al-Aʿwar al-Sulamī came to Medina and stayed with ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl and his like among the hypocrites. They asked the Messenger of Allah for things he disliked, and the Muslims were about to attack them. So there came down ﴿يَٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ with regard to breaking the covenant, because there was a truce between them; so he was commanded not to break the covenant; ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿وَٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ of the people of Medina in what they asked of you.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾: this was mentioned only because of a man called Jamīl ibn Aws, whose kunya was Abū Maʿmar. He had a good memory and memorised much ḥadīth, so the people of Mecca used to say: "He has two hearts and two minds," because of his memory. He fled in defeat on the day of Badr and passed by Abū Sufyān, who was with the caravan. He said: "How are the people, O Abū Maʿmar?" He said: "Some killed and some fleeing." He said: "Then what is the matter that one of your sandals is on your foot and the other in your hand?" He said: "I thought they were both on my feet." So their lie in saying "he has two hearts" became known. Then He joined to it ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ﴾.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزْوَاجَكُمُ ٱللاَّئِي تُظَاهِرُونَ مِنْهُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ﴾, i.e. this is false, just as your saying about Jamīl is false. If a man says his wife is to him like his mother's back, she is not so; and there is for it the expiation that Allah has appointed. His saying ﴿تُظَاهِرُونَ﴾ without doubling [of the ẓāʾ] was read by Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb. Al-Ḥasan read it (تُظَهِّرُونَ), doubled without an alif. The people of Medina read it (تَظَّهَّرون) with fatḥa on the tāʾ. All are correct and their meanings are close. The Arabs say عَقّبت and عاقبت, ﴿وَعَقَّدتُمُ الأيمَانَ﴾ and ﴿عَاقَدْتُمْ﴾, ﴿ولا تُصعِّرْ خَدَّكَ﴾ and ﴿لا تُصَاعِرْ﴾, "O Allah, لا تُرَاءِبى and تُرأبِّى" [Translator's note: so in the source]. Some people [Translator's note: the source has قولم, apparently for قوم] have read accordingly, saying ﴿يُرَاءُونَ﴾ and ﴿يُرَءُّون﴾, like يُرَعُّونَ. Some have read ﴿تَظَاهَرُونَ﴾, and it is a good form, though I do not know its chain of transmission.
And His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدْعِيَآءَكُمْ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ﴾.
In the Jāhiliyya, when one of them admired a man's toughness and cleverness, he would take him to himself and give him a share of his inheritance like that of a male child of his. They were attributed in lineage to them, so it would be said "So-and-so son of So-and-so" of the one to whom he had attached himself. So Allah said: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ قَوْلُكُم بِأَفْوَاهِكُمْ﴾, and it is false; ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾, other than what you have said.

farraa:5-5.t:
Then He commanded them, saying: ﴿ٱدْعُوهُمْ لآبَآئِهِمْ﴾, i.e. attribute them in lineage to their fathers. His saying ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَعْلَمُوۤاْ آبَاءَهُمْ﴾: then attribute them in the way you attribute your clients (mawālī) whose fathers you do not know: So-and-so son of ʿAbdullāh, son of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and the like.
His saying: ﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ﴾ in the mistakes you did not intend; the sin is only in what you did deliberately. His saying ﴿وَلَـٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾: (ما) is in the position of a genitive, referred back [as maʿṭūf (conjoined)] to the (ما) that goes with الخطأ [i.e. فيما أخطأتم به].

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوْلَىٰ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdullāh or Ubayy it is (النَّبيُّ أَوْلَى بالمؤمنينَ من أنفسهم وهو أب لهم) ("and he is a father to them"), and so is every prophet. This came about because the Muslims had been made brothers to one another, and when a man died, the brother with whom he had been paired would inherit from him to the exclusion of his agnates (ʿaṣaba) and relatives. So Allah sent down ﴿النَّبىّ أَوْلَى مِنَ﴾ the Muslims in this standing, and he does not inherit from them — so how should the paired brother inherit from his brother! And He sent down ﴿وَأُوْلُو ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾ in inheritance ﴿فِي كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. that is in the Preserved Tablet with Allah.
His saying ﴿مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ﴾: if you wish, you take (من) as having come in for (أولى): some of them are more entitled to others than the believers and the emigrants are, one to another. And if you wish, you take it — meaning مِن — as intending: those related by blood, from among the believers and the emigrants, are more entitled to inheritance.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً وَجُنُوداً لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾: He means: and We sent hosts of angels which you did not see. This was the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq), which is the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb).

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿إِذْ جَآءُوكُمْ مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ﴾: from the side facing Mecca; ﴿وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾: from the side facing Medina. His saying ﴿وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ ٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾: they swerved away from everything and turned to nothing but their enemy. His saying ﴿وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلْحَنَاجِرَ﴾: it is mentioned that a man among them would have his lungs swell until they raised his heart to his throat out of terror. His saying ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَاْ﴾: the thoughts of the hypocrites.

farraa:11-11.t:
Then Allah said: ﴿هُنَالِكَ ٱبْتُلِيَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُواْ زِلْزَالاً شَدِيداً﴾.
He says: they were moved, pushed towards temptation (fitna), but they were protected.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾: this was the saying of Muʿattib ibn Qushayr al-Anṣārī alone. They have related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a pickaxe from Salmān to a rock that had defeated them, and struck it three blows, with each of which there was something like a flash of lightning. Salmān said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I saw a wonder in them." He said: the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "In the first blow I saw the white [palace] of al-Madāʾin, in the second the palaces of Yemen, and in the third the lands of Persia and Byzantium (al-Rūm). Allah will surely open to my community as far as they reach." When Muʿattib saw the Confederates he said: "Does Muḥammad promise us that Persia and Byzantium will be opened to us, while one of us cannot go out to relieve himself for fear? Allah and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion."

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ مَقَامَ لَكُمْ﴾: the general readership reads it with fatḥa on the mīm, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who gave the mīm a ḍamma and said (لاَ مُقَامَ لَكُمْ). Whoever says ﴿لا مَقامَ﴾ seems to mean: no place of standing. Whoever reads ﴿لا مُقامَ﴾ seems to mean: no staying for you; (فَٱرْجِعُواْ).
All the readers we know have the wāw quiescent in (عَوْرَةٌ). It is reported of one of the readers that he read (عَوِرة) on the pattern faʿila, and it is a valid form. The Arabs say: قد أَعور منزلُك ("your dwelling has become exposed") when a weak point (ʿawra) appears in it, and أَعور الفارسُ ("the horseman has become exposed") when there is a gap in his defence open to a blow. Abū Tharwān recited to me:
* لَهُ الشَّدَّةُ الأُولى إذا القِرنُ أَعورَا *
(His is the first charge when the adversary leaves an opening.)
He means the lion. By saying "our houses are exposed (ʿawra)" they only meant: open to thieves, since they were empty of men. So Allah gave them the lie and said: they are not exposed.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا﴾: meaning the outskirts of Medina; ﴿ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ﴾: He says: a return to unbelief; ﴿لآتَوْهَا﴾: He says: they would have given the fitna. ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with a long alif. The people of Medina read it short, ﴿لأَتَوْهَا﴾, meaning: they would have done it. Those who lengthen it say: since the asking fell on it, the giving falls on it, just as you say: سألتنى حاجَةً فأعطيتُك وآتيتكها (you asked me for something and I gave it you).
The feminine in His saying ﴿لآتَوْهَا﴾ may also refer to "the deed" (al-faʿla), and the masculine would have been permissible had it come; just as you say about a thing a man does: قد فعلتَها، أما والله لا تذهب بها (you have done it [fem.]; by Allah, you will not get away with it), meaning the deed.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلاَّ يَسِيراً﴾: He says: they would not have remained in Medina after giving in to unbelief except a little, until they perished.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ﴾ is nominative [i.e. the verb is indicative], because there is a wāw with it, and when there is a wāw, there is an implied verb in the wāw [i.e. it is joined to what precedes], and the sense of (إذاً) is postponement, i.e. "and if they did that, they would not remain after you except a little, then (idhan)." In one of the two readings it is (وإذاً لا يَلْبَثوا) [Translator's note: the verse discussed here is in fact 17:76, ﴿وَإِذاً لَّا يَلْبَثُونَ خِلَافَكَ إِلَّا قَلِيلاً﴾; this entry is placed at 33:16 in the source], with the nūn dropped, intending the accusative (naṣb). That is permissible, because the verb is left aside, so it becomes as though it begins the speech, even though there is a wāw with it. The Arabs say: إذاً أكسِرَ أنفك (then I will break your nose), إذاً أضربَكَ (then I will strike you), إذاً أغُمَّكَ (then I will grieve you), when they answer a speaker with it. But when they say أَنا إِذاً أضرِبُكَ they put it in the nominative, and treat the verb as having more claim to its noun than إذاً, as though they said: أضربك إذاً. Do you not see that they say أظنُّك قائماً (I think you are standing), giving ẓann (thinking) its effect when they begin with it / 147 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker], but when it falls between the noun and its predicate they cancel it, and when it comes after the noun and its predicate they cancel it. Likewise an oath has an answer (jawāb) when it is put first, so one says: والله إنك لعاقل (by Allah, you are surely intelligent); but when it falls between the noun and its predicate they say: أنت والله عاقل (you, by Allah, are intelligent). Likewise when it is placed last it has no answer, because the speech began with something else. The Arabs may make the verb accusative with إذاً when it is between the noun and its predicate in the case of إنَّ alone, saying: إنى إذاً أضربَك (I would then strike you). The poet said:
لا تَترُكنِّى فيهُم شطيراً * إنى إذاً أهلِكَ أوْ أطيرَا
(Do not leave me among them a stranger; then I would perish or fly off.)
The nominative is permissible. It became permissible with (إنّ) and not with a mubtadaʾ (subject) without (إنّ) only because the verb can never be put first after إنَّ, whereas it could be put first if [إنّ] were dropped.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ is accusative by qaṭʿ (detachment) [Translator's note: al-Farrāʾ's Kufan term for what the Basrans call ḥāl (circumstantial)], i.e. from the nouns that have been mentioned: [those] mentioned of them. If you wish, from His saying ﴿يعوِّقونَ﴾ here at the time of fighting, and they are niggardly about spending on the poor Muslims. If you wish, from those who say to their brothers (هَلُمّ) ("come"), they being thus. If you wish, from His saying ﴿وَلاَ يأْتُونَ البأسَ إلا قلَيلاً أشِحَّةً﴾; He says: cowards in battle, niggardly in spending on the poor Muslims. This is the one I like best. The nominative is permissible as a fresh start (iʾtināf), but I have not heard anyone read it so. (أشحَّة) may also be in [the accusative of] blame, just as one puts the praised into the accusative [of praise]; like His saying ﴿مَلْعُونِينَ﴾.
His saying: ﴿سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾: they hurt you with words in time of safety; ﴿بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾: sharp.
The Arabs say صَلَقُوكم, but it is not permissible in recitation because it differs from it [i.e. the written text]. One of them recited to me:
أصْلقَ نَابَاه صِيَاح العُصْفورْ * إنْ زَلّ فوه عن جَواد مئشير
(His two canines rang out like a sparrow's cry, if his mouth slipped from a lively, frisky [steed].)
That is when canine strikes canine and you hear its sound.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَ عَنْ أَنبَآئِكُمْ﴾: about the news of the camp in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.
Al-Ḥasan read it (يَسَّاءلون) (asking one another), and the general readership has (يَسْألونَ), because they only ask others about the news; they do not ask one another.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ﴾: ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd used to read (أُسْوة) with ḍamma on the alif [i.e. the hamza] throughout the Qurʾān, while Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb gave it ḍamma in some places and kasra in others. They are two dialectal forms; the ḍamma is in Qays. Al-Ḥasan and the people of the Ḥijāz read (إسْوَةٌ) with kasra throughout the Qurʾān without varying. The meaning of "uswa (example)" is that they stayed behind him in Medina on the day of the Trench, while wishing in that that the Prophet ﷺ would be victorious, out of anxiety for their town. So He said: there was in the Messenger of Allah a good example, since he fought on the day of Uḥud. That is also His saying ﴿يَحْسَبُون الأحزْابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا﴾, so they are in fear and dread, ﴿وإنْ يَأْتِِ الأَحْزَابُ يَوَدُّوا لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بَادُونَ فى الأَعراب﴾ (He says: outside Medina). In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: (يحسبونَ الأحزابَ قد ذهبُوا، فإذا وجدوهم لم يذهَبُوا وَدُّوا لو أنهم بادُونَ فى الأعراب) ("they think the Confederates have gone, and when they find they have not gone they wish they were out in the desert among the Bedouin").
His saying ﴿لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو ٱللَّهَ﴾: He restricted it to the believers. Similar in restriction is His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ تَعَجّلَ فِى يَوْمَيْنِ فلاَ إثْمَ عَلَيْهِ وَمَنْ تَأَخَّر فَلاَ إثمَ عَليه﴾ — this is ﴿لمنْ اتّقَى﴾ the killing of game.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمَّا رَأَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلأَحْزَابَ﴾: they believed and said ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾; the Prophet, peace be upon him, had told them that they [the Confederates] would march against him. That is His saying ﴿وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلاَّ إِيمَاناً وَتَسْلِيماً﴾. And had it been وما زادوهم ("and they did not increase them"), it would mean the Confederates. [Translator's note: the apodosis "it would be correct" is implied; the source leaves the sentence as given.]
His saying: ﴿وَمَا زَادَهُمْ إِلاَّ إِيمَاناً﴾, i.e. looking / 148 a [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] at the Confederates increased them only in faith.
And He said in another sūra: ﴿لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكُمْ مَا زَادُوكُمْ إلاَّ خَبَالاً﴾; had it been مَا زادكم إلا خبَالاً it would have been correct, meaning: their going out would have increased you only in corruption. This is part of the breadth of Arabic that you hear.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَاهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: "rijāl (men)" is made nominative by (مِنْ). ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ﴾: his term [of life]. This concerns Ḥamza and his companions.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِغَيْظِهِمْ﴾: they had hoped to wipe out the Muslims because of their great numbers, but Allah set upon them a cold wind which prevented any of them from bridling his mount. The horses ran loose in the camp and their tent-ropes snapped, and Allah routed them without fighting, and the angels struck them.
That is His saying: ﴿إذْ جَاءتْكُمْ جُنُودٌ فَأَرْسَلْنَا عليهمْ رِيحاً وجُنُوداً لَمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾, meaning the angels.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَاهَرُوهُم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾: these are the Banū Qurayẓa. They were Jews and had helped the people of Mecca against the Prophet, peace be upon him. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (آزروهم) ("they supported them") in place of ﴿ظاهروهم﴾. ﴿مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ﴾: from their fortresses. Its singular is ṣīṣiya, which is the tip of a horn and of a mountain. Ṣīṣiya is without hamza.
His saying: ﴿فَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ﴾: meaning killing their men and sparing their offspring.
His saying: ﴿وَتَأْسِرُونَ فَرِيقاً﴾: all the readers agree on kasra on the sīn. تأسُرُون is a dialectal form, but no one read it so.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَرْضاً لَّمْ تَطَئُوهَا﴾: He meant Khaybar; they had not yet obtained it, and Allah promised it to them.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ﴾: the readers agree on reading ﴿مَن يَأْتِ﴾ with yāʾ, and they differ over His saying ﴿وَيَعْمَلْ صَالِحاً﴾: ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read it with tāʾ [i.e. تعمل], and al-Aʿmash and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it with yāʾ. Those who read with yāʾ made the second verb follow ﴿يَأْتِ﴾, since that is masculine. Those who made it feminine said: since the verb came after هُنَّ ("you women"), it is known to be for a female, so we brought it out according to the meaning. The Arabs say: كم بيع لك جاريةً (how many slave-girls were sold for you — masculine verb), but when they say كم جاريةً بيعت لك they make it feminine, and in both cases the verb belongs to كم; except that when the verb came after الجارية it was taken as feminine. Had it been masculine it would have been correct, because الجارية is explanatory [tamyīz (specification)], and the verb does not belong to it. One of the Arabs recited to me:
أيام أم عمرٍو من يكن عقرَ داره * جواءٌ عدىٍّ ياكل الحشرات
ويسود من لفح السّموم جَبينه * ويَعْرَ وإن كانوا ذوى بكرات
(In the days of Umm ʿAmr, whoever has the hollow of ʿAdī for the heart of his home eats vermin, his brow blackens from the scorching hot wind, and he goes bare, even if they own young camels.) And [also] جواءَ عَدِىٍّ.
Al-Farrāʾ said: I also heard it in the accusative. Had he said (وإن كان) ("even if he is") it would have been correct, and all are good.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَقْنُتْ﴾: with yāʾ; the readers did not differ over it.
His saying: ﴿نُؤْتِهَـآ﴾: the people of the Ḥijāz read it with nūn ("We will give her"). Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it with yāʾ ("He will give her").

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَخْضَعْنَ بِٱلْقَوْلِ﴾: He says: do not make speech soft; ﴿فَيَطْمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾, i.e. lewdness; ﴿وَقُلْنَ قَوْلاً مَّعْرُوفاً﴾: sound, not encouraging a lewd man.

farraa:33-33.t:
[His saying]: ﴿وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾: from al-waqār (dignity, staying settled). You say of a man: قد وَقَرَ فى منزله يقِر وُقوراً (he has stayed settled in his home). ʿĀṣim and the people of Medina read (وَقرْنَ) with fatḥa. That cannot be from al-waqār; but we consider that they meant: اقْرَرْن فى بيوتكنّ, then they elided the first rāʾ and its fatḥa was shifted to the qāf; just as they said: هل أحَسْتَ صاحبك (did you perceive your companion? — for أحسست), and as He said ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ﴾, meaning فظلِلْتم.
Some Arabs say واقرِرْن فى بيوتكُنّ, so if someone said وقِرنَ with kasra on the qāf, meaning واقرِرن / 148 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] with kasra on the rāʾ, shifting the kasra of the rāʾ (when it falls away) to the qāf, it would be a valid form. We have not found this, in either of the two forms, used in the speech of the Arabs except in فعلت، فعلتم and فعلنَ; as for the imperative, the prohibitive and the imperfect, no. But we have allowed it because the [final] radical in the feminine plural is quiescent in فعلن and يفعلنَ, so that was permissible. A Bedouin of the Banū Numayr said: يَنْحَطْنَ من الجَبَل (they come down from the mountain), meaning ينحطِطن. This strengthens it.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾: he said: that was in the period in which the prophet Abraham, peace be upon him, was born. A woman at that time would wear a shift of pearls not sewn at the sides. It is also said: she would wear garments worth a fortune that did not cover her body. So they were commanded not to do the like of that.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَٱلْمُسْلِمَاتِ﴾: someone may say: how is it that He mentioned the Muslim men and the Muslim women, when in meaning one of them would suffice?
That is because a woman said: "O Messenger of Allah, good is only for men; they are the ones who are commanded and forbidden," and she mentioned other things such as the pilgrimage and jihād. So Allah mentioned them [the women] for that reason.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلاَ مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْراً أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾: it was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jaḥsh al-Asadiyya. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to marry her to Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, and mentioned that to her. She said: "No, by the life of Allah! I am your paternal aunt's daughter and the unmarried woman (ayyim) of the women of Quraysh." So he recited this verse to her, and she accepted and submitted, and Zayd married her. Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, came to Zayd's house for some need and saw Zaynab in a shift and head-covering, and said: "Glory be to the Turner of hearts!" When Zayd came home, Zaynab told him the story, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ to complain of her to him. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is pride in Zaynab, and she hurts me with her tongue, so I have no need of her." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Fear Allah and keep your wife." He refused and divorced her, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, married her after that. Both things happened — Zayd marrying her and the Prophet, peace be upon him, afterwards — because people used to say "Zayd son of Muḥammad," whereas he was only an orphan in his care. So Allah showed them that he was not his father, since He had forbidden a man to marry his father's wife, or a man to marry his son's wife once [the son] had consummated the marriage.

farraa:37-37.t:
