His saying: ﴿وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ﴾ about marrying her ﴿مَا ٱللَّهُ﴾ will make manifest. ﴿وَتَخْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ﴾: He says: you feel shy before people; ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ﴾ that you should feel shy before Him.
Then He said: ﴿لِكَيْ لاَ يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِيۤ أَزْوَاجِ أَدْعِيَآئِهِمْ﴾.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُ﴾: in this, and in the nine wives, which were not lawful for anyone else. His saying: ﴿سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He says: this is a practice that has also gone before for others than you. David and Solomon had the wives we have mentioned, and they were favoured with that; so are you.

farraa:39-39.t: Then He said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسَالاَتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: We favoured them with that, meaning the prophets. (الذين) is in the position of a genitive if you refer it back to His saying ﴿سُنَّةَ اللهِ فى الذِينَ خَلوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾; if you wish, you make it nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf). The accusative of السُنَّة is by qaṭʿ (detachment), as in your saying: فعل ذلكَ سنُة (he did that as a practice). There is much like it in the Qurʾān. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: (ٱلَّذِينَ بَلَّغُوا رِسَالاَتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَخْشَوْنَهُ) ("who conveyed the messages of Allah and fear Him"). This is like His saying ﴿إنَّ الذينَ كَفَرُوا وَيَصُدُّونَ﴾: yafʿalu is joined to faʿala, and faʿala to yafʿalu. All are correct.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ﴾ is evidence concerning the matter of marrying Zaynab. ﴿وَلَـٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: its meaning is: but he was the Messenger of Allah. Had you made it nominative on [the reading] "but he is the Messenger of Allah", it would have been correct, and it has been read so. The preferred form is the accusative.
His saying: ﴿وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ﴾: al-Aʿmash and the people of the Ḥijāz gave it kasra, and ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan gave it — meaning the tāʾ — fatḥa. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (ولكن نبيّاً خَتَم النبيِّين) ("but a prophet who sealed the prophets"); this is an argument for whoever says ﴿خاتِم﴾ with kasra. Whoever says ﴿خاتَمَ﴾ means: he is the last of the prophets, as ʿAlqama read, according to what is reported of him, (خاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ), i.e. its end is musk. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym narrated to us from al-Ashʿath ibn Abī al-Shaʿthāʾ al-Muḥāribī, who said: ʿAlqama used to read (خاتَمُهُ مِسْكٌ) and say: Have you not heard a woman say to the perfumer: "Make its khātam musk for me," i.e. its end?

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: He forgives you, and His angels ask forgiveness for you.

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالاَتِكَ ٱللاَّتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is (وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالاَتِكَ وٱللاَّتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ). The emigrant women may then be from among the daughters of the maternal uncle and maternal aunt, even though there is a wāw, so that He said (واللاتِى). The Arabs qualify [a noun] with a wāw and without a wāw, as the poet said:
فإنَّ رُشيداً وابنَ مَرْوان لم يكن * ليفعل حتّى يُصدر الأمرَ مُصْدَرَا
(Rushayd, the son of Marwān, would not act until he had brought the matter to its proper issue.)
And you say in ordinary speech: إن زرتنى زرتُ أخاك وابن عمّكَ القريب لك (if you visit me, I will visit your brother and your cousin who is close to you), and if you say والقريب لكَ ("and the one close to you") it is correct.
His saying ﴿وَٱمْرَأَةً مُّؤْمِنَةً﴾: you make it accusative through ﴿أحْلَلْنا﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿وَٱمْرَأَةً مُّؤْمِنَةً وَهَبَتْ﴾, without (أن) in it, and the meaning of both is the same; as you say in ordinary speech: لا بأسَ أن تستَرِقَّ عبداً وُهبَ لكَ (there is no harm in your taking as a slave a slave who was given to you), and عبداً إن وُهب لك (a slave if he was given to you) — the same. Some read ﴿أَنْ وَهَبَتْ﴾ with fatḥa [on the hamza], on the basis of His saying ﴿لا جناح عليه أن ينكحها﴾ in [the matter of] her having given herself: no blame on him in her gift of herself. Whoever gives it kasra makes it a conditional (jazāʾ). It is like His saying ﴿لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنآنُ قَوْمٍ أنْ صَدُّوكُمْ﴾ and ﴿إنْ صَدُّوكُمْ﴾. ﴿إنْ أَرَادَ النَّبىُّ﴾ has kasra, and there was no disagreement over it.
His saying ﴿خَالِصَةً لَّكَ﴾: He says: this trait is exclusively yours and a dispensation not for the believers; it is not for the believers to marry a woman without a dowry. Had you made (خالصة) لك nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf), it would have been correct; as He said ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلاَّ سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾, i.e. this is a proclamation. Whatever is of the type سُنّة الله, صبغة الله and the like is accusative because it is connected to what precedes it, in the manner of حقّاً ("truly") and the like. The nominative is permissible, because it is like an answer: do you not see that a man says "ʿAbdullāh has stood," and you say حقّا when you connect it [to his words]? When you intend a fresh start, you make it nominative and cut it off from what precedes. This is the pure qaṭʿ (detachment) that you hear of from the grammarians.

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾: with hamza and without hamza, and both are correct. ﴿وَتُؤْوِيۤ إِلَيْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ﴾: this too is among the things with which the Prophet ﷺ was singled out: that he might assign to whichever of them he liked a day, or more, or less, and leave aside whichever of them he wished and not go to her. Before that, each woman of his wives had a day and a night.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَن تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾: He says: if you did not assign a day to any one of them and they were in that / 149 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker] equal, it would be more likely to please them and they would not grieve. It is also said: when they knew that Allah had permitted that to you, they were content, since it was from Allah. It is also said: it is more likely to cool their eyes [with contentment] if other women besides them are not lawful to you. All are good.
His saying: ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَآ آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ﴾: nominative and nothing else, because the meaning is: and each one of them is content. It is not permissible to make ﴿كلّهن﴾ a naʿt (adjective) [i.e. tawkīd (emphasis)] of the hāʾ [pronoun] in the giving, because it would have no meaning; do you not see that you say لأكرمنّ القوم ما أكَرمونى أجمعينَ (I will honour the people as long as they honour me, all of them), and your saying ﴿أجمعونَ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, though the example has أجمعين] has no meaning [with the object pronoun]. Had it had a meaning, its accusative would be permissible.

farraa:52-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ أَن تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: (أَنْ) is in the position of a nominative; as you say: women are not lawful to you, nor exchanging them. The readers agree on ﴿لاَّ يَحِلُّ﴾ with yāʾ. That is because the meaning is: nothing of women is lawful to you; for that reason the masculine verb was preferred. Had the meaning been for all the women, the feminine would have been better in Arabic. The tāʾ is permissible, since النساء appears overtly without مِنْ.
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ﴾: غير is accusative because it qualifies the people [addressed], who are definite, while (غير) is indefinite, so it was made accusative "on the verb" [i.e. as ḥāl (circumstantial)]; like His saying ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الأَنْعَامِ إلاَّ مَا يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّى الصَّيْدِ﴾. Had you put ﴿غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ﴾ in the genitive it would have been correct, because before it there is ﴿طعامٍ﴾, which is indefinite, so you would make their action follow الطعام, since the mention of the food returns in (إنَاهُ). As the Arabs say: رأيت زيداً مع امرأة محسنٍ إليها (I saw Zayd with a woman being kind to her — genitive) and محسناً إليها (accusative). Whoever says ﴿محسناً﴾ makes it a description of Zayd; whoever puts it in the genitive, it is as though he said: I saw Zayd with the woman to whom he is kind. When the ṣila (relative clause) belongs to the indefinite noun, you make it follow it, even though it is the action of something else. Al-Aʿshā said:
فقلت له هذه هَاتِهَا * فجاء بأدماءَ مقتَادِهَا
(I said to him: this one — bring her; so he brought a tawny she-camel, he leading her.)
He made المقتاد follow the case of الأدماء, because it is equivalent to your saying "a tawny one whom he leads"; so you put it in the genitive because it is a ṣila for it. It is also recited بأدماءِ مقتادِهَا, putting الأدماء in the genitive by annexing it to المقتاد; its meaning is: with the handful of him who led her. Similar to it in Arabic is your saying: إذا دعوتَ زيداً فقد استغثت بزيدِ مستغِيثِه (when you call on Zayd, you have sought help from the Zayd of the one who seeks his help); the sense of "Zayd" is praise, i.e. he suffices the one who seeks his help. It is not permissible to put it in the genitive on the model of your saying مررت على رجل حَسَنِ وجهه (I passed by a man handsome of his face), because this is not sound until you drop the pronoun referring back to the first, and say: حسن الوجه. It is wrong to say مررت على امرأة حسنِة وجهِها, while حسنِة الوجه is correct.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ﴾ is in the position of a genitive, made to follow الناظرين [as governed by غير]; as you say: كنت غير قائم ولا قاعدٍ (I was not standing nor sitting); and as you say to a guardian: "Eat of the orphan's property in a fair manner, غيرَ متأثّل مالا، ولا واقٍ مالكَ بماله (not amassing wealth, nor protecting your own property with his)." You might make المستأنسين in the position of an accusative, imagining that you make it follow غير, since you have separated the two with words. Likewise, any meaning that admits two forms, when you separate them with words, the second may take a case different from the first. Of that kind is your saying: ما أنت بمحسن إلى مَن أحسن إليك لا مُجْمِلاً (you are not doing good to one who did good to you, nor being gracious), putting المُجْمِل in the accusative or genitive: the genitive by making it follow المحسن, and the accusative by imagining that you had said ما أنت مُحسناً. One of the Arabs recited to me:
ولستُ بذى نَيْربٍ فى الصديق * ومنَّاعَ خَيرٍ وسبّابهَا
ولا من إذا كان فى جانب * أضاع العشيرة واغتابها
(I am not one who sows discord among friends, nor withholder of good and reviler of it; nor one who, when he is apart, neglects the clan and backbites it.)
And Abū al-Qamāqim recited to me:
أجِدُّكَ لستَ الدهرَ رائىَ رامةٍ * ولا عاقلٍِ إلاّ وأنت جَنيب
ولا مصعدٍ فى المُصْعدين لمَنْعِجٍ * ولا هابطاً ما عشت هَضْب شَطِيب
(Truly, will you never again see Rāma, nor ʿĀqil, except as one led along; nor go up with those going up to Manʿij, nor, as long as you live, come down the hills of Shaṭīb?)
And this verse is recited:
مُعَاوِىَ إننا بَشَرٌ فَأَسجحْ * فلسنا بالجبالِ ولا الحديدَا
(Muʿāwiya, we are human, so be gentle; we are not mountains nor iron.)
(الحديدا) is recited both genitive and accusative; most of what I have heard is the genitive. The accusative of المستأنسين may also be through an implied verb, as though He said: then enter not lingering for conversation. There may also be with the wāw an implied [verb of] entering; as you say: قم ومطيعاً لأبيك (stand up, and [do so] obeying your father).
The meaning in the exegesis of the verse is that the Muslims used to come in to the Prophet, peace be upon him, at the time of the midday meal, and when they had eaten they would sit for a long time and ask his wives for things they needed. That became hard for the Prophet ﷺ, until Allah sent down this verse. Some people spoke about it and said: "Are we forbidden to go in to the daughters of our paternal uncle except with permission, or from behind a screen? If Muḥammad dies I will certainly marry one of them." Then the fathers — Abū Bakr and his kin — stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we too not go in to them except with permission, and not ask them for things except from behind a screen?" So Allah sent down ﴿لاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ فى آبائِهنّ﴾ to the end of the verse. And concerning marriage He sent down ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللهِ وَلاَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا أَزْوَاجَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أبَداً﴾.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ بِغَيْرِ مَا ٱكْتَسَبُواْ﴾: it was revealed concerning the people of immorality and lewdness. They used to follow the slave-girls in Medina and commit lewdness with them. The Muslims were living in tents; they had not built or settled. A woman of the Muslims' women would go out to relieve herself, and one of the lewd men would accost her, thinking she was a slave-girl; she would shout at him and he would go away. The dress was the same, so the Prophet, peace be upon him, was commanded: ﴿قُلْ لأَزْوَاجِكَ وَبَنَانِكَ ونساء المؤمنين يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلاَبِيبهِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ فَلاَ يُؤْذَيْنَ [Translator's note: the source has بنانك for بناتك]. The jilbāb is the outer wrap (ridāʾ).
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn al-Muhallab Abū Kudayna narrated to me from Ibn ʿAwn from Ibn Sīrīn concerning His saying: {يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلاَبِيبهنّ﴾.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلاَبِيبِهِنَّ﴾ — thus: he said: she covers one of her eyes and her forehead and the other side, except the eye. [Translator's note: this continues the report from Ibn Sīrīn begun at the end of the previous entry.]

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾: the rumour-mongers (al-murjifūn) were from among the Muslims. Those whose hearts were being reconciled (al-muʾallafa qulūbuhum) spread rumours about the People of the Ṣuffa; they would slander the People of the Ṣuffa, alleging that it was they who were approaching the women, because they were unmarried. His saying ﴿لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾, i.e. We will certainly give you power over them and set you upon them.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us / 150 b [Translator's note: manuscript folio marker]: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said: they will not remain your neighbours in it except a short while, until they perish. It is also possible to make "few" a description of them, a description of the cursed, as though you said: except [as] few, cursed; because His saying ﴿أَيْنَما ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا﴾ indicates that they will become few and scattered.

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿مَّلْعُونِينَ﴾ is accusative as an [accusative of] reviling (shatm), and also "on the verb," i.e. they will not remain your neighbours in it except as cursed. The reviling is by way of a fresh start, as He said ﴿وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالةَ الْحَطَبِ﴾, for whoever reads it in the accusative. Then He said ﴿أَيْنَمَا ثُقِفُوۤاْ أُخِذُواْ﴾, beginning afresh; this is a conditional (jazāʾ).

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾: the readers have ﴿تُقَلَّبُ﴾; had it been read ﴿تَقَلَّبُ﴾ ("turn about") and ﴿نُقلَّبُ﴾ ("We turn about"), they would be two valid forms.
His saying: ﴿وَأَطَعْنَا ٱلرَّسُولاَ﴾: one pauses on it with the alif. Likewise ﴿فأَضَلُّونَا السَّبِيلاَ﴾ and ﴿الظُّنُونَا﴾: one pauses on the alif, because it is written in them, and they occur among verses ending in alif. I saw them in the copies of the Qurʾān of ʿAbdullāh without an alif. Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash used to pause on these words without an alif in them, and the people of the Ḥijāz pause with the alif. Their view is dearer to us, because it follows the written text. Had they been read in continuous recitation with the alif it would have been correct, because the Arabs do that. Some have read with the alif both in continuous recitation and in pause.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ أَطَعْنَا سَادَتَنَا﴾: one [word], accusative. Al-Ḥasan read (سَاداتنا), and it is in the position of an accusative.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿لَعْناً كَثِيراً﴾: the general readership reads it with thāʾ, except Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, who read it (وَٱلْعَنْهُمْ لَعْناً كَبِيراً) with bāʾ ("a great curse"); and it is so in the reading of ʿAbdullāh. Al-Farrāʾ said: We do not allow it — meaning كثيراً. [Translator's note: so in the source; the reference of "it" is unclear as written.]

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿لِّيُعَذِّبَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ وَٱلْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَٱلْمُشْرِكَاتِ وَيَتُوبَ﴾: accusative [subjunctive] by following [what precedes]; if you intend a fresh start (iʾtināf) with it, you make it nominative [indicative], as He said ﴿لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فى الأرْحَامِِ﴾. However, the reading is (وَيَتُوبَ) in the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: «اللاتي»: naʿt (adjective) of «أزواجك». «ما»: a relative noun conjoined to «أزواجك». The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يستنكحها» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «أراد». «خالصة»: ḥāl from the hāʾ in «يستنكحها». The preposition «لك» is attached to «خالصة». The preposition «من دون» is attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خالصة». The clause «وهبت» is a second naʿt of «امرأة», and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: then she is lawful for him. The clause «إن أراد النبي» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «وهبت», and the clause «قد علمنا» is parenthetical between the preposition and what it is attached to. The interpreted maṣdar «لكيلا يكون» is genitive, attached to «خالصة». The preposition «عليك» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «يكون». The clause «وكان الله غفورا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The preposition «منهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَن». His words «ومَن ابتغيت»: «مَن» is conditional, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and the clause «ابتغيت» is conjoined to the clause «تؤوي». The clause «فلا جناح عليك» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The clause «ذلك أدنى» is resumptive. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تقرَّ» is accusative by removal of the preposition (إلى). «كلهن»: tawkīd (emphasis) of the fāʿil (agent) in «يرضين». The clause «والله يعلم» is resumptive. The preposition «في قلوبكم» is attached to the implied ṣila (relative clause). The clause «وكان الله عليما» is conjoined to the clause «الله يعلم», and «حليما» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تبدل» is conjoined to «النساء»; «أزواج» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The wāw in «ولو» is circumstantial; «لو» is a non-jussive conditional particle, and the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, i.e.: exchanging is not lawful for you. This wāw conjoins to an implied ḥāl (circumstantial) for exhaustiveness, i.e.: it is not lawful for you in any state, even in this state. The clause «ولو أعجبك» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «تبدَّل». «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «ما» is a relative noun, badal (substitute) of «النساء». The clause «وكان الله رقيبا» is resumptive, and the preposition «على كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رقيبا».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «لا تدخلوا» is the response to the vocative, resumptive. «إلا» is for restriction. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يؤذن» is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ), [the bāʾ being] attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied ḥāl (circumstantial): "accompanied by permission". The preposition «إلى طعام» is attached to «يؤذن». «غير»: ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم». «إناه»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «ناظرين». The clause «ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا» is conjoined to the response to the vocative. The clause «فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا» is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause, and the clause «طعمتم» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct). His words «مستأنسين»: a noun conjoined to «غير», and the preposition is attached to «مستأنسين», i.e.: do not enter it not waiting, nor seeking to settle in. The clause «إن ذلكم ...» is parenthetical. The clause «والله لا يستحيي» is conjoined to the clause «إن ذلكم كان». The clause «وإذا سألتموهن فاسألوهنَّ» is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause, and «متاعا» is a second object. The clause «ذلكم أطهر» is resumptive, and the preposition «لقلوبكم» is attached to «أطهر». The clause «وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا» is conjoined to the clause «لا تدخلوا», the response to the vocative. The preposition «لكم» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and the maṣdar «أن تؤذوا» is the noun of «كان». The second interpreted maṣdar «أن تنكحوا» is conjoined to the preceding maṣdar. The clause «إن ذلكم كان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The preposition «في آبائهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached, and the preposition «على كل» is attached to «شهيدا».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «صَلُّوا» is the response to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «لعنهم الله» is a khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The preposition «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُؤذون». The fāʾ in «فقد» is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause «فقد احتملوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين».

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «يدنين» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «ذلك أدنى» is resumptive. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يعرفن» is accusative by removal of the preposition (إلى). The clause «فلا يؤذين» is conjoined to the clause «يعرفن».

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «في قلوبهم مرض» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The clause «لنغرينَّك» is the response to the oath. The clause «ثم لا يجاورونك» is conjoined to the response to the oath. «قليلا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: «ملعونين»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) (أَذمُّ, "I condemn"). «أينما»: a jussive conditional noun, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause (أذمُّ ملعونين) is resumptive, and the conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: «سنة»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, i.e.: Allah established that as a practice (سَنَّ الله ذلك سنة). The preposition «في الذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سنة». The clause «سنَّ الله سنة» is resumptive, and the clause «ولن تجد» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The clause «وما يدريك» is conjoined to the resumptive [clause] «قل», and the clause «لعل الساعة تكون» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يدريك», which is suspended [from operating] by «لعل».

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: «خالدين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {لَهُمْ}. The clause «لا يجدون» is a second ḥāl from the pronoun in {لَهُمْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the following «يقولون». The clause «يقولون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in {يَجِدُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The clause «وقالوا» is conjoined to the clause {يَقُولُونَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: «ضعفين»: second object. The preposition «من العذاب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ضعفين».

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «وكان عند الله وجيها» is resumptive, and the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وجيها».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «يصلح» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, and the conditional clause is resumptive. The clause «يطع» is a khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يحملنها» is the object of «أبين».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليعذب» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «حملها» in the preceding verse. The clause «وكان الله غفورا» is resumptive; «رحيما» is a second khabar (predicate) of «كان».

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «النبي»: ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). «حكيما»: second khabar (predicate). The clause «إن الله كان» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «واتبع» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا تطع». The two prepositions «إليك» and «مِنْ» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يوحى». The preposition «بما» is attached to «خبيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition «بالله» is the fāʿil (agent) of «كفى», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). «وكيلا»: tamyīz (specification). The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The preposition «لرجل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل». «من قلبين» is the object of «جعل», and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). «في جوفه» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of قلبين. «اللائي»: naʿt. The preposition «منهن» is attached to «تظاهرون». The preposition «بأفواهكم» is attached to the maṣdar (قولكم). The clause «والله يقول» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ذلكم قولكم», and the clause «وهو يهدي» is conjoined to the clause «والله يقول».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «هو أقسط» is resumptive. The adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أقسط». The clause «فإن لم تعلموا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ادعوهم». His words «فإخوانكم»: the fāʾ is the linking one (rābiṭa), and the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم" (they). The preposition «في الدين» is attached to إخوانكم because it has the meaning of a derived word, i.e. "those who agree with you in it". The clause «وليس عليكم جناح» is resumptive, and the clause «ولكن ما تعمدت» is conjoined to the clause «ليس عليكم جناح». The preposition «فيما» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of جناح. «لكن» is for correction (istidrāk). «ما»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "you are held accountable for it".

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition «بالمؤمنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أولى», and likewise «من أنفسهم». The clause «وأزواجه أُمهاتهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «النبي أولى». «بعضهم» is a second mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «بعضهم أولى» is the khabar (predicate) of «أولو». The two prepositions «ببعض» and «في كتاب» are attached to أولى, and likewise «من المؤمنين». The interpreted maṣdar «أن تفعلوا» is a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ). The preposition «في الكتاب» is attached to «مسطورا».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: His words «وإذ»: the wāw is resumptive, and «إذ» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) «اذكر» (remember). The clause «وأخذنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause «أخذنا».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The interpreted maṣdar «ليسأل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَخَذْنَا}, and the clause «وأعدَّ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «اذكروا» is resumptive. The preposition «عليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نعمة». «إذ»: an adverbial noun, badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «نعمة». The clause «لم تروها» is an adjective (ṣifa). The clause «وكان الله ...» is parenthetical between the badal and the one it substitutes for. The preposition «بما» is attached to «بصيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, badal (substitute) from «إذ جاءتكم». The preposition «من فوقكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاءوكم», and the preposition (منكم) is attached to أسفل. His words «وإذ زاغت»: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «إذ جاءوكم», and the clause «زاغت» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «وتظنون» is conjoined to the clause «بلغت». «والظنون»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «هنالك»: a demonstrative, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ابتلي».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The wāw is a conjunction. «إذ»: an adverbial noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ}, and the clause «يقول» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «في قلوبهم مرض» is the ṣila (relative clause). «غرورا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a promise of delusion", and the second object is omitted, i.e. "victory".

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «إذ»: an adverb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «إذ يقول». The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of طائفة. The preposition «لكم» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «لا». The clause «فارجعوا» is conjoined to the clause «لا مقام لكم». The clause «ويستأذن» is resumptive. The clause «يقولون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الفريق», which is specified by the adjective. The clause «وما هي بعورة» is a ḥāl; «ما» operates like laysa, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar. The clause «إن يريدون إلا فرارًا» is parenthetical, and «فرارًا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يستأذن», and the clause «وما تلبَّثُوا» is conjoined to the clause «آتوها». «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr). «يسيرا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "except a brief lingering".

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ولقد كانوا عاهدوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ}, and the clause «لقد كانوا» is the response to an implied oath. The clause «لا يُوَلُّون» is the response to the oath understood from «عاهدوا», and «الأدبار» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «إن فررتم» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. «إذًا»: an inoperative particle of response. «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr). «قليلا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «لا تمتعون» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "and if you did that, you would then be given enjoyment only a little".

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «مَنْ»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is «ذا». «الذي»: a relative noun, badal (substitute) from «ذا». The clause «إن أراد» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «ولا يجدون» is resumptive. The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object, and the preposition «من دون» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وليا».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «قد» is for verification (taḥqīq). The preposition «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المعوقين», and the preposition «لإخوانهم» is attached to القائلين. «هلم»: an imperative verbal noun (ism fiʿl amr) meaning "come", and its fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the addressees; the preposition «إلينا» is attached to «هَلُمَّ». The clause «ولا يأتون» is a ḥāl from those mentioned before. «قليلا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "except a little coming".

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «أشحة»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {يَأْتُونَ}, and the preposition «عليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشحة. The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا يأتون». The clause «ينظرون» is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, and the clause «تدور أعينهم» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «ينظرون». His words «كالذي»: the kāf is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a rolling like the rolling of the eye of one who…". The two prepositions «عليه» and «من الموت» are attached to «يغشى». The clause «فإذا ذهب الخوف» is conjoined to the clause «فإذا جاء الخوف». His words «أشحة»: ḥāl from the fāʿil of «سلقوكم», and the preposition «على الخير» is attached to «أشحة». The clause «أولئك لم يؤمنوا» is resumptive, and the clause «فأحبط» is conjoined to the clause «لم يؤمنوا». The preposition «على الله» is attached to «يسيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «يحسبون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in {يُؤْمِنُوا}, and the clause «لم يذهبوا» is the second object. The clause «وإن يأت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يحسبون». «لو» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is the object of «يودُّوا». The interpreted maṣdar «أنهم بادون» is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied «ثبت». The clause «يسألون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يحسبون». The conditional clause «ولو كانوا» is conjoined to the clause «يحسبون». «قليلا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "except a little fighting".

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The preposition «في رسول» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أسوة». His words «لمن»: a badal (substitute) from «لكم», attached to what that is attached to. «كثيرا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "much remembrance".

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «ما»: a relative noun, khabar (predicate) of «هذا». The clause «وصدق الله» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl). The fāʿil (agent) of «زاد» is the pronoun of the promise, and «إيمانًا» is the second object. The clause «وما زادهم» is conjoined to the conditional clause.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «صدقوا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجال». «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «فمنهم من قضى» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive «من المؤمنين رجال», and the clause «وما بدَّلوا» is conjoined to the clause «منهم من ينتظر».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The interpreted maṣdar «ليجزي» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ما بدَّلوا». The clause «إن شاء» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «أو يتوب» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يعذب».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «وردَّ» is resumptive. The preposition «بغيظهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, i.e. "bearing their rage", and the clause «لم ينالوا» is a second ḥāl from the relative noun. The clause «وكفى الله» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ردَّ», and the clause «وكان الله» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وأنزل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ردَّ». The preposition «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ظاهروهم», and the preposition «من صياصيهم» is attached to أنزل. The clause «وقذف» is conjoined to the clause «أنزل». «فريقًا»: an object of «تقتلون» placed first, and the clause «تقتلون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قلوبهم»; the linking pronoun is implied, i.e. "of them".

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «أورثكم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَقَذَفَ}, and the clause «لم تطئوها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أرضا».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «قل» is the response to the vocative, resumptive, and the clause «فَتَعَالَيْنَ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). His words «أمتعكن»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis of an implied condition. «سراحا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the maṣdar being تسريح.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The preposition «منكن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المحسنات».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The preposition «منكن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يأت», and the preposition «بفاحشة» is attached to «يأت». «ضعفين»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The preposition «على الله» is attached to «يسيرا». The clause «وكان ذلك» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «ومن يقنت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «من يأت». The preposition «منكن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يقنت», and the preposition «لله» is attached to the verb. «مرتين»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «لستن» is the response to the vocative, resumptive, and the clause «فلا تخضعن» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The fāʾ in «فيطمع» is causal, and the verb is subjunctive by an implied أن after the causal fāʾ; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a maṣdar derived from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there be no softness, and so desire". The clause «في قلبه مرض» is the ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The object of «يريد» is implied, i.e. "He wills this injunction in order to remove", and the genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يريد». «أهل»: one addressed in the vocative, a muḍāf, accusative; the vocative clause is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the two prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يتلى». «خبيرا»: second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «فروجهم»: the object of the active participle. «كثيرا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «أعدَّ» is the khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ} at the beginning of the verse.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «ما كان» is resumptive. «إذا» is a pure adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the "being" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) of kāna is attached. The interpreted maṣdar «أن يكون» is the ism (subject) of kāna, and the preposition «لِمُؤْمِنٍ» is attached to the khabar of kāna. The preposition «من أمرهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الخيرة». The conditional clause is resumptive, and «مَنْ» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The wāw is resumptive. «إذ»: an adverbial noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) «اذكر» (remember). The preposition «عليك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied "أعني" (I mean); «أمسك» does not pass over to it, because in this category the verb of an attached latent pronoun does not pass over to its own attached pronoun. The clause «تخفي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تقول». The clause «الله مبديه» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal relative, and «ما» is the object of «تخفي». The clause «والله أحق» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تخشى». The maṣdar «أن تخشاه» is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ). The clause «فلمَّا قضى» is conjoined to the clause «تقول». The two pronouns in «زوَّجناكها» are the two objects of the verb. The lām in «لكي» is a preposition of cause, and «كي» is a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām, attached to the verb «زوَّجْناكها». The preposition «في أزواج» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «حرج». «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to the implied apodosis (jawāb) indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "when they have accomplished their need of them, there is no blame on them", and the governor of «إذا» is implied, i.e. "the blame is removed when…". The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «قضوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «حرج»: ism (subject) of kāna, and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «على النبي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the preposition «فيما فرض» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «حرج». «سُنة»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb. The preposition «في الذين» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سنة الله». The clause (سنَّ الله سنة) is parenthetical, and the clause «وكان أمر الله» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «الذين»: khabar (predicate) of an implied «هم» (they). The clause «ولا يخشون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يخشونه», and the Divine Name is a badal (substitute) from «أحدا». The clause «وكفى بالله» is resumptive; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and «حسيبا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The preposition «من رجالكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of أحد. His words «ولكن رسول»: the wāw is a conjunction, «لكن» is a particle of correction (istidrāk), and «رسول» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied kāna. The clause «ولكن رسول الله» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ما كان». The clause «وكان الله عليما» is resumptive, and the preposition «بكل» is attached to «عليما».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «بكرة»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar «ليخرجكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصلِّي», and the clause «وكان» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يصلي».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «تحيتهم»: mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is «سلام». «يوم»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «تحيتهم», and the clause «يلقونه» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «وأعدَّ» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «تحيتهم سلام».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The preposition «إلى الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «داعيا», and the preposition «بإذنه» is attached to «داعيًا».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «وبشِّر» is resumptive, within the scope of the response to the vocative. The interpreted maṣdar formed from «أن» and what follows it is genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بشّر».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the fāʿil (agent) of «كفى», and «وكيلا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The conditional clause is the response to the vocative, resumptive. The maṣdar «أن تمسوهن» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause «تمسُّوهن» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī). The clause «فما لكم عليهن ...» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). «عدة»: mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the preposition «عليهن» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عدَّة». The clause «تعتدُّونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عدَّة». The clause «فمتِّعوهن» is resumptive. «سراحا»: stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the maṣdar being تسريح.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, exalted is He, {يَا أَيهَا النَّبِي}: أي is a singular vocative (one addressed), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma; ها is for alerting and is obligatory with أي. النبي is a naʿt (adjective) of أي that cannot be dispensed with, because it is the one addressed in meaning. Most grammarians do not allow it to be put in the accusative according to the position (of أي). Al-Māzinī allowed it, making it like your saying يا زيدُ الظريفَ, with الظريف in the accusative according to the position of زيد. But this (الظريف) is an adjective that can be dispensed with, whereas the adjective of أي cannot be dispensed with, so it is not good to put it in the accusative according to the position. Moreover, the adjective of أي is the one addressed in meaning, so it is not good to put it in the accusative. Al-Akhfash said: it is a ṣila (relative complement) of أي; but in the speech of the Arabs no singular noun is known as a ṣila of أي.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying وَكفى بِاللَّه وَكيلا: بالله is in the position of the nominative because it is the fāʿil (agent), and {وَكيلا} is accusative as a clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {وَالله يَقُول الْحق}: الحق is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He says the true saying". الحق may also be the object of the verb "to say".

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {وَلَكِن مَا تَعَمّدت}: ما is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ما in His saying {فِيمَا أخطأتم}. It may also be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "but what your hearts intended, you will be held to account for it".

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {إِلَّا أَن تَفعلُوا}: أن is in the position of the accusative by the exception that is not of the same kind as the first.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {وَإِذ يَقُول} and {وَإِذ قَالَت}: the governor of both is an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember, O Muhammad, when (they) say" and "when (a party) said".

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {إِن بُيُوتنَا عَورَة}: عورة is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it means "possessing exposure" (ذات عورة). It may also be an active participle whose origin is عَوِرة, then made vowelless for lightening. It may also be a maṣdar in the position of the active participle, as you say رجل عدل, i.e. عادل ("just").

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying {هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنَا}: its meaning is "come to us". This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; others say هلموا for a group and هلمي for a woman. The origin of هلم is ها المم: ها is for alerting, and المم means "make for us and come to us". But its use became frequent, so the connecting alif (alif al-waṣl) of المم was dropped when the lām took a vowel from the ḍamma of the first mīm at the time of assimilation, so it became ها لم. Then the alif of ها was elided because it was vowelless and the lām after it was vowelless, since the lām's vowel is accidental — just as the wāw is elided in قالوا الآن in the reading of Warsh: the lām has taken a vowel, but its vowel is not taken into account because it is accidental. Likewise the vowel of the lām of لم is not taken into account, and it follows its original state, so the alif of ها was elided because it is vowelless and the lām is originally vowelless. The hāʾ was then joined to the lām, and it became هلم as you see, and the mīm was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, as you say ردَّ and مدَّ. It has also been said that the alif of ها was elided only because it was vowelless and the lām was vowelless, before the vowel of the first mīm was thrown onto the lām, so it became هلمم; then the vowel of the first mīm was thrown onto the lām and it was assimilated into the one after it, and it became هلم as you see.
His saying {إِلَّا قَلِيلا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverb, its implied form being "except a little coming" or "except a little time". Similar to it is {مَا قَاتلُوا إِلَّا قَلِيلا}.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {أشحة عَلَيْكُم}: its pattern is أفعلة, the plural of شحيح, like رغيف and أرغفة; but the vowel of the first ḥāʾ was moved to the shīn and it was assimilated into the second; its origin is أشححة. It is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its governor is {والقائلين}, so it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in القائلين; this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. He also allowed it to be governed by an implied verb indicated by المعوقين, so it would be a ḥāl from the agent of the implied verb, as though He said "they hinder, being niggardly". He also allowed its governor to be {وَلَا يأْتونَ}, so it would be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in يأتون. He also allowed it to be accusative as dispraise (dhamm). According to the Basrans the governor may not be المعوقين nor القائلين, because (the ḥāl) would then be inside the ṣila (relative complement) of the alif and lām, and you would have separated them by His saying {وَلَا يأْتونَ الْبَأْس}, which is not inside the ṣila — unless you make {وَلَا يأْتونَ الْبَأْس} in the position of a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in القائلين; then أشحة may also be a ḥāl from that pronoun, governed by القائلين, because all of it is inside the ṣila of the alif and lām of القائلين. On the doctrine of the Basrans it is not good in any way for أشحة to be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in المعوقين, nor from the latent pronoun in يأتون, because {والقائلين} is conjoined to المعوقين and is not inside its ṣila; and أشحة, if you made it a ḥāl from the pronoun in المعوقين, would be inside the ṣila, and likewise ولا يأتون, so you would have separated the ṣila from the relative by the conjoined word. On the doctrine of the Basrans it is also not good for it to be governed by an implied verb which المعوقين explains, just as it is not permissible for المعوقين to govern it, because what is inside the ṣila does not explain what is not inside the ṣila; so understand that. The correct view is that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in يأتون, which governs it, and His saying ولا يأتون is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in القائلين, and both are inside the ṣila. Likewise, if you make both of them aḥwāl from the latent pronoun in القائلين, that is good, since both are inside the ṣila. As for its being accusative as dispraise, that is permissible.
His saying {أشحة على الْخَيْر}: a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in {سلقوكم}, which governs it.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying {وَمَا زادهم}: the hāʾ and mīm (i.e. the latent subject of زاد) refer to the looking, because the meaning of His saying {وَلما رأى الْمُؤْمِنُونَ} is "and when they looked". It is also said that the latent pronoun refers to the seeing (الرؤية); its being masculine is permissible because رأى indicates the seeing, and because its femininity is not real.
[Translator's note: the source says «الهاء والميم» (the -hum), though the pronoun referring to the looking/seeing is the latent agent of زاد; translated as written.]

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying {صدقُوا مَا عَاهَدُوا}: ما is in the position of the accusative by صدقوا, and it with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "they were true to the covenant", i.e. they fulfilled it.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying فتعالين: it is from العلوّ ("height"), and its origin is rising; but its use became so frequent that it came to be used in the sense of "come down", so one says to someone on high تعال, i.e. "come down".

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying {وَقرن فِي بيوتكن}: whoever reads the qāf with kasra takes it from الوقار ("dignity") and staying with dignity in the houses, so it is like عِدْن and زِنّ, because its first radical (fāʾ al-fiʿl), which is the wāw, is elided. It may also be from القرار ("staying"), and then it is a doubled verb: one says قرّ في المكان يقِرّ, which is the well-known dialect. Its origin would be اقرِرن; then the rāʾ that is the second radical (ʿayn al-fiʿl) is replaced by a yāʾ out of dislike of doubling, as they replaced it in قيراط and دينار; the yāʾ has kasra, so its vowel is thrown onto the qāf and it is elided because it is vowelless and the rāʾ is vowelless, and the connecting alif is dispensed with because the qāf has a vowel; so it becomes قِرن. It is also said that rather the first rāʾ was elided out of dislike of doubling, as they said ظلت, the origin being ظللت, and its vowel was kept on the qāf, and the connecting alif was elided, again because the qāf has a vowel. As for whoever reads it with fatḥa on the qāf, it is a dialect that Abū ʿUbayd reported from al-Kisāʾī, that one says قرِرت في المكان أقَرّ; it is a rare dialect, and al-Māzinī and others rejected it. Then the morphological weakening proceeds according to the two ways mentioned first for the kasra. It has also been said that it is taken from قررت به عينا أقرّ ("I was gladdened by it"), then weakened according to one of the two origins mentioned first; so know it.
His saying {أهل الْبَيْت}: accusative as a vocative, or, if you wish, as praise (madḥ). In ordinary speech the genitive is permissible, according to the Kufans, as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm in عنكم; that is not permissible according to the Basrans, because the absent (third person) is substituted for the addressee because of their difference. It is also said that it is not permissible because the badal is a clarification, and the addressee and the addressee do not need a clarification.
[Translator's note: the reasoning requires "the absent (third person) is not substituted for the addressee"; the negation seems to have dropped out of the source. Also «والمخاطب والمخاطب» is probably meant as "the speaker and the addressee" (المتكلم والمخاطب). Both are translated as written.]

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying {والحافظين فروجهم والحافظات}: He made the first of these two verbal forms govern. According to the rules of this chapter (of the conflict of governors, tanāzuʿ), had the object of the first verb been placed after (both), the analogical form would have been to say والحافظاتها. But since He placed it first, the pronoun was dispensed with because the meaning is clear — that the first is the one made to govern — since its object comes right after it and is not delayed until after the second verb. Omitting the pronoun here, when what the first governs is placed first, is good and eloquent; and keeping the pronoun, when the object of the first is delayed to the end of the sentence, is better and more eloquent. Similar to it by analogy is {والذاكرين الله كثيرا وَالذَّاكِرَات}: had the object been delayed to the end of the sentence, the proper form of the sentence would have been والذاكراته; but since it was placed first, omitting the pronoun became good, and keeping it in speech is permissible because it has been mentioned before.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {وَالله أَحَق أَن تخشاه}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أحق is its khabar (predicate), and أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition. If you wish, you may make أن and what follows it a second mubtadaʾ with أحق as its khabar, and the clause is a khabar about الله. And if you wish, you may make أن and what follows it a badal (substitute) for الله, exalted is He, (which is) a mubtadaʾ with أحق as its khabar. It is not permissible at all to assume an annexation of أحق to أن, because أفعل (the elative) is annexed only to that of which it is a part.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying {سنة الله}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by the meaning of what precedes it.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying {الَّذين يبلغون}: الذين is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for, or a naʿt (adjective) of, His saying {فِي الَّذين خلوا}.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying {وَلَكِن رَسُول الله}: رسول is the khabar (predicate) of an implied كان, its implied form being "but Muhammad was the Messenger of Allah". Whoever reads it in the nominative does so by implying هو, i.e. "he is the Messenger of Allah".

mekki-muskil:50-50.t:
His saying {وَامْرَأَة مُؤمنَة}: conjoined to الأزواج and what follows them, and the governor is أحللنا. Whoever reads أن وهبت نفسها with fatḥa on أن — which is transmitted from al-Ḥasan — makes أن a badal (substitute) for امرأة. It is also said that it is by omission of the preposition, i.e. "because (لأن) she gave".
His saying {خَالِصَة}: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying {لكيلا يكون عَلَيْك}: the lām is attached to His saying أحللنا; it is also said: to فرضنا.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying {بِمَا آتيتهن كُلهنَّ}: كلهن is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun in يرضين. It may not be a tawkīd of the pronoun in آتيتهن, because the meaning is otherwise.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا ملكت}: ما is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for النساء, or in the position of the accusative by exception. It may not be in the position of the accusative by ملكت, because the ṣila (relative clause) does not govern the relative noun. In the sentence there is a hāʾ omitted from the ṣila by which the sentence is completed, its implied form being "except what your right hand possesses (ملكته)". You may also make ما and the verb a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the object; then the maṣdar is in the position of the accusative because it is an exception not of the same kind, and there is no need to omit a hāʾ, its implied form being "except the possession of your right hand", with ملك meaning "possessed", so it is like their saying هذا درهم ضرب الأمير, i.e. "minted by the emir".

mekki-muskil:53-53.t:
His saying {غير ناظرين إناه}: إناه is an adverb of time, and it is a metathesis of آن, which means "time": the nūn was moved before the alif, and the hamza was changed to the kasra. So its meaning is "not waiting for its time (آنه)", i.e. its moment; then it was metathesised and changed as I have mentioned.
His saying {غير}: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in لكم, governed by يؤذن. It is not good to make غير an adjective of الطعام, because that would require making overt the pronoun in ناظرين, so that one would have to say غير ناظرين أنتم إناه; for when an active participle runs as an adjective, a khabar (predicate), a ḥāl or a ṣila (relative clause) on someone other than the one to whom it belongs, the pronoun of the agent is not latent in it — while that is permissible in the verb. So had He said, in ordinary speech, إن أذن لكم إلى طعام لا تنتظرون إناه فكلوا, it would be permissible for لا تنتظرون to be an adjective of the food, or a ḥāl from the kāf and mīm in لكم. Do you not see that you say زيد تضربه: زيد is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and تضربه is its khabar, and it is a verb belonging to the addressee, not to Zayd, and the pronoun of the addressee is latent in it; were it not for the hāʾ, it would not be a khabar of Zayd, since nothing connected with him or mentioning him would refer back to him. But if in place of تضربه you put ضاربه, you would have to make the pronoun overt and say زيد ضاربه أنت. Likewise the analogy of الذي تضربه زيد: تضربه is the ṣila of الذي and contains the pronoun of the addressee; if you put ضاربه in its place you make the pronoun overt and say الذي ضاربه أنت زيد. The same applies to the adjective and the ḥāl in your saying مررت برجل تضربه and مررت بزيد تضربه: if in place of تضربه you put an active participle, you would have to make the pronoun overt in the adjective and the ḥāl, just as it was made overt in the khabar and the ṣila. This is the meaning of what I said to you: when the active participle runs on someone other than the one to whom it belongs, as a khabar, an adjective, a ḥāl or a ṣila, the pronoun must be made overt; while that (running on another) is permissible in the verb without making the pronoun overt. So understand it.
His saying {وَلَا مستأنسين لحَدِيث}: in the position of the accusative, conjoined to {غير ناظرين}, or in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ناظرين.
His saying {وَمَا كَانَ لكم أَن تُؤْذُوا}: أن is in the position of the nominative as the ism (noun) of كان; and likewise ولا أن تنكحوا is conjoined to it.

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {فِيهَا إِلَّا قَلِيلا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative latent pronoun in يجاورونك, i.e. "they will not be your neighbours except in a state of being few and abased". It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted adverb, its implied form being "except a little neighbourhood" or "a little time".

mekki-muskil:61-61.t: His saying {ملعونين}: also a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in يجاورونك. It is also said that it is accusative as dispraise and reviling (al-dhamm wa-l-shatm).

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His saying {سنة الله}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "Allah, exalted is He, established that as a practice regarding those who spread alarming rumours about the prophets and were hypocrites".

mekki-muskil:73-73.t: His saying {وَكَانَ الله غَفُورًا رحِيما}: i.e. He has always been so. رحيما is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in غفورا, which governs it, i.e. He forgives in a state of His mercy. It may also be a naʿt (adjective) of غفور, or a second khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام﴾: a resumptive statement set out to explain what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter. (تحيتهم): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), being the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object; (يوم): an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (تحيتهم); the clause ﴿يلقونه﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; (سلام): khabar (predicate) of (تحيتهم); and the clause ﴿تحيتهم يوم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وأعد لهم أجرا كريما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (أعد): past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; (لهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعد﴾; (أجرًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كريما): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t: ﴿يا أيها النبي إنا أرسلناك شاهدًا ومبشرًا ونذيرًا﴾: (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (النبي) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (إنّا): (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; (أرسلناك): past verb, agent and object; the clause ﴿أرسلناك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (شاهدًا): ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf of address in ﴿أرسلناك﴾, and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. "We sent you destined to be a witness over the messengers and the nations." (مبشرًا): conjoined to (شاهدًا), and (نذيرًا): also conjoined to (شاهدًا).

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وداعيًا إلى الله بإذنه وسراجًا منيرًا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (داعيًا): conjoined to (شاهدًا); (إلى الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (داعيًا); (بإذنه): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by His facilitation." (سراجًا): also conjoined, and (منيرًا): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وبشر المؤمنين بأن لهم من الله فضلًا كبيرًا﴾: conjoined to what preceded. (بشر): imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (المؤمنين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the bāʾ is a preposition; (أن): an abrogating, maṣdar-forming particle; (لهم): the fronted khabar (predicate) of (أن); (من الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿فضلا﴾; (فضلا): the postponed noun of (أن); (كبيرًا): an adjective of (فضلا); and ﴿أنّ﴾ together with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the preposition ﴿الباء﴾, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿بشر﴾.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿ولا تطع الكافرين والمنافقين ودع أذاهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): prohibitive; (تطع): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (الكافرين): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (المنافقين): conjoined to (الكافرين); (دع): imperative verb with a latent agent; (أذاهم): mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), by way of the annexation of the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its agent or to its object, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلًا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (توكل): imperative verb with a latent agent; (على الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توكل); (كفى): past verb; the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) particle, and the Name of Majesty is genitive in form but nominative in position because it is the fāʿil of (كفى); (وكيلا): tamyīz (specification) or ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:49-49.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نكحتم المؤمنات﴾: (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (الذين) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (آمنوا): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين), a clause with no grammatical position. (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; (نكحتم المؤمنات): verb, agent and object, and the clause ﴿نكحتم المؤمنات﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it.
﴿ثم طلقتموهن من قبل أن تمسوهن﴾: (ثم): conjunction; (طلقتموهن): past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the nūn is a sign of the feminine with no grammatical position; (من قبل): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (طلقتموهن); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تمسوهن): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the group is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the nūn is a sign of the feminine with no grammatical position; and ﴿أنْ﴾ together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) in the genitive.
﴿فما لكم عليهن من عدة تعتدونها﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذا); (ما): negating; (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (عليهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿عدة﴾; (مِن): a connective (ṣila) preposition; (عدة): genitive in form, nominative in position because it is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause ﴿تعتدونها﴾ is an adjective of (عدة).
﴿فمتعوهن وسرحوهن سراحا جميلا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition); (متعوهن): imperative verb, agent and direct object; (سرحوهن): conjoined to (متعوهن); (سراحًا): standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); (جميلا): an adjective.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿يا أيها النبي إنا أحللنا لك أزواجك اللاتي آتيت أجورهن﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أيُّ) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (النبي) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (إنّا): (إن) is an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; the clause ﴿أحللنا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحللنا); (أزواجك): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (اللاتي): an adjective; the clause ﴿آتيت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿اللاتي﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (أجورهن): mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وما ملكت يمينك مما أفاء الله عليك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (ما): conjoined to (أزواجك); the clause ﴿ملكت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (يمينك): fāʿil (agent) of (ملكت); (مما): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) clarifying ﴿ما ملكت﴾; (أفاء الله): verb and agent; (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أفاء).
﴿وبنات عمك وبنات عماتك وبنات خالك وبنات خالاتك اللاتي هاجرن معك﴾: conjoined to ﴿أزواجك﴾; (اللاتي): an adjective, and the clause ﴿هاجرن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿اللاتي﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (معك): an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) (هاجرن).
﴿وامرأة مؤمنة إن وهبت نفسها للنبي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (امرأة): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿أزواجك﴾; (مؤمنة): an adjective; (إن): conditional; (وهبت): past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "she" (هي); (نفسها): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (للنبي): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وهبت); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being "We made her lawful" (أحللناها).
﴿إن أراد النبي أن يستنكحها خالصة لك من دون المؤمنين﴾: (إن): conditional, restricting the first one; (أراد): past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (النبي): fāʿil (agent); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (يستنكحها): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), and ﴿ها﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the maṣdar-forming ﴿أنْ﴾ together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿أراد﴾; and the second conditional clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (خالصة): ḥāl from the object of ﴿يستنكحها﴾, or from the agent of (وهبتْ), or from ﴿امرأة﴾ because it has been qualified and thereby specified; or it is a naʿt (adjective) of an implied maṣdar, i.e. "an exclusive gift" (هبةً خالصةً). (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خالصة); (من دون): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خالصة) or to a ḥāl from the pronoun in ﴿خالصة﴾; (المؤمنين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿قد علمنا ما فرضنا عليهم في أزواجهم وما ملكت أيمانهم﴾: (قد): particle of verification; (علمنا): verb and agent; (ما): object of (علمنا), and the clause ﴿فرضنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (عليهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فرضنا﴾; (في أزواجهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿فرضنا﴾; (ما): conjoined to (أزواجهم), and the clause ﴿ملكت أيمانهم﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿قد علمنا...﴾ is parenthetical, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿لكيلا يكون عليك حرج﴾: the lām is for causation; (كي): maṣdar-forming and governing the accusative; (لا): negating. (يكون): an incomplete imperfect verb (one of kāna and its sisters), accusative (manṣūb) by ﴿كي﴾; ﴿كي﴾ together with what follows it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the lām of causation, and the lām of causation and its genitive are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خالصة﴾. (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (يكون); (حرج): the postponed noun of (يكون).
﴿وكان الله غفورا رحيما﴾: (كان) is an incomplete past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (غفورا): khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); (رحيما): a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t:
﴿ترجي من تشاء منهن وتؤوي إليك من تشاء﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (ترجي): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (مَن): object of (ترجي), and the clause ﴿تشاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (منهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿مَن﴾ or from the implied resumptive pronoun, i.e. "whomever you wish to defer from among them." (تؤوي): conjoined to (ترجي); (إليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تؤوي); (مَن): object of (تؤوي), and the clause ﴿تشاء﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿ومن ابتغيت ممن عزلت فلا جناح عليك﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (مَن): conditional, in the position of the accusative as the fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿ابتغيت﴾, and ﴿ابتغيت﴾ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) in the position of the jussive, and the clause ﴿فلا جناح عليك﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); or ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿فلا جناح عليك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, joined with the fāʾ because the relative is treated like a condition, and the clause ﴿ابتغيت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿مَن﴾, a clause with no grammatical position, the resumptive pronoun being omitted. The fāʾ is linking; (لا): the lā of generic negation; (جناح): noun of (لا); (عليك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar of ﴿لا﴾; and the clause ﴿ومن ابتغيت...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿ذلك أدنى أن تقر أعينهن ولا يحزن ويرضين بما آتيتهن كلهن﴾: (ذلك): mubtadaʾ (subject); (أدنى): khabar (predicate); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تقر): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾ together with what falls within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "closer to [إلى] their eyes being comforted," the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أدنى﴾. (أعينهن): fāʿil (agent) of (تقرَّ); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): negating; (يحزنَّ): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿لا يحزنَّ﴾ is conjoined to ﴿تقرَّ أعينهن﴾; (يرضين): conjoined to ﴿تقرَّ أعينهن﴾; (بما): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يرضين﴾. The clause ﴿آتيتهن﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (كلهن): tawkīd (emphasis) of the nūn in (يرضين).
﴿والله يعلم ما في قلوبكم وكان الله عليما حليما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (الله): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿يعلم﴾ is the khabar (predicate); (ما): object of (يعلم); (في قلوبكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, i.e. ﴿يعلم ما استقر في قلوبكم﴾ "He knows what is settled in your hearts," and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The clause ﴿والله يعلم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. (كان) is an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (عليما): khabar of (كان), accusative (manṣūb); (حليما): a second khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:52-52.t:
﴿لا يحل لك النساء من بعد ولا أن تبدل بهن من أزواج﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (لا): negating; (يحل): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (لك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يحل); (النساء): fāʿil (agent); (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (النساء); the adverb ﴿بعدُ﴾ is built (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning. The wāw is a conjunction; (لا): negating; (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تبدل): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾ together with the imperfect verb after it is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to (النساء). (بهن): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبدل); (مِن): a connective (ṣila) particle; (أزواج): genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولو أعجبك حسنهن﴾: the wāw is circumstantial; (لو): conditional; (أعجبك): past verb, and the kāf is the fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حسنهن): the postponed fāʿil (agent); the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is implied, indicated by what precedes it; and the conditional clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (تبدل).
﴿إلا ما ملكت يمينك﴾: (إلا): particle of exception; (ما): a relative noun in the position of the accusative, excepted from (النساء), or in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute); and the clause ﴿ملكت يمينك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وكان الله على كل شيء رقيبا﴾: (كان) is an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; (على كل شيء): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رقيبًا﴾; (رقيبا): khabar (predicate) of (كان), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. (يا): vocative particle; (أيها): (أي) is the one addressed, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is for drawing attention; (الذين) is an adjective of ﴿أي﴾. (آمنوا): verb and agent, and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, a clause with no grammatical position. (لا): prohibitive; (تدخلوا): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); (بيوت): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa); (النبي): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إلا أن يؤذن لكم إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه﴾: (إلا): particle of restriction; (أن): maṣdar-forming; (يؤذن): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), passive; (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤذن); (إلى طعام): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤذن), because it has the meaning "unless you are invited to a meal." ﴿أن يؤذن﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "except being given permission." (غير): ḥāl from the agent in (تدخلوا) or from the genitive pronoun in (لكم); (ناظرين): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إناه): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle (ناظرين).
﴿ولكن إذا دعيتم فادخلوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (لكن): a particle of rectification (istidrāk), lightened and inoperative; (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause ﴿دعيتم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ادخلوا): imperative verb and agent.
﴿فإذا طعمتم فانتشروا ولا مستأنسين لحديث﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause ﴿طعمتم﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (انتشروا): imperative verb, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا): connective (ṣila), to emphasise the negation; (مستأنسين): conjoined to ﴿غير ناظرين﴾ or to an implied ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "do not enter them barging in, nor lingering," so it is a conjoined accusative; and it has been said that it is genitive, conjoined to (ناظرين). (لحديث): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مستأنسين).
﴿إن ذلكم كان يؤذي النبي فيستحيي منكم والله لا يستحيي من الحق﴾: the clause gives the reason for the prohibition. (إن): an abrogating particle (one of inna and its sisters); (ذلكم): noun of (إن); (كان): an incomplete verb, and the noun of (كان) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو); the clause ﴿يؤذي النبي﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of (كان), and the clause ﴿كان يؤذي النبي﴾ is the khabar of (إن). (فيستحيي): conjoined to (يؤذي); (منكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يستحيي﴾; the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (الله): mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿لا يستحيي من الحق﴾ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause ﴿والله لا يستحي من الحق﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وإذا سألتموهن متاعا فاسألوهن من وراء حجاب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا): an adverb for future time containing the sense of a condition, and the clause ﴿سألتموهن﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اسألوهن): imperative verb, agent and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (متاعًا): second mafʿūl bihi; (من وراء): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اسألوهن); (حجاب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ذلكم أطهر لقلوبكم وقلوبهن﴾: (ذلكم): mubtadaʾ (subject); (أطهر): khabar (predicate); (لقلوبكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أطهر); (قلوبهن): conjoined to (قلوبكم).
﴿وما كان لكم أن تؤذوا رسول الله ولا أن تنكحوا أزواجه من بعده أبدا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; (ما): negating; (كان): an incomplete past verb (one of kāna and its sisters); (لكم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (أن): maṣdar-forming; (تؤذوا): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-forming ﴿أنْ﴾ and the imperfect verb is the postponed noun of (كان). (رسول الله): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿وما كان لكم...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. (ولا): the wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is for emphasising the negation; ﴿أن تنكحوا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أن تؤذوا﴾; (أزواجه): mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; (من بعده): a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (أبدًا): an adverb, accusative (manṣūb).
