﴿وكان الله بكل شيء عليما﴾: كان: a defective past verb, the word of majesty (Allah) being its noun; بكل شيء: a preposition, its genitive noun and a muḍāf ilayhi, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿عليمًا﴾; عليمًا: the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرًا كثيرًا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position. يا: a vocative particle; أيها: أي is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and ها is for drawing attention; الذين: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أي﴾. آمنوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. اذكروا: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the name of majesty is the object of اذكروا; ذكرًا: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); كثيرًا: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا﴾: the wāw: a conjunction; سبحوه: an imperative verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بكرة: an adverb (ẓarf) for the beginning of the day, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحوه; أصيلًا: conjoined to بكرة; the clause ﴿سبحوه بكرة وأصيلا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿اذكروا الله﴾.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿هو الذي يصلي عليكم وملائكته﴾: a causal explanation of the preceding command to remember and glorify. هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذي: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿يصلي﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. يصلي: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa"; عليكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يصلي﴾; ملائكته: conjoined to the fāʿil of يصلي.
﴿ليخرجكم من الظلمات إلى النور﴾: the lām: of causation; يخرجكم: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an understood أن after the lām of causation, its fāʿil latent, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the understood ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb after it are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), genitive by the lām of causation, and the lām of causation with its genitive is attached to ﴿يصلي﴾. من الظلمات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخرجكم﴾; إلى النور: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يخرجكم﴾.
﴿وكان بالمؤمنين رحيما﴾: the wāw: a conjunction, or resumptive. كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) verb, the noun of كان being latent, its implied form being "huwa"; بالمؤمنين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رحيمًا﴾; رحيمًا: the khabar of كان; the clause is resumptive, or conjoined to the ṣila clause; on both views it has no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ﴾: you put ḍamma on أيّ because it is a singular vocative (nidāʾ mufrad), and the particle of attention (hā) is inseparable from it. النبيّ is a naʿt (adjective) of أيّ according to the grammarians, except al-Akhfash, who says it is a ṣila (relative clause) of أيّ. That is a mistake according to most grammarians, because a ṣila can only be a clause; the way of accounting for what he said is that, since it is an obligatory adjective, he called it a ṣila; likewise the Kufans call the adjective of an indefinite noun its ṣila. Some grammarians permitted the accusative. ﴿اتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾: the yāʾ is dropped because it is an imperative. ﴿وَلا تُطِعِ الْكافِرِينَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ﴾: i.e. do not obey them in what you have been forbidden, and do not incline towards them. By His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾ He indicated that he used to incline towards them only to call them to Islam, i.e. if Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knew that your inclining towards them had any benefit in it, He would not have forbidden it to you, because He is Wise.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَاتَّبِعْ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ﴾: i.e. regarding avoiding them.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: i.e. in fear of their harm. ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾: i.e. sufficient for you against what you fear from them. «وكيلا» is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِنْ قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾: «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. The resemblance of this to the first [verse] is that He did not give a person two hearts: a heart with which he is sincere to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and a heart with which he inclines towards His enemies. ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أَزْواجَكُمُ اللَّائِي تُظاهِرُونَ مِنْهُنَّ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾: two objects. [تظاهرون] is derived from الظهر ("the back"), because the back is the place of riding. The Arabs used to divorce by ẓihār. ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أَدْعِياءَكُمْ أَبْناءَكُمْ﴾: the exegetes hold that this was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Ḥāritha. In the ḥadīth: Khadīja, may Allah be pleased with her, gave him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then his father Ḥāritha came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Take his ransom from me." He said to him: "I will give him the choice; if he wishes to stay with me he will stay, and if he chooses you, take him." He chose to stay, so the Prophet ﷺ freed him and said: "He is my son; he inherits from me and I inherit from him." Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أَدْعِياءَكُمْ أَبْناءَكُمْ﴾, i.e. call them after their fathers. Ibn ʿUmar said: we used to call him nothing but Zayd ibn Muḥammad. So every adopted son was attributed to his father.
﴿ذلِكُمْ قَوْلُكُمْ بِأَفْواهِكُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e. it is a saying without reality. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَقُولُ الْحَقَّ﴾: i.e. the true saying; [الحقّ is] a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar, and it may be an object.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا آباءَهُمْ فَإِخْوانُكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ﴾: i.e. then they are your brothers. ﴿وَمَوالِيكُمْ﴾ is conjoined to it.
﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ فِيما أَخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ﴾: Qatāda's view is that it is a man attributing [someone] to other than his father while believing that he is his father. Abū Jaʿfar said: it has been said that this is general (mujmal), i.e. there is no blame on you in anything in which you erred. ʿAṭāʾ's legal opinion was on this basis: if a man swore not to leave his debtor until he had received his due in full from him, and took from him what he thought were good dinars, then found them to be glass, there is nothing on him; and likewise in his view, if he swore that he would not greet so-and-so, then greeted him without recognising him, he does not break his oath, because he did not intend that. ﴿وَلكِنْ ما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾: «ما» is in the position of the genitive, referred back to the «ما» that is with أخطأتم; and it may be in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied meaning being: "but that for which you are taken to account is what your hearts intended".

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
﴿النَّبِيُّ أَوْلى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾: there are two views on its meaning: one is that the Prophet has a greater claim on the believers than they have on one another, like ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 54]; the other is that when the Prophet ﷺ commands something and the soul calls to something else, the command of the Prophet ﷺ takes precedence. In the ḥadīth: "I am closer to the believers than their own selves; whoever leaves wealth, it is for his heirs, and whoever leaves a debt or dependants, it is upon me."
﴿وَأَزْواجُهُ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ﴾: i.e. in sanctity, and it is not lawful for them to marry them. ﴿وَأُولُوا الْأَرْحامِ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ﴾ a second mubtadaʾ or a badal (substitute); ﴿أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُهاجِرِينَ﴾: the implied meaning may be "and those related by blood among the believers and the Emigrants", and the meaning may be "have a greater claim than the believers and the Emigrants". ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ تَفْعَلُوا إِلى أَوْلِيائِكُمْ مَعْرُوفاً﴾ is in the position of the accusative, an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, Allah's mercy be upon him, said: it was revealed permitting bequests to a Jew or a Christian. ﴿كانَ ذلِكَ فِي الْكِتابِ مَسْطُوراً﴾: i.e. written in order, like a line (saṭr). One says:
سَطَر, plural أسطار; and whoever says سَطْر says أسطُر and سُطور; [the latter] is suitable for both of them, except that it is more fitting and more frequent with the one with sukūn. [Translator's note: the vowelling of سطر is not shown in the printed text; supplied here from the sense.]

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثاقَهُمْ﴾: al-Thawrī said, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās: "And when We took from the prophets their covenant": he said: concerning their peoples. And from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: it is like ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 172], the verse. He said: so He took their covenant, and upon the prophets among them, Allah's blessings be upon them, was the light, as though they were lamps; then He took the covenant of the prophets specifically for the message. He said: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثاقَهُمْ﴾, the verse. He said:
«ومن نوح» and did not say "ونوح" because when an overt noun is conjoined to a genitive pronoun, the preposition is repeated; you say: مررت به وبزيد ("I passed by him and by Zayd"). ﴿وَإِبْراهِيمَ﴾: conjunction of an overt noun to an overt noun, so the preposition was not repeated; and likewise ﴿وَمُوسى وَعِيسَى﴾.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿لِيَسْئَلَ الصَّادِقِينَ عَنْ صِدْقِهِمْ﴾: we have already mentioned it.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً﴾: in the ḥadīth: "I was given victory by the east wind (al-ṣabā), and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind (al-dabūr)." In this wind were the greatest of signs and proofs for the Prophet ﷺ, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent upon His enemies a bitterly cold wind which tore their tents and preoccupied them with its cold, while the believers were facing them and none of it reached them.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونَا﴾: the Kufans read it without alif, and that is contrary to the Muṣḥaf, even if it is good in Arabic. The best thing in this is to pause on it with the alif and not to join it [to what follows], because if one joins it with the alif he commits a solecism, and if one joins it without the alif he contradicts the Muṣḥaf; whereas if one pauses with the alif he follows the written text (al-sawād) and agrees with the grammar, because the Arabs keep this alif in rhymes (qawāfī) and keep it in verse-endings (fawāṣil) so that the speech is harmonious.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿هُنالِكَ ابْتُلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: i.e. at that time the believers were tested. The lām [in هنالك] is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, though it has kasra, and the kāf is for address. ﴿وَزُلْزِلُوا زِلْزالًا شَدِيداً﴾: one also says زَلزال, in reduplicated verbs specifically; in non-reduplicated ones the fatḥa is not permissible. [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant زَلزال is not shown in the printed text; it is supplied from the sense.] One says: دحرجته دِحراجاً ("I rolled it").

nahhas-irab:12-13.t:
﴿وَإِذْ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "And remember"; and likewise ﴿وَإِذْ قالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ يا أَهْلَ يَثْرِبَ﴾. Abū ʿUbayda said: Yathrib is the name of a territory, and Medina is part of it. ﴿لا مُقامَ لَكُمْ﴾: i.e. a place in which they stay. And he recited [in the wāfir metre]: 341-
فأيّي ما وأيّك كان شرّا ... فسيق إلى المقامة لا يراها
(Whichever of us, I or you, was the worse, may he be driven to the place of standing without seeing it.)
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Aʿraj read ﴿لا مُقامَ لَكُمْ﴾ [Translator's note: the printed text does not distinguish this reading from the one quoted above; the reading with ḍamma, مُقام, is evidently meant here, as against مَقام]: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) from أقام يقيم [Translator's note: the text has قام يقيم], or a place in which they stay or are made to stay. ﴿وَيَسْتَأْذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمُ النَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنا عَوْرَةٌ وَما هِيَ بِعَوْرَةٍ﴾: the reading of Abū Rajāʾ, also related from Ibn ʿAbbās, is ﴿إِنَّ بُيُوتَنا عَوْرَةٌ وَما هِيَ بِعَوْرَةٍ﴾ [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variant has been lost in the printed text; from what follows it is عَوِرَة, with kasra on the wāw]; this is the active participle from عَوِرَ يَعْوَرُ عَوَرة. [عَوْرة] may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "possessing exposure", and it may be in the position of the active participle by extension, as you say رجل عدل ("a just man"), i.e. عادل. One says أعور المكان when an exposure appears in the place, and أعور الفارس when a weak point in the horseman becomes apparent. ﴿إِنْ يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِراراً﴾: i.e. their purpose is not what they said; their purpose is only to flee.

nahhas-irab:14-15.t:
﴿وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَقْطارِها﴾: that is, the houses or the city. ثمّ سئلوا الفتنة لأتوها [i.e. لَأَتَوْها, "they would have come to it"]: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries; the reading of the people of Basra and the people of Kufa is ﴿لَآتَوْها﴾ ("they would have given it"), and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He adduced as proof the ḥadīth about the group among whom was Bilāl, that they gave the fitna of themselves [i.e. yielded to the persecutors' demands], except Bilāl. Abū Jaʿfar said: the ḥadīth about the case of Bilāl does not resemble the verse, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, gave this report about these people, whereas Bilāl and his companions were only coerced. In this verse, ﴿وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَقْطارِها﴾ means: if the disbelievers had entered upon them, they would have come to them; and this is contrary to what they had pledged to Allah. And in the story: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كانُوا عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ لا يُوَلُّونَ الْأَدْبارَ﴾; so this points to «لأتوها» without the long vowel (maqṣūr).
﴿وَما تَلَبَّثُوا بِها إِلَّا يَسِيراً﴾: i.e. punishment would seize them, or they would perish.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وَإِذاً لا تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾: in some transmissions it is وإذاً لا تمتّعوا, accusative [i.e. subjunctive] by إذن. The nominative [indicative] is in the sense of "you will not be given enjoyment, then", so إذن is suspended (mulghā); and making it govern is also permissible. This is its rule when it is preceded by wāw or fāʾ. If it comes at the beginning, it governs the subjunctive, and you say: إذن أكرمَكم ("Then I will honour you"). Sībawayh related from one of the companions of al-Khalīl, from al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, that «أن» is implied with it, while what he [Sībawayh] heard from him was that it governs the subjunctive itself. If it comes in the middle, it may not govern the subjunctive according to the Basrans; you say: أنا إذن أكرمُك, كنت إذن أكرمُك, and إنّي إذن أكرمُك. Al-Farrāʾ uses the subjunctive here, I mean specifically with «إنّ», and recited [in the rajaz metre]: 342-
إنّي إذا أهلك أو أطيرا
(Then I would perish, or fly off.)
— and the poem has the accusative rhyme. His reason concerning «إنّ» is that it is not inflected (lā tanṣarif).

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ الْمُعَوِّقِينَ مِنْكُمْ﴾: i.e. those who set themselves to turn people away from the Prophet. Derived from عاقني عن كذا ("he held me back from such-and-such"), i.e. he diverted me from it; and عوّق is for intensification (al-taktīr). ﴿وَالْقائِلِينَ لِإِخْوانِهِمْ هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنا﴾: according to the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; others say هلمّوا for a group and هلمّي for a woman. [It is invariable] because the origin is hā, which is for drawing attention, to which «لُمَّ» was joined; then the alif was dropped for lightness, and it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; neither kasra nor ḍamma is permissible in it because it is not conjugated. The meaning of «هلمّ» is "come forward".

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿أَشِحَّةً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: according to al-Farrāʾ its accusative is from four angles: one is that it is by way of censure (dhamm); he also permits it to be accusative [as in] يعوّقون أشحّةً ("they hinder, being niggardly"); he also permits the implied meaning to be "and those who say, being niggardly"; and he also permits [the meaning] "and they do not come to battle except a little; they come to it being niggardly", i.e. niggardly towards the poor with the booty, cowardly. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is not permissible that what governs it be المعوّقين or القائلين, so as not to separate the ṣila (relative clause) from the relative. ﴿فَإِذا جاءَ الْخَوْفُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أَعْيُنُهُمْ كَالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ﴾: He described them with cowardice; and such is the way of the coward: he looks right and left, staring fixedly, and he may faint. ﴿فَإِذا ذَهَبَ الْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدادٍ﴾: al-Farrāʾ related صلقوكم with ṣād. خطيب مِسلاق and مِصلاق [is said] when he is eloquent. ﴿أُولئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾: i.e. even if their outward appearance is faith, they are not believers, because the hypocrite is in reality a disbeliever; Allah, Majestic and Mighty, described them with disbelief. ﴿وَكانَ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيراً﴾: i.e. He speaks the truth. [Translator's note: so in the text; the gloss does not obviously fit this phrase.]

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ الْأَحْزابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا﴾: i.e. because of their cowardice. Ṭalḥa read وإن يأت الأحزاب يودّوا لو أنهم بُدّى في الأعراب ("they would wish they were nomads among the Bedouin"). One says بادٍ and بُدّى with the short ending, like غازٍ and غُزّى, and it is also lengthened, like صائم and صُوّام. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read يسّاءلون عن أنبائكم; the original is يتساءلون, then it was assimilated. ﴿وَلَوْ كانُوا فِيكُمْ ما قاتَلُوا إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾: [قليلا is] a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ﴾: i.e. in his going out to the Trench and his patience. ʿĀṣim read ﴿أُسْوَةٌ﴾ with ḍamma on the hamza. Kasra is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs, and the plural of both is the same according to al-Farrāʾ. His reason for the ḍamma, according to the dialect of those who use kasra in the singular, is to distinguish between those with wāw and those with yāʾ [as the final radical]; so they say كِسوة, كُسى and لِحية, لِحى. ﴿لِمَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ﴾: according to the skilled grammarians, «يرجو» may only be written without alif when it is for one person, because the reason [for the alif] in the plural does not exist in the singular. ﴿وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ كَثِيراً﴾: i.e. much remembrance.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَلَمَّا رَأَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْأَحْزابَ﴾: some Arabs say راءَ, by metathesis (qalb). ﴿قالُوا هذا ما وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾: if you make «ما» in the sense of الذي ("that which"), the hāʾ [the resumptive pronoun] is omitted; and if you make it a maṣdar, it needs no resumptive pronoun. ﴿وَما زادَهُمْ إِلَّا إِيماناً وَتَسْلِيماً﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: and looking at the Confederates only increased them. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: رأى indicates seeing (al-ruʾya), and the femininity of الرؤية is not real; the meaning is "and the seeing only increased them", like من كذب كان شرّا له ("whoever lies, it [the lying] is worse for him").

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجالٌ﴾: [رجال is] nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is valid because «صدقوا» is in the position of a naʿt (adjective). Abū Isḥāq said: «ما» is in the position of the accusative. Abū Jaʿfar said: one says صدقت العهد, i.e. I fulfilled it. ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضى نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ﴾: «من» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; we have already mentioned its meaning.

nahhas-irab:25-26.t:
﴿وَرَدَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنالُوا﴾: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr said, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said regarding His saying ﴿وَرَدَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِغَيْظِهِمْ﴾: Abū Sufyān and ʿUyayna ibn Bard [Translator's note: so in the text; the well-known name is ʿUyayna ibn Badr (ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn ibn Badr)]; Abū Sufyān returned to Tihāma and ʿUyayna to Najd. ﴿وَكَفَى اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الْقِتالَ﴾ by sending the wind against them until they returned; and Banū Qurayẓa returned to their fortresses. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The matter of Banū Qurayẓa was taken care of by terror, until they submitted to the judgement of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, Allah's mercy be upon him, and he ruled that their fighting men be killed and their offspring taken captive. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ قَوِيًّا﴾: i.e. His command is not repelled; ﴿عَزِيزاً﴾: He is not overcome.
He made this clear regarding Banū Qurayẓa; He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوهُمْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ مِنْ صَياصِيهِمْ وَقَذَفَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ﴾. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the basic meaning of الصيصية is that by which one protects oneself; so a fortress is a ṣīṣiya, and the horns of cattle are called صياصٍ because of their protecting. Likewise it is said of the spur of a rooster. He said: and the weaver's spike [Translator's note: the text reads الشوكة الحائك; شوكة الحائك is meant] is called a ṣīṣiya, by comparison with it; and he recited [in the ṭawīl metre]: 343-
كوقع الصّياصي في النّسيج الممدّد
(Like the striking of the weaver's spikes into the outstretched web.)
﴿فَرِيقاً﴾ is accusative by تقتلون, and ﴿فَرِيقاً﴾ is accusative by تأسرون. Al-Farrāʾ related «تأسرون» with ḍamma on the sīn [i.e. تأسُرون].

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيارَهُمْ وَأَمْوالَهُمْ وَأَرْضاً﴾: because the Emigrants had no houses in Medina.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿فَتَعالَيْنَ﴾: the nūn of the feminine is in it, and it is not dropped because [the verb] is indeclinable (mabnī); if it were dropped, it would be ambiguous. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the basic meaning of تعالَ is "rise up"; then their use of it became frequent, until it was said to one who is high up: تعالَ, i.e. "come down".

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وَمَنْ يَقْنُتْ مِنْكُنَّ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتَعْمَلْ صالِحاً﴾: [this is] the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The rest of the Kufans read ويعمل صالحا [with yāʾ], and Abū ʿUbayd inclines to this reading because it is conjoined to the first; they agreed on the first being with yāʾ, reading «ومن يقنت». Abū Jaʿfar said:
The second differs from the first, because the first is construed according to the wording [of مَن] and has nothing before it for it to follow, whereas the second has منكنّ before it, and this nūn is for the feminine; so تعمل with tāʾ is more fitting, because it follows a feminine, even though [reading] with yāʾ is permissible and good. And after it is ﴿نُؤْتِها أَجْرَها مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾, with the feminine in the written text (al-sawād), and likewise ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنا لَها رِزْقاً كَرِيماً﴾. The exegetes hold that the noble provision here is Paradise.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿يا نِساءَ النَّبِيِّ لَسْتُنَّ كَأَحَدٍ مِنَ النِّساءِ إِنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ﴾: He did not say كواحدة ("like any one [feminine]"), because «أحد» is a general negative that applies to masculine and feminine, and the plural is in a single form. ﴿فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), as the past verb is indeclinable; this is the school of Sībawayh. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said — ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related it to us from him, and I do not know it in any of his books — he said: if something is defective from two angles and it is a noun, it is barred from full declension (it becomes a diptote); and if it is defective from three angles it becomes indeclinable, because after being barred from full declension there is nothing left but indeclinability. This verb is defective from three angles: among them, the verb is heavier than the noun; and it is plural, and the plural is heavier than the singular; and it is for the feminine, and the feminine is heavier than the masculine. This view is a mistake according to Abū Isḥāq, who said: it obliges him not to decline Firʿawn at all when a woman is named with it, because it has three causes in it. ﴿فَيَطْمَعَ الَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾: accusative [subjunctive] because it is the answer to the prohibition; we have explained it at greater length than this. Abū Ḥātim related that al-Aʿraj read ﴿فَيَطْمَعَ الَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm. Abū Jaʿfar said: I reckon this a mistake, and that he read ﴿فَيَطْمَعِ الَّذِي﴾ with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, conjoining it to «يخضعن»; and this is a good, fine reading. «فيُطمِعَ» الذي is also permissible, in the sense "so that the softness, or the speech, makes [him] covet". [Translator's note: the vowelling of the variants here is largely lost in the printed text; the forms in brackets are supplied from the explanations given.] ﴿وَقُلْنَ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً﴾.

nahhas-irab:33-34.t:
﴿وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾: this is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows fatḥa, but from what follows the reading of these readers is وَقِرْنَ with kasra], and the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim read ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ with fatḥa on the qāf. «قِرن» with kasra on the qāf admits two analyses. The school of al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd is that it is from الوقار ("dignity"); one says وقر يقر وقوراً when one stays firmly at home. The other view is that it is from قرّ في المكان يقِرّ ("he stayed in the place"), with kasra on the qāf; the original then is اقْرِرْن: the first rāʾ was dropped because the doubling was felt to be heavy, and its vowel was cast onto the qāf, so it became وقِرن, as one says ظِلت أفعل ("I continued doing"), with kasra on the ẓāʾ. As for «وقَرن», a number of the scholars of Arabic have discussed it. Abū Ḥātim claimed that it has no justification in the speech of the Arabs, and Abū ʿUbayd claimed that his teachers used to reject it as being from the speech of the Arabs.
Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the statement of Abū ʿUbayd that his teachers rejected it — he mentioned this in "Kitāb al-Qirāʾāt" — he related the contrary of it in "al-Gharīb al-Muṣannaf": he related from al-Kisāʾī that the people of the Ḥijāz say قرِرت في المكان أقَرّ. And al-Kisāʾī is one of the most eminent of his teachers, and the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz is the old, eloquent dialect. As for Abū Ḥātim's statement that it has no justification, he has been contradicted on it; there are two justifications for it: one is what al-Kisāʾī related, and the other is what I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say; he said: it is from قرِرت به عيناً أقَرّ ("I was gladdened by it"); so the meaning is "and be content with it in your houses". This is a good analysis, except that the ḥadīth indicates that it is from the first, as it is related that ʿAmmār said to ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has commanded you to stay in your home." She said: "O Abū al-Yaqẓān, you have never ceased to be one who speaks the truth." He said:
"Praise be to Allah, who made me so upon your tongue." ﴿وَلا تَبَرَّجْنَ﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās said: the essence of tabarruj is displaying adornment and displaying what it is better to cover; it is taken from spaciousness; one says "there is tabarruj in his teeth" when they are spaced apart. He said: «الجاهلية الأولى» is as you say "the ignorant Jāhiliyya". He said:
In the ignorant Jāhiliyya women used to display what is shameful to display, to the point that a woman would sit with her husband and her paramour (khilm), and her paramour would have exclusive use of what is above the waist-wrapper, upwards, and her husband exclusive use of what is below the waist-wrapper, downwards; and sometimes one of them would ask the other to swap. ﴿إِنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: it is said that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ are meant by it, and it is said that his wives and his family who are the people of his house are meant by it. Abū Jaʿfar said: the ḥadīth on this is well known from Umm Salama and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that this was revealed concerning ʿAlī, Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them, with a cloak over them; and His saying «عنكم» (masculine plural) indicates that it is not for the women specifically. Abū Isḥāq said: ﴿أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ﴾ is accusative by way of praise (madḥ); he said: and if you wish, as a vocative. He said: the nominative and the genitive are also permissible.
Abū Jaʿfar said: if you make it genitive as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm, it is not permissible according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd; he said: no substitute is made for the speaker or for the one addressed, because they do not need clarification. [Translator's note: the text reads لا يبدل من المخاطب ولا من المخاطب, which in the unvowelled form means "the addressed nor the addressed"; المخاطِب (speaker) and المخاطَب (addressee) are evidently intended.] ﴿وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيراً﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of emphasis. According to the transmitted ḥadīth, the address was turned to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, so He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَاذْكُرْنَ ما يُتْلى فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾.
The first nūn [in اذكرن] is light (unstressed) because it is equivalent to the wāw of the masculine — you say in the masculine واذكروا — and it is doubled in the second [بيوتكنّ] because the two [nūns] are equivalent to the mīm and wāw in your saying في بيوتكمو, except that the wāw may be dropped because of its heaviness, since the mīm before it indicates it. ﴿مِنْ آياتِ اللَّهِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ﴾: most of the exegetes hold that الحكمة here is the Sunna, and some of them say it is [part] of the verses.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾: the noun (ism) of inna. ﴿وَالْمُسْلِماتِ﴾ is conjoined to it; their nominative is permissible according to the Basrans, whereas al-Farrāʾ permits it only where the inflection does not appear. ﴿وَالْحافِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمْ وَالْحافِظاتِ﴾: the implied form is والحافظاتها, then it was omitted. On this basis one may say ضربني وضربتُ زيدٌ ("Zayd struck me and I struck [him]"); if you do not omit, you say وضربته. Similar to it is ونخلع ونترك من يفجرك ("and we cast off and abandon whoever acts wickedly towards You"); if you do not omit, you say ونتركه. Sībawayh related: متى ظننت أو قلت زيداً منطلقاً ("When did you think, or say, Zayd to be departing?"); if you do not omit, you say: متى ظننت أو قلت هو زيداً منطلقاً; and if you wish you say: متى ظننت أو قلته زيداً منطلقاً. All this is on [the principle of] making the first [verb] govern. If you make the second govern, you say: متى ظننت أو قلت زيدٌ منطلقٌ; this is the good usage. And if you wish you say: متى ظننت أو قلت زيداً منطلقاً, making the second govern, with قلت governing like ظننت. ﴿وَالذَّاكِرِينَ اللَّهَ كَثِيراً وَالذَّاكِراتِ﴾ is similar. Mujāhid said: one is not "remembering Allah, Majestic and Mighty, much" until [one remembers Him] standing, sitting and lying down. Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: whoever wakes his wife at night and they pray four rakʿas, they are both recorded among the men and women who remember Allah much.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْراً﴾: al-Ḥasan said: it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah commands a matter and His Messenger commands a matter, to disobey Him. The Kufans read ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ [with yāʾ], and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because [here] the feminine has been separated from its verb. Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading with yāʾ is permissible; as for its being given precedence over the tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense appears to be that the tāʾ reading is to be preferred], [that is] because the word is feminine, so making its verb feminine is good; and the masculine is on the basis that ﴿الْخِيَرَةُ﴾ is in the sense of التخيّر ("choosing").

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ وَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشاهُ فَلَمَّا قَضى زَيْدٌ مِنْها وَطَراً زَوَّجْناكَها لِكَيْ لا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِي أَزْواجِ أَدْعِيائِهِمْ إِذا قَضَوْا مِنْهُنَّ وَطَراً وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولاً﴾ (37) ﴿وَإِذْ تَقُولُ﴾: [إذ is] in the position of the accusative, and it is not inflected because it is not fully nominal (lā tatamakkan). ﴿لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ﴾: one of the scholars said: this was not [a sin] on the part of the Prophet ﷺ; do you not see that he was not commanded to repent or to seek forgiveness for it? A thing may not be a sin, except that something else is better than it; and he concealed that within himself for fear that people would be tempted.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿ما كانَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيما فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ﴾: «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because what precedes it is in the sense of "He made that a practice (sanna)".

nahhas-irab:39-39.t:
﴿الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ اللَّهِ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of His saying ﴿الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾. He said: it may also be in the position of the nominative. He said:
It may also be in the position of the accusative by way of praise (madḥ).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿ما كانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجالِكُمْ﴾: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did have children, among them Ibrāhīm, al-Qāsim and al-Ṭayyib; and al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them, are children of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, just as Jesus, peace be upon him, is of the children of Adam ﷺ. There are two answers to this. One of them, which is the view of Abū Isḥāq, is that the meaning is: Muḥammad was not the father of any of those he adopted, but he is the father of his community in reverence and veneration, and his wives, may Allah be pleased with them, are forbidden to them. Another answer is that this is literal: at the time this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ was not the father of any man, and those we mentioned — Ibrāhīm, al-Qāsim and al-Ṭayyib — died as boys. ﴿وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾: al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "but he was the Messenger of Allah". He [al-Farrāʾ] permitted ولكن رسولُ الله وخاتمُ النبيين with the nominative, by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and al-Farrāʾ claimed that it has been read so. Al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī and ʿĀṣim read ﴿وَخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ with fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. the last of the prophets, just as ʿAlqama ibn Qays read خاتَمُه مسك [al-Muṭaffifīn: 26], i.e. its end. And خاتِم is from ختم, so he is خاتِم ("the one who seals"). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ولكنّ نبيّاً ختم النّبيّين ("but a prophet who sealed the prophets"). For what is worn [i.e. a ring] one says خاتَم, خاتِم, خيتام and خاتام. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً﴾: [عليما is] the khabar (predicate) of kāna, the implied form being "knowing of everything".

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: [Translator's note: the entry opens without quoting the verse; it concerns ﴿وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا﴾.] Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: الأصيل is the late afternoon (al-ʿashiyy), and its plural is أصائل; and الأُصُل is in the sense of الأصيل, and its plural is آصال. Someone else said: أُصُل is the plural of أصيل, like رغيف and رُغُف.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلائِكَتُهُ﴾: according to the lexicographers, the basic meaning of al-ṣalāt is supplication (al-duʿāʾ), as al-Aʿshā said [in the basīṭ metre]: 344-
عليك مثل الّذي صلّيت فاغتمضي ... يوما فإنّ لجنب المرء مضطجعا
(Upon you be the like of what you prayed; so close your eyes in sleep one day, for a man's side must have a place to lie down.)
i.e. keep to the like of the supplication you made for me, because before it is:
345-
تقول بنتي وقد قرّبت مرتحلا ... يا ربّ جنّب أبي الأوصاب والوجعا
(My daughter says, as I bring near my mount for departure: "O Lord, keep my father away from ailments and pain.")
It is also related: عليكِ مثلُ الذي صلّيت, i.e. upon you be the like of your supplication. The prayer was called ṣalāt because of the supplication in it; and for this and other reasons the jurists of the people of Medina say [that one] may supplicate in his prayer for whatever he wishes. However, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd claimed that the basic meaning of al-ṣalāt is showing mercy (al-taraḥḥum), and derived all of it from one root: al-ṣalāt from Allah is His mercy to His servants; from the angels it is tenderness towards them and asking mercy for them from Allah, Majestic and Mighty; and al-ṣalāt from people is to seek mercy from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, by performing the obligatory or supererogatory [prayer]. Moreover, in the ḥadīth the Children of Israel asked ﷺ [Translator's note: a name appears to be missing here; presumably Moses, peace be upon him] whether your Lord, Majestic and Mighty, prays; he thought that a grave thing, so He, Majestic and Mighty, revealed to him: "My ṣalāt, i.e. My mercy, has preceded My anger." ﴿لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ﴾: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الظلمات» is disbelief and «النور» is faith. «الظُّلَمات» is also permissible, the ḍamma being replaced by fatḥa because of the lightness of the fatḥa; however, al-Kisāʾī used to say: ظُلَمات is the plural of ظُلَم, and ظُلَم is the plural of ظُلْمة. And whoever says ظُلْمات drops the ḍamma because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: the vowelling of these variant forms is not shown in the printed text; it is supplied from the explanation.]

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
﴿تَحِيَّتُهُمْ يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ سَلامٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The most eminent thing related about it is that al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said:
"Their greeting on the day they meet Him is 'Peace'": the Angel of Death greets the believer with peace when taking his soul; he does not take his soul until he has greeted him. Abū Isḥāq interpreted it as being in Paradise, and adduced as evidence His saying ﴿تَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيها سَلامٌ﴾. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd distinguished between al-taḥiyya and al-salām, saying: al-taḥiyya applies to every supplication, whereas al-salām is specific; and from this is ﴿يُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً وَسَلاماً﴾ [al-Furqān: 75].

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: [Translator's note: the entry opens without quoting the verse; it concerns ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْناكَ شاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾.] Accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Saʿīd said from Qatāda: ﴿شاهِداً﴾ over his community that he conveyed [the message], ﴿وَمُبَشِّراً﴾ of Paradise, ﴿وَنَذِيراً﴾ of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَداعِياً إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: i.e. to the testimony that there is no god but Allah. ﴿بِإِذْنِهِ﴾: he [Qatāda] said: by His command. ﴿وَسِراجاً مُنِيراً﴾: he said: the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied meaning according to his view is: "and calling to the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and possessing a lamp", i.e. possessing a clear Book. Abū Isḥāq permitted it to be in the sense of "and reciting a Book".

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ﴾: the bāʾ may be dropped from the like of this; and the entry of the lām [of emphasis] into the khabar (predicate) is not permissible [here].

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿وَلا تُطِعِ الْكافِرِينَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ وَدَعْ أَذاهُمْ﴾: Abū Isḥāq interpreted it in the sense of: leave the harm with which they harm you, i.e. [do not retaliate] for their doing it, until you are commanded something concerning them. [Translator's note: the text reads لإنجازهم عليه, which is obscure; perhaps لا تجازهم عليه, "do not requite them for it", is meant.] Someone else interpreted it as: do not harm them; and in his view this was before he was commanded to fight.

nahhas-irab:49-50.t:
﴿فَما لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ عِدَّةٍ﴾: «من» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. ﴿وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً﴾: conjoined, i.e. "and We made lawful for you a believing woman". ﴿إِنْ وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَها لِلنَّبِيِّ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: if she gives herself to the Prophet, she becomes lawful for him.
Al-Ḥasan read أن وهبت with fatḥa on the hamza, and «أن» is in the position of the accusative. Abū Isḥāq said: so it is "because she gave"; and someone else said: أنْ وهبت is a badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for امرأة. ﴿خالِصَةً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما فَرَضْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِي أَزْواجِهِمْ وَما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ﴾: Qatāda said: what He, Majestic and Mighty, prescribed for them regarding their wives is that there is no marriage except with a guardian, two upright witnesses and a dowry, and that a man may not marry more than four. Someone else said: this is indicated by ﴿وَأَنْكِحُوا الْأَيامى مِنْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 32], ﴿وَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 19] and ﴿وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 32] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse is al-Ṭalāq: 2], together with what strengthens that from the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿وَما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ﴾: what was prescribed concerning it is that no women are lawful [by ownership] except captives of those who have no covenant of protection. ﴿لِكَيْلا يَكُونَ عَلَيْكَ حَرَجٌ﴾: i.e. do not go beyond this. It is also said that it refers back to His saying ﴿إِنَّا أَحْلَلْنا لَكَ أَزْواجَكَ﴾ and what follows it.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
ترجئ من تشاء منهنّ [﴿تُرْجِئُ مَنْ تَشاءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾], with hamza, from أرجأت الأمر when you postponed it. It is also read ﴿تُرْجِي﴾ without hamza. The grammarians have discussed how to account for it. Some of them said: it is a dialect, even if not an eloquent one; and some of them said: it is by substitution of the hamza, according to the dialect of those who say قريت [for قرأت]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the correct view of Sībawayh is that he does not permit substitution of the hamza, because Abū Zayd said to him: "Some of the Arabs say قريت for قرأت, like رميت." Sībawayh said: "How do they say it in the imperfect?" He said: "They say يقرأه." Sībawayh said to him: "They ought to have said يقري, like رميت أرمي." Abū al-Ḥasan said: this statement of Sībawayh indicates that it is not permissible in his view. He said: and I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: it is derived from رجا يرجو; one says رجا, and أرجيته, i.e. I made him hope. ﴿ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾: we have already mentioned it. It has also been said about it: that is more likely [to ensure] that she is not grieved, since none of them is together with another and witnesses the preference and inclination. ﴿وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِما آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ﴾: [كلّهنّ is] tawkīd (emphasis) of the implied (muḍmar) pronoun, i.e. "and they will be pleased, all of them". Abū Ḥātim and Abū Isḥāq permitted ويرضين بما آتيتهنّ كلَّهنّ [in the accusative] as tawkīd of the pronoun in «آتيتهنّ»; al-Farrāʾ does not permit it, because the meaning is not along those lines, since the meaning is "and each one of them will be pleased", and the meaning is not "with what you have given them all". Abū Jaʿfar said: what he said is good.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t:
﴿لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّساءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: the readers are agreed on reading with yāʾ, ﴿لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ﴾; and he claimed that if it were for all women, tāʾ would be better. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a plain mistake. How can it be said that the readers are agreed on yāʾ, when Abū ʿAmr read with tāʾ without any disagreement transmitted from him? And when it is for a group of women, yāʾ is permissible and good. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say:
I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: whoever reads لا تحلّ لك النساء takes it in the sense of "the group (jamāʿa) of women", and whoever reads with yāʾ takes it in the sense of "all (jamīʿ) the women". Al-Farrāʾ, when it is with yāʾ, takes it as "nothing of the women is lawful for you", and construes the masculine on this basis. ﴿إِلَّا ما مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for النساء, and it may be in the position of the accusative as an exception. ﴿وَلا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْواجٍ﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to النساء, i.e. "neither women nor exchanging them is lawful for you". Whoever said that the verse may not [be abrogated] permitted that [abrogation] only because it is in the sense of a prohibition; even though the wording of both is the wording of reports, which may not be abrogated. [Translator's note: this last sentence is garbled in the printed text; the gist appears to be that those who allow this verse to be abrogated do so because, though worded as a statement (and statements cannot be abrogated), it has the force of a prohibition.]

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ﴾: «أن» is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "except by your being given leave"; and it may be an exception not of the same kind as the first. ﴿إِلى طَعامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إِناهُ﴾: [غير is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. do not enter in this state. Anything other than [the accusative, namely] the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الطعام, is not permissible, because if it were an adjective it would be necessary to make the agents overt, and it would be غيرِ ناظرين إناه أنتم. A parallel to this in grammar is: هذا رجل مع رجل ملازمٌ له ("This is a man with a man, clinging to him"), and if you wish you say: هذا رجل ملازم له هو; and مررت برجل معه صقر صائدٍ به ("I passed by a man with a falcon, hunting with it"), and if you wish you say: صائدٍ به هو.
﴿وَلكِنْ إِذا دُعِيتُمْ فَادْخُلُوا﴾: the fāʾ in the apodosis of إذا is necessary because of the sense of requital (mujāzāt) it contains. ﴿وَلا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to غير; and it may be genitive, conjoined to what follows غير. ﴿فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ لا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: one also says يستحي with a single yāʾ, the yāʾ being dropped for lightness. Abū Jaʿfar said: I have mentioned this in the sūra in which the Cow is mentioned [al-Baqara]. ﴿وَما كانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾: in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of kāna. ﴿وَلا أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا﴾ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلائِكَتَهُ﴾: conjoined. «وملائكتُه» with the nominative is also related, and al-Kisāʾī permitted on this basis: إنّ زيداً وعمرٌو منطلقان. All the grammarians other than him forbade this. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the verse does not resemble what he permitted, because if you said إنّ زيداً وعمرٌو منطلقان, you would make two things govern منطلقان, and this is impossible. The implied meaning in the verse is: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty, blesses the Prophet, and His angels bless the Prophet ﷺ"; then [the predicate] was omitted from the first because the second indicates it. What he said is good. And one of the theologians (ahl al-naẓar) said, regarding the reading of those who read ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَمَلائِكَتَهُ﴾ with the accusative, the like of what ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said about the nominative. He said: because يصلّون is only for the angels specifically, since a pronoun [referring to] other than Allah, Majestic and Mighty, may not be combined with Allah, out of reverence and veneration for Him. A man once said to the Prophet ﷺ: "What Allah wills and you will," and the Prophet ﷺ disapproved of that and taught him, saying to him: "Say: What Allah wills, then you will."

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, and what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause). It [الذي] applies to every absent masculine; its sisters are «من», «ما» and «أيّ», and its feminine is «التي». If you say رأيت من في الدار ("I saw who was in the house"), it is for human beings specifically; if you say رأيت الذي في الدار, it is indeterminate, for human beings and others; and if you say رأيت ما في الدار, it is for what lacks reason specifically, and for the description of what has reason: if someone said ما عندك؟ ("What do you have with you?") and you said كريم ("a noble one"), it would be good. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: if you said رجل ("a man"), it would be permissible, because it falls among the genera; but you may not say زيد or عمرو. However, من and ما occur in the interrogative and in the conditional (jazāʾ) without a ṣila, because if you gave them a ṣila in the interrogative you would be asking about what you know, and the conditional is indeterminate, not specific to one thing rather than another; for this reason the ṣila is not permissible in it. «يؤذون» has a hamza because it is from آذى, and the original is clearly with hamza, like آمن. If you lighten the hamza, you replace it with a wāw and say يوذون, because there is no way to make it "between-between" (bayna bayna) since it is quiescent.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾: in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); and it may be in the position of the accusative by conjunction.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِأَزْواجِكَ﴾: its singular is زوج. For a woman one says زوج and زوجة; the eloquent and frequent [form] is without hāʾ, and everything in the Quran came with it [i.e. the form without hāʾ]. زوجة may not be pluralised as أزواج; أزواج is only the plural of زوج, like حوض and أحواض. The original [plural] would be أزوُج, like فَلْس and أفلُس, but they found the vowel on the wāw heavy; and أفعال does occur for [the pattern] فَعْل, so they shifted it to that and said أزواج and أحواض, and for a large number حياض and زياج [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps زِواج or زِيجان is intended]. As for their saying زوج without hāʾ, there are two views: one is that its femininity is a femininity of form, like عقرب and عناق, and it does not run on the verb so as to require the hāʾ; what runs on the verb is متزوّجة. The other view is that the Arabs call any two things that are paired زوجان: one says of a pair of boots زوجان, and likewise of sandals, scissors and shears. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿احْمِلْ فِيها مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [Hūd: 40], and He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْواجٌ﴾ [Ṣād: 58]. ﴿وَبَناتِكَ﴾: a sound (feminine) plural; it is the plural of بنة, like هنة and هنات, and what has been dropped from it is a yāʾ. Some grammarians have said:
what has been dropped from it is a wāw, adducing their saying البُنُوّة ("sonship"). Abū Jaʿfar said: this, by my life, is one of the places where sophistry occurs, because there is no proof in it, since they have said الفُتُوّة, and it is from those with yāʾ; what shows you that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ السِّجْنَ فَتَيانِ﴾ [Yūsuf: 36]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the best I have heard about it is the view of Abū Isḥāq; he said: in my view it is derived from بنى يبني ("to build"). ﴿وَنِساءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: it is said:
نساء is a plural; [يدنين is] the answer to the command. [Translator's note: some words appear to be missing here in the printed text.] The command is omitted, and the implied form according to al-Māzinī is: "Say to them: draw [your cloaks] close; [and] they will draw close". ﴿يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ﴾: from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās: الجلباب is the outer wrap (al-ridāʾ). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said:
الجلباب is anything that covers, whether a garment or a wrapper, i.e. they let some of it hang down over their faces. ﴿ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ فَلا يُؤْذَيْنَ﴾: i.e. they will be recognised by their covering and chastity.

nahhas-irab:60-61.t:
﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْمُرْجِفُونَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ﴾: the exegetes hold that the three descriptions are of one thing, as Sufyān ibn Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr [Translator's note: so in the text; probably "Sufyān ibn Saʿīd from Manṣūr" is meant] related from Abū Razīn, who said:
"The hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and the scaremongers in Medina are one thing", meaning that they combined these things. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾: he said: wickedness and doubt. He said: "If they do not desist from harming the Prophet and from harming the women." The scholars have more than one view on this verse. Among them is that they did not desist, and that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, did set him against them, because He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿وَلا تُصَلِّ عَلى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ ماتَ أَبَداً وَلا تَقُمْ عَلى قَبْرِهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 84], and He commanded him to curse them; this is the setting-against (al-ighrāʾ). This is one view. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: He set him against them in the verse that follows this one, with the speech connected to it, namely His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَيْنَما ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا وَقُتِّلُوا تَقْتِيلًا﴾; this carries the sense of a command to kill them and seize them, i.e. this is their ruling and this is their sentence: that they be seized and killed, since they persisted in hypocrisy and scaremongering. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Five are to be killed in the Sanctuary"; this has the sense of a command, exactly like the verse. This is among the best of what has been said. And in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Five are to be killed in the Sanctuary." ﴿لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ﴾: the lām of oath, on which the oath falls; and the lām was put on إن as a preparation (tawṭiʾa) for it. ﴿ثُمَّ لا يُجاوِرُونَكَ فِيها إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾: and the matter was as He, Majestic and Mighty, said, because they were only a few. This is one of al-Farrāʾ's two answers, and it is the preferable one in his view, i.e. "except while being killed"; the other answer is that the meaning is "except for a short time".
﴿مَلْعُونِينَ﴾: this is the completion of the statement according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "then they will not be your neighbours except few, [being] accursed". From one of the grammarians, that he said the meaning is "wherever they are seized, accursed"; this is a mistake: what is in a conditional construction (mujāzāt) does not govern what precedes it.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ﴾: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has made it His practice concerning whoever spreads alarming rumours about the prophets and displays his hypocrisy, that he be seized and killed.

nahhas-irab:64-65.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَنَ الْكافِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ سَعِيراً﴾: He used the feminine [in فيها] because السعير is in the sense of "the Fire" (al-nār). ﴿خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً﴾.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ﴾: al-Farrāʾ related «يوم تَقَلَّبُ» in the sense of تتقلّب ("turn about"), and يوم نُقلِّبُ وجوهَهم في النار ("the Day We turn their faces about in the Fire"). ﴿يَقُولُونَ يا لَيْتَنا أَطَعْنَا اللَّهَ وَأَطَعْنَا الرَّسُولَا﴾: this alif occurs in verse-endings (fawāṣil) so that they agree; one pauses on it and does not join with it.

nahhas-irab:67-68.t:
[Translator's note: the entry opens without quoting the verse; it concerns ﴿وَقالُوا رَبَّنا إِنَّا أَطَعْنا سادَتَنا وَكُبَراءَنا﴾.] Al-Ḥasan read إنّا أطعنا ساداتِنا with kasra on the tāʾ, because it is a sound plural of سادة. In this there is a deterrent against blind imitation (taqlīd).
ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read ﴿وَالْعَنْهُمْ لَعْناً كَبِيراً﴾, and (كثيراً) is more fitting in this, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أُولئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّاعِنُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 159], and this cursing is much (kathīr).

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: ﴿وَكانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَجِيهاً﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna. If you said كان عبد الله عندنا جالساً ("ʿAbd Allāh was with us, sitting"), there would be two analyses of its accusative: it may be the khabar of kāna, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-wajīh, among the Arabs, is one of great standing and high rank. It is related that whenever he [Moses] asked Allah for something, He gave it to him.

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: [Translator's note: the entry opens without quoting the verse; it concerns ﴿وَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيداً﴾.] Al-Ḥakam ibn Abān said from ʿIkrima: «قولوا قولا سديدا»: he said: "There is no god but Allah", and what resembles it of truthfulness and correctness. Abū Jaʿfar said: the noun from this is السَّداد, with fatḥa on the sīn; and one says: استدّ فلان ("so-and-so became right"). The analogy for its verb is سدّ, the original being سدد. As for السِّداد with kasra on the sīn, it is that with which a thing is stopped up; [as in] سِداد من عوز ("something to stop a gap of need").

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: ﴿إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا الْأَمانَةَ عَلَى السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَالْجِبالِ فَأَبَيْنَ أَنْ يَحْمِلْنَها﴾: we have already mentioned it. Among the good things said about its meaning is that عرضنا means "We displayed", as you say عرضت الجارية على البيع ("I displayed the slave-girl for sale"); the meaning is: We displayed the trust and the squandering of it to the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth, among the angels, the jinn and mankind, ﴿فَأَبَيْنَ أَنْ يَحْمِلْنَها﴾, i.e. [they refused] to carry its burden (wizr), as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 13]. «وحملها الإنسان»: al-Ḥasan said: the disbeliever and the hypocrite are meant by it. He said: ﴿إِنَّهُ كانَ ظَلُوماً﴾ to himself, ﴿جَهُولًا﴾ of his Lord. On this answer it is figurative, like ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾. There is another answer in it, on the basis of its being literal: that He displayed to the heavens, the earth and the mountains the trust and the squandering of it, which are the reward and the punishment, i.e. He made that manifest to them, so they did not carry its burden, and they obeyed in what they were commanded and what they were made subservient for; and man carried it, according to the answer that preceded.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t:
﴿لِيُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْمُنافِقاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكاتِ وَيَتُوبَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً﴾ (73) ﴿لِيُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ الْمُنافِقِينَ وَالْمُنافِقاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكاتِ﴾: i.e. by the proofs established against them through the displaying of the trust to them, which is the making manifest of what was made manifest to them of the threat. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said:
The trust is the prayer, fasting and the ritual bath for jināya [Translator's note: so in the text; janāba (major ritual impurity) is meant, as below]. And from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: part of the trust is that a woman is entrusted with her chastity. And in a ḥadīth traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ): "The trust is the prayer": if you wish you say "I prayed", and if you wish you say "I did not pray"; and likewise fasting and the ritual bath for janāba. Al-Ḥasan read ويتوبُ الله with the nominative, cutting it off from the first, i.e. He turns to them in forgiveness in every case. ﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً﴾: [رحيما is] a khabar (predicate) after a khabar of kāna; it may be a naʿt (adjective) of غفور, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied (muḍmar) pronoun.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ وَٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾.
Its meaning is: remain firm in fearing Allah, just as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمنُوْا آمِنْوا﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾.
That is, ﴿عَلِيماً﴾ (All-Knowing) of what will be before it comes to be, ﴿حَكِيماً﴾ (All-Wise) in what He creates before He creates it.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Concerning the meaning of this and its revelation there are three views:
A- Among them is what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us; he said: Salama narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us; he said: Maʿmar informed us; he said: Qatāda said: "There was a man who heard nothing without retaining it, so the people said: This man retains [all this] only because he has two hearts; and he used to be called 'the one with two hearts' (Dhū al-Qalbayn). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ﴾."
Maʿmar said: And al-Ḥasan said: "There was a man who used to say: One soul commands me to do such-and-such, and another soul commands me to do such-and-such. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾."
Abū Hilāl narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda, who said: In the Jāhiliyya there was a man called Dhū Qalbayn (the one with two hearts), so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: A man of Banū Fihr said: "In my chest there are two hearts; with each one of them I understand better than Muḥammad ﷺ understands." And he lied.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These statements come back to a single meaning, namely that the verse was revealed concerning a particular man; and it is said that the man was "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khaṭal".
B- The second view is a weak view, not sound in the language. It is among the munqaṭiʿ (disconnected) reports of al-Zuhrī, narrated from him by Maʿmar, on His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾: he said: It has reached us that this concerns "Zayd ibn Ḥāritha"; it was struck as a parable for him, saying: the son of another man is not your son.
C- The third view is the soundest of them and the highest in chain of transmission, and its chain is good. It was read out to Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from his father, who said: Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya narrated to us; he said: Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān narrated to us that his father narrated to him, saying: We said to Ibn ʿAbbās: What do you think of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾ — what is meant by it? He said: The Prophet of Allah was praying one day, and a passing thought occurred to him. So the hypocrites who were praying with him said: Do you not see that he has two hearts, one heart with you and one heart with them?! So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the most fitting of the views on the verse, for the reason we have stated.
The meaning is: Allah has not given a man one heart with which he loves and another heart with which he hates, nor one heart with which he believes and another heart with which he disbelieves.
Then He joined to this something with which the polytheists used to divorce, which cannot be [true], and said: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزْوَاجَكُمُ ٱللاَّئِي تُظَاهِرُونَ مِنْهُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ﴾.
It is a word derived from الظَّهر (the back).
Al-Ḥasan read ﴿تَظَاهَرُونَ﴾, and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ rejected this reading and said: This would only be from mutual assistance (al-muʿāwana).
Abū Jaʿfar said: None of this is impossible, since the two words agree [in form]; and الظِّهار (the ẓihār divorce formula) indicates its soundness.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدْعِيَآءَكُمْ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ﴾.
That is, He has not made those whom you adopted and took as sons equivalent to a son in inheritance.
Mujāhid said: This was revealed concerning "Zayd ibn Ḥāritha".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ قَوْلُكُم بِأَفْوَاهِكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلْحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهْدِي ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
That is, it is something you say by way of likening, and it is not a reality.
﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾, that is, the path of truth.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ٱدْعُوهُمْ لآبَآئِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Sālim narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: We used to call "Zayd ibn Ḥāritha" nothing but "Zayd ibn Muḥammad" until ﴿ٱدْعُوهُمْ لآبَآئِهِمْ﴾ was revealed.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, more just.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَعْلَمُوۤاْ آبَاءَهُمْ فَإِخوَانُكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَمَوَالِيكُمْ﴾.
That is, then say: O my brother in religion.
﴿وَمَوَالِيكُمْ﴾, that is, your cousins (the sons of your paternal uncles), or your allies in religion.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ وَلَـٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾.
Concerning its meaning there are three views:
A- Mujāhid said: ﴿فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ﴾: before the prohibition, in this and in other matters.
﴿وَلَـٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾: after the prohibition, in this and in other matters.
B- And it is said «[Translator's note: the text has وقبل, evidently for وقيل "and it is said"]»: ﴿فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ is that one says to him "O my little son" in conversation, without [intending] adoption.
C- Qatāda said: It is that you attribute a man to someone other than his father while you think that he is his father.
This is the most fitting and the clearest of them.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوْلَىٰ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.
Jābir narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: (I am closer to the believers than their own selves; so any man who dies and leaves a debt, it is upon me, and if he leaves wealth, it is for his heirs).
The true meaning of the verse — and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows best — is that when the Prophet ﷺ commanded something, or forbade it, and then the soul opposed him, the command and prohibition of the Prophet ﷺ were more deserving of being followed than [the wishes of] people. «[Translator's note: the text reads إذا أمر شيءٍ, evidently for أمر بشيءٍ "commanded something"; translated accordingly.]»
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ﴾.
That is, in sanctity they have the status of mothers in respect of reverence, and they are not to be married after him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
And it is narrated that this was done only because they are his wives in Paradise.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأُوْلُو ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ ٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ إِلاَّ أَن تَفْعَلُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ أَوْلِيَآئِكُمْ مَّعْرُوفاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, except that you make a bequest to those with whom you made alliances, of the Emigrants and the Helpers. The Messenger of Allah had established brotherhood between the Emigrants, and they used to inherit from one another until this [verse], and bequest was made permissible for them. This is a clear view, because it is far-fetched that a polytheist should be called a walī (ally/close one).
Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, al-Ḥasan and ʿAṭāʾ said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَفْعَلُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ أَوْلِيَآئِكُمْ مَّعْرُوفاً﴾: it is that one makes a bequest to his relatives among the polytheists.
Al-Ḥasan said: He is your walī in lineage, but not your walī in religion.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَانَ ذَلِكَ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ مَسْطُوراً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, written with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, that an unbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that the meaning is: that has been established (ḥalla) in the Book, that is, in the Qurʾān.
And it is possible that "that" is His saying ﴿وَأُوْلُو ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّيْنَ مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: This was in the loins of Adam ﷺ.
Qatāda said: We took their covenant that they would confirm one another.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّيَسْأَلَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ عَن صِدْقِهِمْ﴾.
That is, that He may question the truthful ones among the messengers, as a rebuke to those who denied them, just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاس اتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِنْ دُوَنِ اللَّهِ﴾?
And it is said: that He may question the truthful about their truthfulness — whether it was for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And it is said: so that they may be rewarded for it.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَآءَتْكُمْ جُنُودٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Abū Sufyān, ʿUyayna ibn Badr and Banū Qurayẓa came against them; they are the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً وَجُنُوداً لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: It was the ṣabā (east wind); it overturned their cooking pots and tore out their tents, until it made them depart.
Ibn ʿAbbās narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: (I was given victory by the ṣabā, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the dabūr (west wind)).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجُنُوداً لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: The angels; and they did not fight on that day, "the Day of the Confederates".

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ جَآءُوكُمْ مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: Those who came at them from above them were "Banū Qurayẓa", and those who came at them from below them were "Quraysh" and "Ghaṭafān".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذْ زَاغَتِ ٱلأَبْصَارُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلْحَنَاجِرَ﴾.
Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated from Ayyūb, from ʿIkrima, who said: their terror reached [the throats].
Qatāda said: They rose from their places, and had the throats not been too narrow for them, they would have come out.
And it is said: they almost reached [them].
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of these views is the first, that is, their pounding, from the intensity of the terror, reached the throats, so it is as though they reached the throats through their throbbing.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُنَالِكَ ٱبْتُلِيَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَزُلْزِلُواْ زِلْزَالاً شَدِيداً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, they were purified (tested and sifted).
Then He said: ﴿وَزُلْزِلُواْ زِلْزَالاً شَدِيداً﴾, that is, they were alarmed and shaken.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذْ يَقُولُ ٱلْمُنَافِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾.
Qatāda said: Some people among the hypocrites said: Muḥammad promised us that we would conquer the palaces of Syria and Persia, yet any one of us cannot go beyond his own camp-baggage ﴿مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً﴾.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ يٰأَهْلَ يَثْرِبَ لاَ مُقَامَ لَكُمْ فَٱرْجِعُواْ﴾.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Aʿraj read ﴿لاَ مُقَامَ لَكُمْ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm.
Abū Jaʿfar said: المَقَامُ with fatḥa is the place in which one stands/stays, and [it is also] the maṣdar (verbal noun) of قام يقوم.
And المُقَامُ with ḍamma means residing and the place [of residing], from أقام (he resided) and أقامه غيرُه (someone else made him reside).
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَيَسْتَأْذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوْرَةٌ﴾.
Ibn Isḥāq said: He was "Aws ibn Qayẓī", who said "our houses are exposed", on behalf of a group of his people.
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Abū Rajāʾ read ﴿عَوِرَةٌ﴾ with kasra on the wāw.
One says أَعْورَ المنزلُ (the dwelling became exposed) when it is left unprotected, or has nothing to screen it, or its wall has fallen.
So the meaning is: our houses are unprotected and laid open, with no one to guard them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they are not so, and that the enemy will not reach them, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is guarding them.
Mujāhid said: That is, we fear that they will be robbed.
A woman is also called ʿawra; so it is possible that the meaning is: our houses contain ʿawra (women who must be protected); and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave them the lie.
Qatāda said: Some people among the hypocrites said: Our houses are exposed, and we fear for our families. So the Prophet ﷺ sent [someone] to them, and he found no one in them.
And it is possible that ﴿عَوْرةٌ﴾ is a form with sukūn derived from عَوِرَة.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلاَّ فِرَاراً﴾.
That is, [flight] from supporting the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ لأّتَوْهَا﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿مِّنْ أَقْطَارِهَا﴾, that is, from its sides.
Someone else said: the sides of the houses.
﴿ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ لأَتَوْهَا﴾, that is, they would have headed for it and come to it.
Al-Ḥasan said: The fitna here is shirk (associating partners with Allah).
And it was read: ﴿لآتَوْهَا﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, they would have given it of themselves.
Someone else said: As was narrated concerning those who were tortured, that they gave what was asked of them concerning the Prophet ﷺ — except Bilāl.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلاَّ يَسِيراً﴾.
Al-Qutabī said: That is, in Medina.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
Mujāhid and al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham said concerning His saying ﴿وَإِذاً لاَّ تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: what is between them and the appointed term.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُعَوِّقِينَ مِنكُمْ وَٱلْقَآئِلِينَ لإِخْوَانِهِمْ هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنَا﴾.
Qatāda said: They are a group of the hypocrites who said: The Companions of Muḥammad are, to us, nothing but a handful (a group small enough to be fed by one head [of a slaughtered animal]), and they will never be able to withstand Abū Sufyān and his companions; so come over to us.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتُونَ ٱلْبَأْسَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
That is, only as a pretext (taʿdhīr: a show of effort to be excused).

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ ٱلْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾.
That is, ﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: stingy towards you in spending on your poor and your needy.
﴿فَإِذَا ذَهَبَ ٱلْخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ﴾, that is, they went to extremes in arguing against you.
Qatāda said: They lashed you [with their tongues] in demanding the spoils.
This is a good view, because after it comes ﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ﴾.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās: they confronted you with harm.
Yazīd ibn Rūmān said: They lashed you with what you like [to hear], out of hypocrisy on their part.
One says: خطيبٌ مِسْلاَقٌ and سَلاَّقٌ, that is, an eloquent orator.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أَشِحَّةً عَلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ أوْلَـٰئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾.
That is, stingy over the spoils.
﴿أوْلَـٰئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾: even if they had professed faith outwardly, their belief «[Translator's note: the text has اعتقاهم, evidently for اعتقادهم "their belief"]» was otherwise.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ ٱلأَحْزَابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُواْ وَإِن يَأْتِ ٱلأَحْزَابُ يَوَدُّواْ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بَادُونَ فِي ٱلأَعْرَابِ﴾.
That is, they think the Confederates have not gone to Hell. «[Translator's note: the text reads لجهنم "to Hell"; it may be a corruption of لجبنهم "because of their cowardice"; translated as written.]»
﴿وَإِن يَأْتِ ٱلأَحْزَابُ يَوَدُّواْ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بَادُونَ فِي ٱلأَعْرَابِ﴾: the meaning is: because of their terror and fright, when someone comes to fight them, they wish that they were out in the desert among the Bedouins.
Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: ﴿يَوَدُّوا لَو أَنَّهم بُدَّاً فِي الأَعْرَابِ﴾.
The meaning is the same: it is the plural of بادٍ (a desert-dweller), just as one says غازٍ and غُزَّىً (raider, raiders).

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
Then He, Exalted is He, reported what the believers say, and said: ﴿وَلَمَّا رَأَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلأَحْزَابَ قَالُواْ هَـٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾.
And it is said: what He promised them is in His saying ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُمْ مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مَسَّتْهُمُ البَأْسَاءُ والضَّرَّاءُ﴾; this is what Qatāda said.
Yazīd ibn Rūmān said: The Confederates were Quraysh and Ghaṭafān.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجَالٌ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَاهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
One says صَدَقْتُ العهدَ, that is, I fulfilled the covenant.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَنتَظِرُ وَمَا بَدَّلُواْ تَبْدِيلاً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Masrūq narrated from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿نَحْبَهُ﴾: his covenant.
Khuṣayf narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحْبَهُ﴾:
He said: he died upon what he had pledged; ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَنتَظِرُ﴾ that.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The lexicographers report that النَّحْبُ means the covenant, the soul (life), and the great peril.
The best known of them is that النَّحْبُ is the covenant, as Mujāhid said.
What confirms it is that it is narrated that some people took upon themselves that, if they met the enemy, they would fight truly until they were killed or Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave them victory.
So the meaning is: among them is he who fulfilled his term; and the term was called a covenant because it was in accordance with the covenant; or [the meaning is] he fulfilled his covenant.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا بَدَّلُواْ تَبْدِيلاً﴾.
That is, they did not change their religion in the least.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنَالُواْ خَيْراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: Abū Sufyān and his companions.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَاهَرُوهُم مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ﴾.
That is, those of the People of the Book who aided them.
Mujāhid said: Banū Qurayẓa.
﴿مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ﴾: from their palaces.
Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrima: ﴿مِن صَيَاصِيهِمْ﴾: from their fortresses.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Palaces may be used as fortifications. The root meaning of الصِّيصِيَة
in the language is: that by which one protects oneself; and from this the horns of cattle are called صياصي, and from it is the poet's saying:
* "كَوَقْعِ الصَّياصِي في النَّسِيِج المُمَدَّدِ" * (like the striking of the weaver's spurs/horns on the outstretched woven cloth)
One says: جذَّ اللهُ صِيصَتَه, that is, [may Allah cut off] his root.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَوْرَثَكُمْ أَرْضَهُمْ وَدِيَارَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ وَأَرْضاً لَّمْ تَطَئُوهَا﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: Persia and Byzantium.
Qatāda said: Mecca.
Ibn Isḥāq said: Khaybar. «[Translator's note: the text spells it خبير; the place meant is Khaybar (خيبر). Likewise below.]»
Abū Jaʿfar said: All of these Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has given the Muslims as an inheritance.
However, what most resembles the meaning is that it be "Khaybar", and Allah knows best.
