Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَأَرْضاً لَّمْ تَطَئُوهَا﴾: he said: whatever will be conquered by the Muslims until the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لأَزْوَاجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحْكُنَّ سَرَاحاً جَمِيلاً﴾.
Yūnus narrated from al-Zuhrī, from Abū Salama, from ʿĀʾisha; and Maʿmar from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said: "I am going to mention a matter to you, and you need not hasten in it until you consult your parents." She said: He knew that my parents would never command me to leave him. Then he recited ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لأَزْوَاجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَزِينَتَهَا﴾, and I said: Is it about this that I should consult my parents? For I choose Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and His Messenger and the abode of the Hereafter.
Yūnus said in his ḥadīth: And his wives did as she had done, and that was not a divorce, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them the choice and they chose him.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُّبَيِّنَةٍ يُضَاعَفْ لَهَا ٱلْعَذَابُ ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾.
Abū ʿAmr distinguished between ﴿يُضَعَّفْ﴾ and ﴿يُضَاعَفْ﴾; he said: يُضاعَفُ is for many times, and يُضَعَّفُ is twice; and he read ﴿يُضَعَّفْ﴾ for this reason.
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهَا ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾: it is made three punishments.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The distinction that "Abū ʿAmr" brought is not known to any of the lexicographers, as far as I know. The meaning of ﴿يُضاعَفْ﴾ and ﴿يُضَعَّفْ﴾ is one: that is, it is made two ḍiʿfs, that is, two equivalents — as you say: if you give me a dirham I will give you its ḍiʿfayn, that is, its two equivalents, meaning two dirhams. What indicates this is ﴿نُؤْتها أجرها مرَّتيْن﴾, so the punishment would not be more than the reward.
And He said in another place: ﴿رَبَّنَا آتِهِمْ ضِعْفَيْنِ مِنَ العَذَابِ﴾, that is, two equivalents.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهَا ٱلْعَذَابُ ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾:
He said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَقْنُتْ مِنكُنَّ للَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: whoever obeys.
Qatāda said: Every qunūt in the Qurʾān is obedience.
And he said: ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لَهَا رِزْقاً كَرِيماً﴾: Paradise.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ تَخْضَعْنَ بِٱلْقَوْلِ فَيَطْمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾.
One says خَضَع في قوله (he was soft in his speech) when he spoke softly and did not speak plainly.
This is made clear by His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَقُلْنَ قَوْلاً مَّعْرُوفاً﴾, that is, plain and clear.
Qatāda and al-Suddī said: ﴿فَيَطْمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾, that is, doubt and hypocrisy.
ʿIkrima said: It is the desire for fornication.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلاَ تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
It is from وَقَر، يَقِرُ، وَقَاراً في المكان: when one remains fixed in a place. And there is another view on it:
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd «[Translator's note: al-Mubarrad]» said: It is from قَرَرْتُ في المكان أقِرُّ (I stayed in the place), and the underlying form is واقْرَرْن. It came according to the dialect of those who say مِسْتُ for مَسِسْتُ: the first rāʾ was omitted and its vowel was thrown onto the qāf, so it became ﴿وَقِرْنَ﴾.
He said: And whoever reads ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ has committed a solecism (laḥn).
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is possible that ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ is from قَرَرْتُ به عيناً أقَرُّ (my eye was cooled by it, i.e. I was content with it), so the meaning would be: and be content (with cooled eyes) in your houses.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Aḥmar narrated from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾ is what was between Idrīs and Noah, may Allah bless them both.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr narrated from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: There will be another Jāhiliyya.
Hushaym narrated from Zakariyyā, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: ﴿ٱلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾ is what was between Jesus and Muḥammad, may Allah bless them both.
Mujāhid said: Women used to walk about among the men; that is the tabarruj.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: It is strutting.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Tabarruj in the language is displaying adornment and that by which desire is invited. This was widespread between Jesus and Muḥammad, may Allah bless them both, and there were prostitutes then who were sought out.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنكُـمُ ٱلرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ ٱلْبَيْتِ﴾.
ʿAṭiyya said: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated to me; he said: Umm Salama narrated to me; she said: This verse was revealed in a house while I was sitting at the door. I said: O Messenger of Allah, am I not of the People of the House? He said: You are [headed] towards good, and you are among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. And in the house were "the Prophet, ʿAlī, Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn", Allah's blessings be upon them.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱذْكُـرْنَ مَا يُتْـلَىٰ فِي بُيُوتِكُـنَّ مِنْ آيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْحِكْـمَةِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, the Qurʾān and the Sunna.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated from Abū Salama, from Umm Salama, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, I see Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioning men and not mentioning women. Then ﴿إنَّ المُسْلِمِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمَاتِ وَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ والْقَانِتِينَ وَالْقَانِتَاتِ﴾ was revealed.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْحَافِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمْ وَٱلْحَافِـظَاتِ﴾.
That is, "and the women who guard them" (والحافِظَاتِها, with the object omitted). A parallel to it is:
وكُمْتاً مُدَمَّاةً كَأَنَّ مُتُونَها * ـ جَرَى فَوقَها وَاستْشْعَرتْ ـ لَوْنُ مُذَهب
(And bay horses of blood-red hue, as though their backs — [the colour] ran over them and they took it as an undergarment — were the colour of something gilded.)
Sībawayh narrated it as "لونَ مُذْهَب" in the accusative; the nominative is only permissible on the omission of the hāʾ (the object pronoun), as though he said: فاستَشْعرتْهُ (and they took it as an undergarment), for whoever puts "لون" in the nominative.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلاَ مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْراً﴾.
Qatāda said: When the Prophet ﷺ asked for the hand of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh — she was the daughter of his paternal aunt — intending her for Zayd, she thought that he wanted her for himself. When she learned that he wanted her for Zayd, she refused and held back. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلاَ مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْراً أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾, and she obeyed and submitted.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيۤ أَنعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: He is "Zayd ibn Ḥāritha"; Allah favoured him with Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ favoured him with emancipation. Then He said: ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ وَتَخْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَاهُ﴾
Thābit narrated from Anas, who said: "Zayd came complaining about Zaynab to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to him ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ﴾. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيۤ أَنعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ to the end of the verse.
He said: Had the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him, concealed anything of the Qurʾān, he would have concealed this."
Qatāda said: Zayd came and said: O Messenger of Allah, I complain to you about Zaynab's tongue, and I want to divorce her. He said to him: ﴿أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ﴾. The Prophet ﷺ would have liked Zayd to divorce her, but he disliked saying to him "divorce her" lest people hear of it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, and be led into temptation (fitna).
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon him, was asked about this verse, and he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed the Prophet ﷺ that Zayd would divorce Zaynab and that the Prophet ﷺ would then marry her after him.
That is: I had informed you that he would divorce her, before he divorced her.
* His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيْدٌ مِّنْهَا وَطَراً زَوَّجْنَاكَهَا﴾.
Al-Khalīl said: The meaning of "الوَطَر" is every need that one is concerned with; when one has fulfilled it, it is said: قَضَى وَطَرَه and أرَبَه (he fulfilled his need).
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave the reason for which the affair of Zayd happened as it did, and said: ﴿لِكَيْ لاَ يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِيۤ أَزْوَاجِ أَدْعِيَآئِهِمْ إِذَا قَضَوْاْ مِنْهُنَّ وَطَراً﴾.
That is: We married you to Zaynab, who had been the wife of "Zayd" while you had adopted him, lest it be imagined that "the prohibition through adoption" is like the prohibition through birth, as the Jāhiliyya used to say.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنْ حَرَجٍ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, in what Allah made lawful for him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: In it there is a sense of praise, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَا عَلَى المُحْسِنينَ مِنْ سَبيلٍ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوْاْ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is, they are not taken to task for what was not forbidden to them.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيباً﴾.
It may be in the sense of "مُحَاسِب" (one who takes account), as you say أَكيلٌ (fellow eater) and شريبٌ (fellow drinker).
And it may be in the sense of "مُحْسِب", that is, sufficient; one says أحسَبَني الشيءُ: it sufficed me.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَآ أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon him, said: It was revealed concerning "Zayd ibn Ḥāritha".
Abū Jaʿfar said: That is, he is not their father by birth, even if he is so in veneration and honour.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن رَّسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, the last of them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Whoever reads ﴿خَاتَمَ﴾ with fatḥa on the tāʾ, its meaning for him is: the last of them. And whoever reads with kasra, ﴿خَاتِمَ﴾, its meaning is that he sealed them.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً﴾ [Verse 42]:
the dawn prayer and the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلاَئِكَتُهُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: The Children of Israel asked Moses, may Allah bless him: Does your Lord pray? It was as though he considered that grave, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed to him: "My prayer is that My mercy outstrips My wrath."
And al-aṣīl is the late afternoon/evening (al-ʿashiyy).
Al-Farrāʾ said: The meaning of ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلاَئِكَتُهُ﴾ is: He it is who forgives you, and His angels ask forgiveness for you.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَحِيَّتُهُمْ يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ سَلاَمٌ﴾.
It is as He said: ﴿وَالمَلائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ بَابٍ. سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
That is, their greeting in Paradise is "Peace".

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾.
﴿شَاهِداً﴾, that is, a witness to the conveying [of the message].
﴿وَمُبَشِّراً﴾: of Paradise.
﴿وَنَذِيرَاً﴾: of the Fire.
﴿وَدَاعِيَاً إلى اللَّهِ بِإذْنِهِ﴾, that is, by His command.
﴿وَسِرَاجَاً مُنِيرَاً﴾, that is, and possessor of a lamp, which is the Qurʾān.
And it may be that the meaning is: and one who makes clear and who recites.
Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Rāzī narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Azdī narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥammad al-Muḥāribī narrated to us, from Shaybān al-Naḥwī; he said: Qatāda narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً، وَدَاعِياً إلَى اللَّهِ بإذْنِهِ وَسِرَاجاً مُنِيرَاً﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah called ʿAlī and Muʿādh and said: Go, and make things easy and do not make them difficult, for tonight a verse has been revealed to me: ﴿إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾ — of the Fire — ﴿وَدَاعِياً إلَى اللَّهِ﴾ — he said: to the testimony that there is no god but Allah — ﴿بإذْنِهِ﴾: by His command — ﴿وسِرَاجاً مُنِيرَاً﴾ — he said: by the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ وَٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ وَدَعْ أَذَاهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَدَعْ أَذَاهُمْ﴾, that is, turn away from them.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِذَا نَكَحْتُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ فَمَا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ عِدَّةٍ تَعْتَدُّونَهَا﴾.
Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon him, was asked about a man who said to a woman: If I marry you, you are divorced. He said: It is nothing. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned marriage before divorce, saying: ﴿إِذَا نَكَحْتُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾.
* His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ وَسَرِّحُوهُنَّ سَرَاحاً جَمِيلاً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: It is abrogated by the one in al-Baqara, meaning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَإنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾ — that is, He did not mention the mutʿa (the parting gift) [there].

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ أَزْوَاجَكَ ٱللاَّتِيۤ آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, their dowries.
Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated from Umm Hāniʾ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked for my hand, and I excused myself to him, and he excused me. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ أَزْوَاجَكَ ٱللاَّتِيۤ آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ up to His saying ﴿ٱللاَّتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ﴾; and I had not emigrated — I was only one of the ṭulaqāʾ (those pardoned at the conquest of Mecca) — so I was not lawful for him.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱمْرَأَةً مُّؤْمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with him, ʿUrwa and al-Shaʿbī said: She is "Umm Sharīk".
Al-Zuhrī, ʿIkrima and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: She is "Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith"; she gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Zuhrī said: And "Sawda" gave her day to ʿĀʾisha.
Al-Ḥasan read ﴿أَنْ وَهَبَتْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read: ﴿وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً وَهَبَتْ﴾.
Reading "إِنْ" with kasra (the conditional) is the most comprehensive of the meanings, because it has been said that they were [several] women; whereas if it is read with fatḥa, the meaning concerns one particular woman, because the fatḥa [reading] is as a badal (substitute) for امرأة, and in the sense of لأَنْ (because).
Mujāhid said: She did not give herself.
On this view, "إِنْ" can only be with kasra.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا﴾ is: if she is married without a dowry.
And it is said: it is that she makes the gift [of herself] the dowry, and that this is not lawful for anyone after the Prophet ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is preferable, because the meaning of hiba (gift) in the language is handing over something without compensation.
* His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا فَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيۤ أَزْوَاجِهِـمْ﴾.
That is, We know what benefit there is in that. This is a commonly used expression; one says: I know what is [good] for you in this.
Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا فَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيۤ أَزْوَاجِهِـمْ﴾: he said: two, three and four.
Qatāda said: It was made obligatory upon them that there is no marriage except with a guardian, two upright witnesses and a dowry, and that a man may not marry more than four.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكَيْلاَ يَكُونَ عَلَيْكَ حَرَجٌ﴾:
It is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying ﴿إِنَّآ أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ أَزْوَاجَكَ ٱللاَّتِيۤ آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِيۤ إِلَيْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ﴾.
Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنْهُنَّ﴾: he said: This concerns the women who gave themselves.
Al-Shaʿbī said: They are the women who gave themselves; the Messenger of Allah married some of them and left some of them.
Al-Zuhrī said: We do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deferred any of his wives; rather, he took them all to himself.
Qatāda said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was left free to divide [his time] among them however he wished, yet he did not divide among them except with fairness.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us: Salama narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Razīn, who said: "The deferred ones were Maymūna, Sawda, Ṣafiyya, Juwayriya and Umm Ḥabība; and ʿĀʾisha, Ḥafṣa, Umm Salama and Zaynab were equal in the Prophet's ﷺ division [of time]; he treated them equally in the division."
Mujāhid said: It is that he keeps away from them without divorce.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The statements of Qatāda, Abū Razīn and Mujāhid come back to a single meaning: that this concerns the division [of time].
Manṣūr narrated from Abū Razīn that the Messenger ﷺ wanted to release those whom he had deferred, and they said to him: Divide for us however you wish, and leave us as we are. So he left them.
Qatāda said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿ذَلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَن تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ﴾:
When they know that this is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, their eyes are cooled, they do not grieve, and they are content.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ يَحِلُّ لَكَ ٱلنِّسَآءُ مِن بَعْدُ﴾.
Concerning this verse there are [several] views:
A- Among them is what Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not die until women were made lawful for him.
B- Al-Ḥasan said: When the Prophet ﷺ gave his wives the choice and they chose him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, rewarded them for that, and forbade the Prophet ﷺ to marry others besides them; that is, He tested him with that as He had tested them.
C- ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: He was permitted to marry.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These three views are not contradictory.
ʿĀʾisha's saying, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not die until women were made lawful for him", has a good chain; it is interpreted as abrogating the prohibition, and it is adduced as evidence that the Sunna abrogates the Qurʾān — as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنْ تَرَكَ خَيْرَاً الوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوالِدَيْنِ وَالأَقرَبِيِنَ﴾, while the Prophet ﷺ said: (No bequest for an heir).
The position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is that what abrogates it is His saying ﴿تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَ وتُؤْوي إلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾.
This is not sound, because after it comes ﴿ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلاَ يَحْزَنَّ﴾.
As for the statement of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon him, it may come back to ʿĀʾisha's statement, even though he rejected al-Ḥasan's statement; for al-Ḥasan did not mention that the verse is abrogated, so he may have rejected it from this angle, the verse being abrogated in his view.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, compensated the wives of the Prophet ﷺ for that by making them his wives in Paradise.
There is something else on the verse: Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: I asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لاَّ يَحِلُّ لَكَ ٱلنِّسَآءُ مِن بَعْدُ﴾, and said: Was it lawful for him to marry? He said: Yes, there is no harm in that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّا أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ أَزْوَاجَكَ اللاَّتي آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً﴾
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لاَّ يَحِلُّ لَكَ ٱلنِّسَآءُ مِن بَعْدُ﴾, that is, mothers, sisters and daughters are not lawful for you. This is another view.
That is: women are not lawful for you beyond those We have made lawful, except what your right hand possesses.
Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥakam held another view.
They said: ﴿لاَّ يَحِلُّ لَكَ ٱلنِّسَآءُ مِن بَعْدُ﴾, that is, Jewish women and Christian women are not lawful for you.
Mujāhid said: That is, it is not lawful for you to marry an unbelieving woman who would then be a mother of the believers, even if her beauty pleased you — except what your right hand possesses, for he may take her as a concubine.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ﴾.
Anas ibn Mālik said: I am the most knowledgeable of people about this verse. When the Prophet ﷺ married "Zaynab bint Jaḥsh", he commanded me to invite everyone I met. The Prophet ﷺ invited [people], and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, put blessing in the food. Some people ate and left, and a group remained, while "Zaynab" was in the house. The Prophet ﷺ went in and came out while they were [still] sitting. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ put up the screen, and they left.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ﴾:
not waiting for the moment of its being cooked.
﴿وَلاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ﴾: he said: after eating.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَاعاً فَٱسْأَلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ﴾.
So it was not lawful for anyone to ask them for food or anything else, or to look at them, whether veiled or unveiled, except from behind a screen.
When ʿĀʾisha circumambulated the House, she was screened.
In the ḥadīth: When Zaynab died, ʿUmar said: None shall go out in her funeral except a maḥram (close male relative) of hers. Then the bier [with a canopy] was described to him, and he approved of it and ordered it, and said: Go out and pray over your mother.
Anas said: I used to go in to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ; when this verse was revealed, I came to go in, and the Prophet ﷺ said to me: Stay back, my son.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تؤْذُواْ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلاَ أَن تَنكِحُوۤاْ أَزْوَاجَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ أَبَداً﴾.
Qatāda said: A man among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies, I will marry so-and-so.
Maʿmar said: It was "Ṭalḥa" who said this, about ʿĀʾisha.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَّ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ فِيۤ آبَآئِهِنَّ وَلاَ أَبْنَآئِهِنَّ وَلاَ إِخْوَانِهِنَّ وَلاَ أَبْنَآءِ إِخْوَانِهِنَّ وَلاَ أَبْنَآءِ أَخَوَاتِهِنَّ وَلاَ نِسَآئِهِنَّ وَلاَ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ﴾.
That is, regarding asking permission.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ نِسَآئِهِنَّ﴾ is: nor the people of their religion.
And it has been said: rather it is for all women, that is, those of their own kind.
And it is said: ﴿وَلاَ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ﴾ refers to women specifically.
And it is said: it is general, as long as no suspicion is known.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلاَئِكَـتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ﴾.
Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us in the gathering of "Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda", and Bashīr ibn Saʿd said to him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah; so how shall we send blessings upon you? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent until we wished he had not asked him. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: Say: "O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, [as You blessed Abraham; and grant grace to Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad], as You granted grace to Abraham, among all the worlds; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." And the salutation is as you have been taught.
Al-Masʿūdī narrated from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Fākhita, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, that he said: When you send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, make your blessing upon him excellent, for you do not know — perhaps Allah presents that to him?! They said: Then teach us. He said: Say «[Translator's note: the text has قال قالوا "he said: they said"; translated as "he said: say"]»:
- "O Allah, place Your blessings, Your mercy and Your grace upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the God-fearing and the seal of the prophets, Muḥammad, Your servant and Your messenger, the leader of good, the guide to good, and the messenger of mercy.
- O Allah, raise him to a praised station for which the first and the last will envy him. - O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
- O Allah, grant grace to Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad as You granted grace to Abraham and the family of Abraham; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
It is said: the meaning is: they harm the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah.
Hammām narrated from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said:
(My servant reviled Me, and it was not for him to revile Me.
And he denied Me, and it was not fitting for him to deny Me.
As for his reviling Me, it is his saying: I have taken a son — while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient (al-Ṣamad). And as for his denying Me, he claims that he will never be resurrected).
Meaning: after death.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ بِغَيْرِ مَا ٱكْتَسَبُواْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: They slander the believing men and the believing women for what they did not do.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لأَزْوَاجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلاَبِيبِهِنَّ﴾.
Abū Mālik and al-Ḥasan said: Women used to go out at night for their needs, and the hypocrites would molest them, taking them to be slave women. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لأَزْوَاجِكَ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is more likely that they be known to be free women, and so not be molested.
Al-Ḥasan said: She covers half of her face.
When ʿUmar saw a slave woman who had covered her head, he would strike her with the whip (al-dirra).
Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said: I asked ʿAbīda about His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلاَبِيبِهِنَّ﴾, and he said: She covers her eyebrow with the cloak, then turns it back over her nose, until she covers her head, her face and one of her eyes.
Mujāhid said: They wrap themselves in the jilbāb so that they are recognised, and so are not molested with words.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ ٱلْمُنَافِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّرَضٌ وَٱلْمُرْجِفُونَ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: Some of the hypocrites wanted to make their hypocrisy public, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿لَّئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ ٱلْمُنَافِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّرَضٌ وَٱلْمُرْجِفُونَ فِي ٱلْمَدِينَةِ لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾, that is, We shall surely set you against them.
Mālik ibn Dīnār said: I asked ʿIkrima about His saying ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَّرَضٌ﴾, and he said: fornication; and likewise Shahr ibn Ḥawshab.
Ṭāwūs said: This verse was revealed concerning the matter of women.
Salama ibn Kuhayl said: It was revealed concerning the people of indecencies.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يُجَاوِرُونَكَ فِيهَآ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
The meaning may be: except while they are few.
And the meaning may be: except for a short time.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ آذَوْاْ مُوسَىٰ فَبرَّأَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِمَّا قَالُواْ وَكَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَجِيهاً﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us; he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us; he said: Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda narrated to us; he said: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayra, concerning this verse ﴿لاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ آذَوْاْ مُوسَىٰ فَبرَّأَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِمَّا قَالُواْ﴾: he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Moses ﷺ was a shy man who kept himself covered; hardly anything of his skin could be seen, out of shyness. So those of the Children of Israel who harmed him did so, saying: He does not cover himself like this except because of a defect in his skin — either leprosy, or a scrotal hernia, or some ailment. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, wanted to clear him of what they said. One day Moses was alone by himself; he put his garment on a stone and then bathed. When he finished his bath, he went to his garment to take it, but the stone ran off with his garment. So Moses took his staff and went after the stone, saying: My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone! — until he reached an assembly of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, the best of men in form, and they cleared him of what they had said about him. Then the stone stopped, and he took his garment and put it on. He said: Then he began striking the stone. He said: By Allah, there are marks on the stone from his striking — three, or four, or five."
Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn narrated from al-Ḥakam, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī, peace be upon him, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ آذَوْاْ مُوسَىٰ فَبرَّأَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِمَّا قَالُواْ﴾: he said: Moses and Aaron, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, went up the mountain, and Aaron, peace be upon him, died. The Children of Israel said to Moses: You killed him; he was gentler with us than you and more loving. So he was harmed by that. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by the assemblies of the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death, until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. Then they buried him, and no one knew the place of his grave except the vultures (al-rakham), for Allah had made it deaf and dumb.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: do not harm Muḥammad ﷺ as the people of Moses harmed Moses, and Allah cleared him of what they said — of what they accused him of in both matters together.
﴿وَكَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَجِيهاً﴾, that is, He spoke to him directly.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَقُولُواْ قَوْلاً سَدِيداً﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَقُولُواْ قَوْلاً سَدِيداً﴾, that is, what is right (sadād).
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, truthfully.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا ٱلأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلْجِبَالِ فَأبَيْنَ أَن يَحْمِلْنَهَا﴾.
Concerning this verse there are [several] views:
A- Among them is that the meaning is: to the inhabitants of the heavens.
And the meaning of ﴿عَرَضْنَا﴾ would be "We displayed", as you say: I displayed the goods.
And ﴿فَأبَيْنَ﴾ would follow the wording of the first «[Translator's note: i.e. the feminine plural agreeing with the heavens, the earth and the mountains]», because not all of them bore it; and the meaning would be: they refused to accept it.
﴿وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلإِنْسَانُ﴾, that is, he took it upon himself, and all of them have been charged with it.
B- And it is said: When death approached Adam ﷺ, he was commanded to offer the trust to creation; he offered it, and none accepted it except his sons.
C- A third view, which is the one held by the people of tafsīr:
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us; he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا ٱلأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلْجِبَالِ﴾: he said: The trust is the obligations (al-farāʾiḍ). Allah offered them to the heavens, the earth and the mountains: if they discharged them He would reward them, and if they neglected them He would punish them. They disliked that and were afraid — not out of disobedience, but out of reverence for the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, lest they fail to uphold it. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with all that it contained; and that is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلإِنْسَانُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ ظَلُوماً جَهُولاً﴾ — naïve about the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Mujāhid said: Allah offered reward and punishment to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they refused it and were afraid of it. It was said to Adam, and he accepted it; and he remained in Paradise only two hours.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The obligations were offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they were afraid of them and declined, and Adam ﷺ accepted them.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: Reward and punishment were offered to Adam.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The trust is obedience. It was offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains — if they went against it they would be punished — and they refused, and man bore it.
Qatāda said: The obligations were offered to creation, and they refused, except Adam ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: These views — and they are the views of the leading authorities among the people of tafsīr — are interpreted in two senses:
One of them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave these things that by which they can discern, then offered them the obligations, obedience and disobedience.
The other sense: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, entrusted the son of Adam with obedience, and entrusted these things with obedience and submission; and He informed us that these things did not "bear" the trust, that is, they did not betray it. One says حملَ الأمانةَ and احتملها, that is, he betrayed it and bore its sin.
And it is said the meaning is: and man bore it and did not fulfil it, and [this] was omitted because the one addressed knows it. And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قَالَتَا أَتَيْنَا طَائِعِيِنَ﴾, and He said: ﴿وَإنَّ مِنْها لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ﴾.
﴿وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلإِنْسَانُ﴾, that is, he betrayed it and bore its sin.
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلإِنْسَانُ﴾, that is, the unbeliever and the hypocrite.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Ḥasan's statement points to the second interpretation, and it is also indicated by His saying ﴿لِيُعَذَّبَ اللَّهُ المُنَافِقِينَ وَالمُنَافِقَاتِ والمُشْرِكِينَ وَالمُشْرِكَاتِ، وَيتُوبَ اللهُ عَلَى المُؤْمِنيِنَ وَالمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَكَانَ اللهُ عَفُورَاً رَحِيمَاً﴾.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, (النبيّ) a badal (substitute) of أي, following it in the nominative in outward form, (الواو) conjunction in both places, (لا) prohibitive, making jussive, and the sign of the jussive in (تطع) is the sukūn, and its end was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
The vocative clause «يأيّها..» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «اتّق ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «لا تطع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّ الله كان عليما ...» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of the command and an emphasis of its content.
The clause «كان عليما ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
(2) (الواو) conjunction, (ما) a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) in the position of an accusative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (يوحى) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, and it is the linking pronoun, (إليك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يوحى), (من ربّك) attached to (يوحى) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun that is the nāʾib fāʿil.], (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, and the linking pronoun is omitted, i.e. تعملونه.] ...
The clause «اتّبع..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «يوحى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله كان..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كان.. خبيرا..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle or nominal relative (ما).
(3) (الواو) conjunction, (على الله) attached to (توكّل), (الله) the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) in its outward form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, the fāʿil (agent) of كفى, (وكيلا) a ḥāl, accusative [Note: or a tamyīz (specification), accusative.].
The clause «توكّل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «كفى بالله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(اتّق): it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, in keeping with the indeclinable (imperative) form; its imperfect is يتّقي; its pattern is افتع [Note: and it contains a substitution (ibdāl).. see the discussion at verse (24) of Sūrat al-Baqara.].

* Benefits:
- No safe-conduct for the disbelievers:
This verse was revealed concerning Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb, ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl, Abū al-Aʿwar and ʿAmr ibn Sufyān al-Sulamī. That is because they came to Medina and stayed with ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, the head of the hypocrites, after the battle of Uḥud. The Prophet ﷺ had given them safe-conduct so that they could speak with him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ and Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq stood up with them, and they said to the Prophet ﷺ, while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was with him: Stop mentioning our gods al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt, and say: they have intercession for whoever worships them, and we will leave you and your Lord alone. That was hard on the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, permit me to kill them. He said: I have given them safe-conduct. So ʿUmar said: Get out, under the curse of Allah and His wrath. The Prophet ﷺ ordered ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, to expel them from Medina, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative, (لرجل) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جعل) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the meaning of خلق (created), (قلبين) genitive (majrūr) in its outward form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), (في جوفه) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of قلبين, (الواو) conjunction in the four places, (اللائي) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, a naʿt of أزواج, (منهنّ) attached to (تظاهرون) by its being made to contain the meaning of تتباعدون (you distance yourselves), (أمّهاتكم) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governor being جعل, and likewise (أبناءكم) for the third verb, (بأفواهكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of قولكم, the governor in it being the demonstrative.
The clause «ما جعل الله لرجل..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما جعل أزواجكم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to a resumptive clause.
The clause «تظاهرون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (اللائي).
The clause «ما جعل أدعياءكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ذلكم قولكم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «الله يقول الحقّ..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ذلكم قولكم.
The clause «يقول الحقّ..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
The clause «هو يهدي..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause الله يقول.
The clause «يهدي السبيل..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو).
(5) (لآبائهم) attached to (ادعوهم), (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to أقسط, (الفاء) conjunction, (تعلموا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), (الفاء) the second is linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (إخوانكم) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هم, (في الدين) attached to إخوانكم because it carries the sense of a derived word, i.e. those who agree with you in religion, (مواليكم) conjoined to إخوانكم by (الواو), nominative like it, its sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, (الواو) conjunction, (عليكم) attached to the khabar of ليس, (في ما) attached to جناح, (به) attached to (أخطأتم), (لكن) for istidrāk (rectification), (ما) a relative, conjoined to the preceding ما, in the position of a genitive [Note: it may be a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e.: what your hearts intended, you are answerable for it..], (الواو) resumptive, (رحيما) a second khabar, accusative.
The clause «ادعوهم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «هو أقسط..» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لم تعملوا ...» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic wording is لم تعلموا.] has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ادعوهم..
The clause «(هم) إخوانكم» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ليس عليكم جناح» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم تعلموا ...
The clause «أخطأتم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative (ما).
The clause «تعمّدت قلوبكم..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «كان الله غفورا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive..

* Morphology:
(جوف): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the inside of the body in a human, an animal or other; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.
(أدعياء): plural of دعيّ, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); its pattern is فعيل in the sense of مفعول; it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is دعيو with kasra on the ʿayn and sukūn on the yāʾ; the yāʾ and the wāw came together in the word with the first quiescent, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ ...
Its plural on أفعلاء is not by analogy (ghayr maqīs), because فعيل here is not in the sense of فاعل, as in تقيّ and أتقياء; its analogical form would be on the pattern فعلى with fatḥa then sukūn, as in قتيل and قتلى.

* Benefits:
Can a man have two hearts?
The exegetes said: it was revealed concerning Abū Maʿmar Ḥumayd ibn Maʿmar al-Fihrī. He was an intelligent man who retained what he heard, and Quraysh said: Abū Maʿmar has only retained these things because he has two hearts. He used to say: I have two hearts, with each of which I understand better than Muḥammad's understanding. When Allah defeated the idolaters on the day of Badr, Abū Maʿmar fled in defeat, and Abū Sufyān met him with one of his sandals in his hand and the other on his foot. He said to him: O Abū Maʿmar, how are the people? He said: they have been routed. He said to him: then why is one of your sandals in your hand and the other on your foot? So they knew that day that if he had two hearts he would not have forgotten his sandal in his hand.
From Abū Ẓabyān, who said: we said to Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah be pleased with them both —: what do you think of the saying of Allah:
ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه — what did He mean by it? He said: the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood one day praying, and a passing thought occurred to him, and the hypocrites who were praying with him said: do you not see that he has two hearts: a heart with you and a heart with them. So Allah revealed ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِنْ قَلْبَيْنِ فِي جَوْفِهِ. Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it and said: a ḥasan (good) ḥadīth.
As for the discussion of ẓihār, it will come in detail in Sūrat al-Mujādala, if Allah the Exalted wills.
2- Abolishing the custom of adoption:
The verse conveyed the abrogation and cancellation of adoption. That is because in the Jāhiliyya a man would adopt a man and make him like a son born to him; people would call him by [the adopter's name], and he would inherit from him.
The Prophet ﷺ had freed Zayd ibn Ḥāritha ibn Shuraḥbīl al-Kalbī and adopted him before the revelation, and he made him a brother to Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, who had been the wife of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, the hypocrites said: Muḥammad has married his son's wife, while he forbids people from that. So Allah revealed this verse,
and abrogated adoption with it. More about this story will come in later verses of this sūra, if Allah wills.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(بالمؤمنين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) أولى, (من أنفسهم) attached to أولى, (بعضهم) a second mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is أولى, (ببعض) attached to the khabar أولى, (في كتاب) attached to أولى [Note: it may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in أولى, which is the governor.], (من المؤمنين) attached to أولى [Note: it may be attached to a ḥāl of (أولو الأرحام) by way of clarification.], (إلّا) for exception, (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تفعلوا ...) is in the position of an accusative by the disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
(إلى أوليائكم) attached to (تفعلوا) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the meaning of تقدّموا (you advance), (في الكتاب) attached to (مسطورا).
The clause «النبيّ أولى..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أزواجه أمّهاتهم..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أولو الأرحام بعضهم..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «بعضهم أولى..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of (أولو).
The clause «تفعلوا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «كان ذلك.. مسطورا» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(الأرحام): plural of رحم, which is kinship; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then kasra.

* Rhetoric:
The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَزْواجُهُ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ».
It is a likening of them to mothers in some rulings, namely: the obligation of honouring and respecting them, and the prohibition of marrying them. For that reason ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: «We are not the mothers of the women», meaning that they were only mothers of the men, since they were forbidden to them as their mothers are forbidden; and for this reason the particle of likening must be assumed in it.

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (إذ) a ṣarfī noun [Translator's note: so in the source (اسم صرفيّ); elsewhere the book says اسم ظرفيّ, "an adverbial noun".] in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر, (من النبيين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخذنا), and likewise (منك) and (من نوح), (إبراهيم) conjoined to نوح, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa, (ابن) a naʿt (adjective) of عيسى, or a badal (substitute), or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it, genitive, (منهم) attached to the second (أخذنا).
The clause «أخذنا..» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «أخذنا (the second)» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذنا (the first).
(8) (اللام) of causation, (يسأل) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Allah, (عن صدقهم) attached to (يسأل), (للكافرين) attached to (أعدّ).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يسأل ...) is in the position of a genitive, attached to (أخذنا) [Note: in the speech there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the first person to the third.].
The clause «يسأل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أعدّ ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause أخذنا.

* Rhetoric:
Conjoining the specific to the general: in His saying, the Exalted: «وَمِنْكَ وَمِنْ نُوحٍ وَإِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ».
Because these five mentioned are the possessors of the laws and the Books, and the messengers of firm resolve (ulū al-ʿazm); so He singled them out for mention, to announce their additional distinction and excellence, and that they are among the famous bearers of the laws and the pillars of the messengers of firm resolve. Putting our Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, first is to make clear his lofty standing.
The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَخَذْنا مِنْهُمْ مِيثاقاً غَلِيظاً».
Thickness (al-ghilaẓ) is a metaphor borrowed from the description of bodies, and what is meant is the greatness of the covenant and the majesty of its standing.

safi-cedvel:9-15.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative [Note: and (ها) is for alerting (tanbīh), with no grammatical position.], (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of the one addressed — or a badal (substitute) of it —, (عليكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) نعمة, (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of an accusative, a badal of نعمة, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) [Note: it may be attached to نعمة.], (عليهم) attached to (أرسلنا), (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the linking pronoun being omitted, i.e. تعملونه, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).].
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما تعملون ...) is in the position of a genitive by (الباء), attached to (بصيرا).
The vocative clause «يا أيّها الذين..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «اذكروا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «جاءتكم جنود....» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «أرسلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause جاءتكم.
The clause «لم تروها ...» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt of (جنودا).
The clause «كان الله ... بصيرا» has no grammatical position: a parenthetical resumption.
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
(10) (إذ) a badal of the first, in the position of an accusative, (من فوقكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of جاؤوكم, and likewise (من أسفل), for it is conjoined to the first, (منكم) attached to أسفل, (إذ) conjoined to the preceding إذ, (بالله) attached to (تظنّون) [Note: in the sense of "you doubt".. or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with (الظنون) as the first object.], and (الألف) in (الظنونا) is redundant (zāʾida).
The clause «جاؤوكم....» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «زاغت الأبصار» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «بلغت القلوب..» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause زاغت.
The clause «تظنّون....» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause زاغت.
(11) (هنالك) a demonstrative in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (ابتلي), (زلزالا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «ابتلي ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «زلزلوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ابتلي.
(12) (إذ) conjoined to the preceding إذ, (في قلوبهم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) مرض, (ما) a particle of negation, (إلّا) of restriction, (غرورا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its governor being وعدنا [Note: it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its kind, i.e.: except a promise of delusion, and the second object is implied, i.e. victory ...].
The clause «يقول المنافقون....» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ما وعدنا الله ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
(13) (إذ) conjoined to the preceding إذ, (منهم) attached to a naʿt of طائفة, (لكم) attached to the khabar of the lā of generic negation, (الفاء) conjunction, to link the effect to the cause, (الواو) resumptive, (منهم) a naʿt of فريق, (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya), (ما) negative, operating like ليس, (هي) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as the noun of ما, (عورة) genitive (majrūr) in its outward form, accusative (manṣūb) in position, the khabar of ما, (إن) a particle of negation, (إلّا) of restriction..
The clause «قالت طائفة ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The vocative clause and its response ... are in the position of an accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «لا مقام لكم ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «ارجعوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا مقام لكم [Note: the causal link between the declarative clause and the performative (inshāʾ) clause permits conjoining them.].
The clause «يستأذن فريق ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive..
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of فريق.
The clause «إنّ بيوتنا عورة..» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «ما هي بعورة..» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl [Note: or it is conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.].
The clause «إن يريدون إلّا فرارا» has no grammatical position: parenthetical — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —. [Translator's note: the source has no number marker here; what follows is the i'rab of verse (14).] (الواو) conjunction, (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb دخلت is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هي, i.e. the city, (عليهم) attached to (دخلت), (من أقطارها) attached to (دخلت), and (الواو) in (سئلوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil, (الفتنة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (اللام) linking the apodosis of لو, (ما) negative, (بها) attached to (تلبّثوا), (إلّا) of restriction, (يسيرا) an adverb, accusative, attached to (تلبّثوا) — it is an adjective standing in for an omitted qualified noun —, i.e. a short time.
The clause «لو دخلت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يستأذن.
The clause «سئلوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause دخلت.
The clause «آتوها ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition for the two verbs [Note: i.e.: they would have handed over the city and committed the fitna.].
The clause «ما تلبّثوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
(15) (الواو) conjunction, (اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath, (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), (قبل) a noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of a genitive by من, attached to (عاهدوا), (لا) negative, (الأدبار) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: and the first object is implied, i.e.: they would turn their backs to the enemy.], (الواو) resumptive ...
The clause «كانوا عاهدوا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath..

The clause «عاهدوا ...» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
The clause «لا يولّون ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the oath, for the verb عاهدوا ...
The clause «كان عهد الله مسئولا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(10) الحناجر: plural of حنجرة — the end of the throat —, a non-derived (jāmid) noun; its pattern is فعللة with fatḥa on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn. (10) (الظنونا): plural of الظنّ, an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral ظنّ, of the pattern نصر (category naṣara); its pattern is فعول with two ḍammas; the alif was kept after the nūn in the script of the Muṣḥaf in consideration of the joined reading (waṣl).
(11) (زلزالا): an analogical (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral زلزل; the maṣdar came in this form — other than the form زلزلة — because the verb is of the doubled quadriliteral; its pattern is فعلال with kasra then sukūn.
(13) يثرب: a name of Medina the Illumined; its pattern is يفعل with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn; it is denied tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine, or [because of] the verbal pattern.
(14) أقطار: plural of قطر, a noun meaning region and land; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn, and the plural is أفعال.

* Benefits:
The Battle of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb) (the Trench, al-Khandaq):
The leaders of Banū al-Naḍīr found no rest after their expulsion from their homes and the Muslims' inheriting them; rather it was always in their souls to take their revenge and recover their land. So a group of them went to Mecca, met the chiefs of Quraysh, incited them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and promised them help; they found acceptance from them for what they sought. Then they came to the tribe of Ghaṭafān and incited its men likewise, and told them of Quraysh's pledge to them for war, and they found them well-disposed. So Quraysh and their followers equipped themselves, led by Abū Sufyān, with their banner carried by ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa ibn Abī Ṭalḥa al-ʿAbdarī; they numbered four thousand, with three hundred horses and a thousand camels. Ghaṭafān equipped themselves, led by ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, who had a thousand horsemen with him; Banū Murra equipped themselves, led by al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf, with four hundred; Banū Ashjaʿ equipped themselves, led by Abū Masʿūd ibn Rukhayla; Banū Sulaym equipped themselves, led by Sufyān ibn ʿAbd Shams, and they were seven hundred; and Banū Asad equipped themselves, led by Ṭulayḥa ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadī. The number of them all was ten thousand fighters, their general commander being Abū Sufyān. When the news of these preparations reached him, upon him be blessing and peace, he consulted his Companions about what to do. Salmān al-Fārisī, may Allah be pleased with him, advised him to make the trench, which was a work the Arabs did not know. So he, upon him be blessing and peace, ordered the Muslims to make it, and they began digging it north of Medina, from the eastern lava field (ḥarra) to the western lava field; as for the rest of Medina's borders, they were interlocked with houses and palm trees, and the enemy could not fight from that direction. The Muslims endured grave difficulties in digging the trench, and he, upon him be blessing and peace, worked with them, carrying the earth while reciting the poetry of Ibn Rawāḥa:
اللهم لولا أنت ما اهتدينا ... ولا تصدقنا ولا صلّينا
(O Allah, were it not for You we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed.)

فأنزلن سكينة علينا ... وثبت الأقدام إن لاقينا
(So send down tranquillity upon us, and make firm our feet if we meet [the enemy].)

والمشركون قد بغوا علينا ... وإن أرادوا فتنة أبينا
(The idolaters have transgressed against us; and if they want fitna, we refuse.)
The army camped on the eastern side, with its back against Salʿ, a mountain overlooking Medina; they numbered three thousand. The banner of the Muhājirūn was with Zayd ibn Ḥāritha and the banner of the Anṣār with Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda. As for Quraysh, they camped at Mujammaʿ al-Asyāl, and Ghaṭafān camped in the direction of Uḥud. The idolaters were amazed at the stratagem of the trench, which the Arabs had not known, so they began exchanging arrows with the Muslims. When the waiting grew long for them, a group of them forced their horses to storm the trench, among them ʿIkrima ibn Abī Jahl, ʿUmar ibn Wadd [Translator's note: so in the source here (عمر بن ودّ); a few words later it has عمرو بن ود, ʿAmr ibn Wadd.] and others. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, came out against ʿAmr ibn Wadd and killed him, and his companions fled. The skirmishing and the exchange of arrows continued a whole day, until the Muslims missed the prayer of that day and made it up afterwards. The Prophet ﷺ placed guards over the trench so that the idolaters would not storm it at night, and he himself guarded a breach in it despite the intense cold. The Prophet ﷺ gave his Companions glad tidings of victory and triumph. As for the hypocrites, in this hardship they showed what their hearts concealed, until they said: (ما وَعَدَنَا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إِلَّا غُرُوراً), and withdrew, saying: (إن بيوتنا عورة) — we fear the enemy will raid them — (وما هي بعورة إن يريدون إلا فرارا). The siege grew long and the trial grew severe on the Muslims, and Banū Qurayẓa broke the covenant and declared war on the Muslims. When that reached the Prophet ﷺ, he sent Maslama ibn Aslam with two hundred, and Zayd ibn Ḥāritha with three hundred, to guard Medina, fearing for the women and children. He sent al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām to find out the news for him; when he reached them he found them furious, with evil showing on their faces, and they reviled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims in front of him. So he returned and told the Messenger ﷺ of that. Thereupon the fear of the Muslims intensified, and they were shaken with a severe shaking, because the enemy came at them from above them and from below them, eyes swerved, hearts reached the throats, and they thought various thoughts about Allah, and the hypocrites spoke whatever occurred to them. He, upon him be blessing and peace, wanted to send to ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and make peace with him on a third of the fruits of Medina, so that he would withdraw with Ghaṭafān.
But the Anṣār refused that, saying: they never used to get any of its fruits while we were disbelievers; shall they share them with us after Islam?
When Allah wills a matter, He prepares its means. While they were in this state of distress and hardship, Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd al-Ashjaʿī came — he was a friend of Quraysh and of the Jews — and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have become Muslim and my people do not know of my Islam, so command me as you wish so that I may help you. He went out from him and headed to Banū Qurayẓa, and said: O Banū Qurayẓa, you know my affection for you and my fear for you, and I am telling you something, so keep it secret from me [i.e. do not reveal that it came from me]. They said: yes. He said: you have seen what befell your brothers of Banū Qaynuqāʿ and al-Naḍīr. Quraysh and Ghaṭafān are not like you: if they triumph they profit, and if they are defeated they return to their lands. So I think you should not fight with them until you take seventy of their nobles from them as hostages, so that they do not abandon you and depart from you. They approved of his opinion and agreed to it. Then he rose from them and headed to Quraysh, met their chiefs and said: I am telling you something, so keep it secret from me. They said: we will. He said to them: Banū Qurayẓa have regretted what they did with Muḥammad, and they fear that you will go back and leave them with him; so they said to him: would it please you if we took a group of their nobles and restored our wing that you broke (meaning Banū al-Naḍīr)? And he accepted that from them, and here they are sending to you, so beware of them. Then he came to Ghaṭafān and told them the like of that. Abū Sufyān sent a delegation to Qurayẓa calling them to fight the next day, and they answered: we cannot fight on the Sabbath, and what befell us befell us only from transgressing on it; and even so we will not fight until you give us hostages from among you, so that you do not abandon us and go to your lands. So Quraysh and Ghaṭafān were convinced of the truth of Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd's words; hearts became divided and they feared one another. He, upon him be blessing and peace, had implored Allah, Mighty and Majestic, besides Whom there is no refuge, and called upon Him saying: (O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning, defeat the Confederates; O Allah, defeat them and grant us victory over them). Allah answered his supplication, upon him be blessing and peace, and sent upon the enemies a cold wind on a dark night. The idolaters feared that the Jews would come to terms with the Muslims and attack them, so they resolved upon departing before morning came. With the break of dawn the land was empty of them, and Allah spared the believers the fighting.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(فررتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), (من الموت) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فررتم), (الواو) conjunction, (إذا) with tanwīn: a particle of response, (لا) negative, and (الواو) in (تمتّعون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), (إلّا) of restriction, (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) [Note: or a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for an adverb, i.e. a short time.] standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), since it is its adjective, i.e.: a little enjoyment.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لن ينفعكم الفرار ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إن فررتم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «لا تمتّعون إلّا قليلا..» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if it benefited you outwardly, you would not be given enjoyment....

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being (ذا), (الذي) a relative noun, a badal (substitute) of ذا, in the position of a nominative, (من الله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعصمكم), (إن أراد) like إن فررتم [Note: in the preceding verse (16).], (بكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (سوءا), (أو) a conjunction, (أراد بكم رحمة) like أراد بكم سوءا, (الواو) conjunction, (لا) negative, (لهم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being يجدون, (من دون) attached to a ḥāl of (وليّا), (الواو) conjunction, (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من ذا الذي ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يعصمكم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أراد (the first)» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «أراد (the second)..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أراد (the first).
The clause «لا يجدون..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e.: they will be punished and will not find ...

safi-cedvel:18-20.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) [Note: because Allah's knowledge is realised at every time.], (منكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of المعوّقين, (لإخوانهم) attached to القائلين, (هلّمّ) a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of command meaning "come", and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنتم, (إلينا) attached to (هلّم), (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya), (لا) negative, (إلّا) of restriction, (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), since it is its adjective, (أشحّة) a ḥāl, accusative, of the fāʿil of يأتون, (عليكم) attached to أشحّة..
The clause «يعلم الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هلمّ ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), its governor being القائلين.
The clause «لا يأتون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.
(الفاء) conjunction, (إليك) attached to (ينظرون), (كالذي) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq whose governor is ينظرون or تدور, and it is with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. like the looking of the one who, or like the rolling of the eye of the one who.. (عليه) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb يغشى, (من الموت) attached to (يغشى), and من is causal, (الفاء) conjunction, (بألسنة) attached to (سلقوكم), (أشحّة) a ḥāl, accusative, of the fāʿil of سلقوكم, (على الخير) attached to أشحّة, (الفاء) conjunction, (على الله) attached to the khabar (predicate) (يسيرا).
The clause «جاء الخوف ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «رأيتهم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ينظرون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (رأيتهم). The clause «تدور أعينهم ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of ينظرون.
The clause «يغشى عليه ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ذهب الخوف ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «سلقوكم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أولئك لم يؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لم يؤمنوا ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أولئك).
The clause «أحبط الله....» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لم يؤمنوا.
The clause «كان ذلك.... يسيرا» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
(20) (الواو) conjunction, (لو) a particle of wishing (tamannī), (في الأعراب) attached to (بادون), (عن أنبائكم) attached to (يسألون), (لو) the second is a non-jussive conditional particle, (فيكم) attached to the khabar of كانوا, (ما) negative, (إلّا) of restriction, (قليلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar [Note: or a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, attached to (قاتلوا).].
The clause «يحسبون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in أعمالهم [Note: or it has no grammatical position: resumptive.].
The clause «لم يذهبوا ...» is in the position of an accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The clause «إن يأت الأحزاب ...» is conjoined to the clause يحسبون.
The clause «يودّوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not joined with the fāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم بادون ...) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يودّوا..
The clause «يسألون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in (بادون) [Note: the clause may be a second khabar of the particle resembling the verb, إنّ.].
The clause «لو كانوا فيكم ...» is conjoined to the clause يحسبون.
The clause «ما قاتلوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(18) المعوّقين: plural of المعوّق, an active participle from the quadriliteral عوّق; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, meaning "those who hold back [others]".
(19) أشحّة: plural of شحيح, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral شحّ, of the pattern ضرب (category ḍaraba), meaning to be miserly; it may also come from the category of نصر and the category of فتح. This plural — its pattern is أفعلة — is not analogical, for the analogy of the adjective فعيل whose ʿayn and lām are identical is to be pluralised on أفعلاء, such as خليل and أخلّاء, and ظنين and أظنّاء; and أشحّاء has been heard.
(حداد): plural of حديد in the sense of "cutting"; its pattern is فعيل, an assimilated adjective from the triliteral حدّ السيف, of the pattern ضرب (category ḍaraba), i.e. he sharpened it and it became cutting; and the pattern of حداد is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.. and there is another plural, أحدّاء, on the measure أفعلاء.
(20) بادون: an active participle from the triliteral بدا; its pattern is فاعون; it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion in keeping with the plural, as is the case with the defective noun (ism manqūṣ); its origin is باديون; the ḍamma was heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and its vowel was transferred to the dāl — an iʿlāl by making quiescent —; two quiescent letters met, so the yāʾ was deleted.. and that is an iʿlāl by deletion.

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of the witty touch (al-tandīr): in His saying, the Exalted, «فَإِذا جاءَ الْخَوْفُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أَعْيُنُهُمْ كَالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ». It is an art alluded to by the author of Nihāyat al-Arab and by Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ. Its definition: that the speaker brings a sweet rarity or a novel witticism; it occurs in earnest and in jest, so it does not fall within the scope of sarcasm, nor within the scope of the art of jest by which earnest is meant, and it may fall within the scope of the chapter of hyperbole (mubālagha). That is clear in His, the Exalted's, hyperbole in describing the hypocrites with fear and cowardice, where He reported of them that their eyes roll while they are looking, like the state of one who faints from [the approach of] death.
2- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدادٍ».
Here the tongue is likened to the sword and the like, by way of implicit metaphor: the thing likened to was omitted, and one of its properties was borrowed, namely striking. This metaphor works on the interpretation of السلق as striking.

* Benefits:
- The maṣdar-forming (لو):
Among the uses of (لو) is that it comes as a maṣdar-forming particle like (أن), except that it does not make accusative. It occurs most often after ودّ or يودّ or what has their meaning, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ — يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ لَوْ تُسَوَّى بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ — يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ.
An example of its occurrence without the verb يود is the saying of Qutayla bint al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, after her father was killed on the day of Badr, addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
ما كان ضرّك لو مننت وربما ... منّ الفتى وهو المغيظ المحنق
(What harm would it have done you had you shown grace? Often a young man shows grace even when he is enraged and furious.)
A difficulty for them is its entering upon (أنّ), as in the verse we are dealing with, namely His saying, the Exalted, وَإِنْ يَأْتِ الْأَحْزابُ يَوَدُّوا لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ بادُونَ فِي الْأَعْرابِ. The answer is that لو has only entered upon an omitted verb implied after (لو), its implied form being (يودّوا لو ثبت أنهم بادون في الأعراب) (they would wish that it were established that they were in the desert among the Bedouins).

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath for an implied oath, (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان, (في رسول) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أسوة, (لمن) a badal (substitute) of (لكم) with repetition of the preposition, and the noun of كان is a pronoun هو, the linking pronoun, (كثيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun).
The clause «كان لكم ... أسوة» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath.
The clause «كان يرجو ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «يرجو ...» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كان.
The clause «ذكر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(أسوة): a noun meaning following an example; it is used in the verse in the place of the maṣdar, which is الائتساء; its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction, (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قالوا), (ما) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هذا, and the linking pronoun is omitted, (الواو) conjunction, (ما) negative, and the fāʿil (agent) of (زادهم) is a pronoun referring to the promise, (إلّا) a particle of restriction, (إيمانا) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being زادهم.
The clause «رأى المؤمنين ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هذا ما وعدنا الله....» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «صدق الله ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the speech reported [Note: or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with (قد) implied.].
The clause «وعدنا الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «ما زادهم إلّا إيمانا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis.

* Rhetoric:
The art of repeating the overt noun: in His saying, the Exalted, «وَصَدَقَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».
This repetition and use of the overt noun, despite the prior mention, is for magnification; and because had He repeated them as pronouns, He would have combined the name of Allah the Exalted and the name of His Messenger in a single word, saying «وصدقا» (and they both spoke the truth). The Prophet disliked that when he answered one of the preachers who spoke in his presence, when he said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them both (يعصهما) has gone astray." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What a bad preacher of the people you are! Say: and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger", intending the magnification of Allah the Exalted.

safi-cedvel:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(من المؤمنين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) (رجال), (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), (عليه) attached to (عاهدوا), (الفاء) conjunction, (منهم) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ من, (الواو) conjunction, (ما) negative, (تبديلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «من المؤمنين رجال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «صدقوا..» is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رجال.
The clause «عاهدوا..» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «منهم من قضى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قضى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative (من).
The clause «منهم من (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause منهم من (the first).
The clause «ينتظر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
