The clause «ما بدّلوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause منهم من (the second) [Note: or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of ينتظر.].
(24) (اللام) of causation, (يجزي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, (بصدقهم) attached to (يجزي), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يجزي) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (صدقوا) [Note: or attached to something implied and resumed, i.e.: what happened happened so that Allah may recompense the truthful ...].
(الواو) conjunction, (يعذّب) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يجزي), (شاء) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is هو, (أو) a conjunction, (يتوب) conjoined to (يعذّب), accusative, (عليهم) attached to (يتوب)..
The clause «يجزي الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يعذّب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يجزي.
The clause «إن شاء ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: if He wills to punish them, He punishes them by causing them to die in hypocrisy.
The clause «يتوب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يعذّب ...
The clause «إن الله كان....» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كان غفورا ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(نحبه): a noun meaning death; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- Among the uses of (من):
(من) comes as a qualified indefinite (nakira mawṣūfa), and for this reason ربّ entered upon it, in the saying of Suwayd ibn Abī Kāhil:
ربّ من أنضجت غيظا قلبه ... قد تمنّى لي موتا لم يطع
(Many a one whose heart I have made to seethe with rage has wished death for me, and was not obeyed.)
And it was qualified by an indefinite, as in their saying: (مررت بمن معجب لك) (I passed by someone who admires you). Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him, said: فكفى بنا فضلا على من غيرنا ... حبّ النبي محمد إيانا
(It suffices us as a merit over those other than us that the Prophet Muḥammad loves us.)
It is related with «غيرنا» in the nominative, so it is possible that (من) is in its [indefinite] state, and it is possible that it is relative. On both, the implied form is (على من هو غيرنا), and the clause is an adjective or a ṣila. And He, the Exalted, said: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ. A group asserted that it is qualified (mawṣūfa), which is far-fetched because of how rarely it is used so; and others that it is relative (mawṣūla). Al-Zamakhsharī said: if you take the «ال» in «الناس» as being for the known referent (ʿahd), then it is relative, as in His saying, the Exalted, وَمِنْهُمُ الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ النَّبِيَّ; or for the genus, then it is qualified, as in the verse we are dealing with: مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ رِجالٌ صَدَقُوا ما عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَضى نَحْبَهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْتَظِرُ وَما بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلًا

safi-cedvel:25-27.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (بغيظهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative, i.e. clothed in their rage, (القتال) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, (كان الله قويّا عزيزا) is like كان غفورا رحيما [Note: in the preceding verse (24)].
The clause «ردّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لم ينالوا ...» is in the position of an accusative as a second ḥāl of the relative.
The clause «كفى الله المؤمنين....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كان الله قويا ...» has no grammatical position: a parenthetical resumption.
(26) (الواو) conjunction, (من أهل) attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of ظاهروهم, (من صياصيهم) attached to (أنزل), (في قلوبهم) attached to (قذف), (فريقا) a fronted mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تقتلون ...
The clause «أنزل....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ظاهروهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «قذف....» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أنزل [Note: or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.].
The clause «تقتلون ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in قلوبهم..
The clause «تأسرون ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause تقتلون..
(27) (الواو) conjunction in the four places, while the fifth is resumptive, (أرضهم) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (على كلّ) attached to (قديرا).
The clause «أورثكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لم تطؤوها ...» is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (أرضا).
The clause «كان الله.. قديرا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(صياصيهم): plural of صيصية or صيصة, a noun for anything one fortifies oneself with, even the spur on a rooster's leg, or [the spine of] a fish, or the horn of a bull..
The pattern of صيصية is فعلية with kasra on the fāʾ and the lām and fatḥa on the light (unstressed) yāʾ; the pattern of صيصة is فعلة with kasra on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the lām; and the pattern of صياصي is فعالي with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
The art of correspondence (al-munāsaba): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَرَدَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِغَيْظِهِمْ» to the end of the verse.
This art is of two kinds: correspondence in meanings and correspondence in wordings, and what has come in this verse is of the first kind. For had the speech been limited to what is before the verse-ending (fāṣila), that would have made some of the weak imagine that this report agrees with the disbelievers' belief that the wind that occurred was the cause of their returning disappointed and of the believers being spared their fighting, and that the wind only occurred by chance, as it occurs in some of their battles and in their fighting one another, and they would think that it was not from Allah. So precaution (iḥtirās) was achieved by the coming of the verse-ending, in which He, Glorified is He, reported that He is Strong, Mighty, able by His strength over every inaccessible thing, and that His party is the victorious one, and that by His power He makes victory for the believers of many various kinds.

* Benefits:
- The expedition against Banū Qurayẓa:
When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, relieved His Prophet ﷺ and his Companions of the Confederates, he wanted to take off the garb of war, but it was revealed to him that he should settle his account with Banū Qurayẓa. So he said to his Companions: let none of you pray the ʿAṣr except at Banū Qurayẓa. They set out hurrying, and he, upon him be blessing and peace, followed them, his banner in the hand of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, and his deputy over Medina being ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm; the number of the Muslims was three thousand. A group of the Companions was overtaken by the ʿAṣr prayer on the way: some of them prayed it, taking the command as meaning haste, and others did not pray it until at Banū Qurayẓa, after its time had passed, taking the command literally; and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not reproach any of them. When the army of the Muslims appeared before Banū Qurayẓa, Allah cast terror into their hearts, and the Muslims besieged them for twenty-five nights. When they despaired, they asked the Muslims to let them surrender on the terms on which Banū al-Naḍīr had surrendered: exile with their wealth and abandoning their weapons. The Messenger ﷺ did not accept that from them, so they asked for safety for their lives, and he did not agree to that either; rather he said: they must surrender and accept whatever is decided about them, good or bad. When they found no escape from accepting the judgement, he, upon him be blessing and peace, said to them: will you accept the judgement of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh?
They said: yes. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him, and he was carried, because he had been wounded in his akḥal — the artery of the forearm — on the day of the Trench. When he approached the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ said: stand up for your chief and help him down; and they did. The Messenger ﷺ said to him: judge among them, O Saʿd! Saʿd — may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him — turned towards the side where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not, and said: upon you is the covenant of Allah and His pledge that the judgement shall be as I judge? They said: yes. Then he turned towards the side where the Messenger ﷺ was and said: and upon whoever is here likewise? — lowering his gaze in reverence for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They said:
yes. He said: then I judge that you kill the men and take the women and children captive. He, upon him be blessing and peace, said: you have judged among them with the judgement of Allah from above seven heavens. He ﷺ gathered the spoils, and they were divided into fifths together with the palm trees, after the judgement had been carried out on them, and their necks were struck in one of the trenches of Medina; they were between seven hundred and nine hundred.

safi-cedvel:28-29.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أيّها) its i'rab has preceded [Note: in verse (9) of this sūra.], (النبيّ) a badal (substitute) of أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in outward form, (لأزواجك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قل), (كنتنّ) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) is the noun of كان, and (النون) is a particle for the feminine plural, (تردن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a nominative, and (النون) is a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent), (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (تعالين) an inflexible (jāmid) imperative verb [Note: it has no past and no imperfect.], indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (النون) is the fāʿil, (أمتعكّن) an imperfect verb, jussive as the response to the request.. كنّ is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and likewise (أسرّحكنّ), (سراحا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «إن كنتنّ ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تردن الحياة ...» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتنّ.
The clause «تعالين ...» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أمتعكنّ ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, so it has no grammatical position [Note: i.e.: if you come, I will provide for you.].
The clause «أسرحكنّ..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أمتعكنّ.
(29) (الواو) conjunction, (إن كنتن تردن الله) is like إن كنتن تردن الحياة, (الفاء) linking the apodosis, (للمحسنات) attached to (أعدّ), (منكنّ) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of المحسنات..
The clause «إن كنتنّ تردن..» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause كنتنّ (the first).
The clause «تردن الله ...» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كنتنّ.
The clause «إنّ الله أعد» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أعدّ للمحسنات ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(سراحا): the noun from the quadriliteral (سرّح) meaning divorce, or it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
- The occasion of the verses and their ruling:
From Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: Abū Bakr came seeking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found people sitting at his door, none of whom had been given permission. Permission was given to Abū Bakr and he entered. Then ʿUmar came and sought permission, and it was given to him, and he found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting, surrounded by his wives, gloomy and silent. He said:
I will say something to make the Prophet ﷺ laugh. So I said: O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Khārija:
[i.e. his wife] she asked me for maintenance, so I got up to her and struck her on the neck. The Prophet ﷺ laughed and said: they are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance. So Abū Bakr got up to ʿĀʾisha and struck her on the neck, and ʿUmar got up to Ḥafṣa and struck her on the neck, both saying: do you ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what he does not have? They said: by Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything he does not have. Then he kept away from them for a month, or twenty-nine [days], until this verse was revealed. He began with ʿĀʾisha and said: O ʿĀʾisha, I want to put a matter before you, and I would like you not to hasten in it until you consult your parents.
She said: and what is it, O Messenger of Allah? He recited the verse to her, and she said: is it about you, O Messenger of Allah, that I should consult my parents? Rather I choose Allah, His Messenger and the abode of the Hereafter; and I ask you not to tell any woman among your wives what I have said. He said: no woman among them will ask me without my telling her; Allah did not send me to be harsh or to cause hardship, but He sent me as a teacher, a bringer of glad tidings.
The ruling of the verse:
The scholars differed about the ruling of this choice: was it a delegation of divorce to them, so that it would take effect by the choosing itself, or not? Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and most of the people of knowledge held that it was not a delegation of divorce; rather he gave them the choice on the basis that if they chose the world he would part from them, because of His saying, the Exalted:
فَتَعالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحْكُنَّ; as evidenced by the fact that their answer was not immediate, and that he said to ʿĀʾisha:
do not hasten until you consult your parents; whereas in the delegation of divorce the answer is immediate.
As for the ruling of giving the choice (takhyīr), ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās said: if a man gives his wife the choice and she chooses her husband, nothing takes effect; and if she chooses herself, one divorce takes effect. This is what most of the scholars hold.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), (منكنّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يأت, (بفاحشة) attached to (يأت), (لها) attached to (يضاعف), (العذاب) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), (ضعفين) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, (الواو) conjunction, (على الله) attached to (يسيرا).
The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من يأت ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «يأت....» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «يضاعف لها العذاب ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كان ذلك ... يسيرا..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (من) a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), (منكنّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يقنت, (لله) attached to the verb يقنت, (نؤتها) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (مرّتين) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), since it is its number, (الواو) conjunction, (لها) attached to (أعتدنا)..
The clause «من يقنت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يقنت منكنّ ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «تعمل ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يقنت.
The clause «نؤتها ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أعتدنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.

safi-cedvel:32-34.t:
* I'rab:
(نساء) the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb), (كأحد) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of ليس, (من النساء) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of أحد, (اتقيتنّ) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (لا) prohibitive, making jussive, (تخضعن) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive, (بالقول) attached to (تخضعن) by its being made to contain (taḍmīn) the meaning of تغتررن, (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), (يطمع) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, (في قلبه) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) مرض, (قولا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, with the direct object implied.].
The clause «يا نساء ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لستنّ ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «إن اتقيتنّ ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لا تخضعن ...» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يطمع الذي ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يطمع) is in the position of a nominative, conjoined by the fāʾ to a maṣdar taken from the preceding prohibition, i.e.: let there be no softness from you, and [thereby] desire from the one in whose heart is a sickness.
The clause «في قلبه مرض ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «قلن ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخضعن.
(33) (الواو) conjunction, (قرن) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and the nūn is the fāʿil (agent), (في بيوتكنّ) attached to (قرن), (لا تبرجن) like لا تخضعن, (تبرّج) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative, (إنّما) a restraining particle (kāffa) and a restrained one (makfūfa), and (اللام) is redundant (zāʾida), (يذهب) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, (عنكم) attached to (يذهب), (أهل) the one addressed, annexed, accusative, (تطهيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذهب) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يريد.
The clause «قرن ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخضعن.
The clause «لا تبرّجن ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخضعن.
The clause «أقمن ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخضعن.
The clause «آتين ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تخضعن.
The clause «أطعن ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to لا تخضعن or أقمن.
The clause «إنّما يريد الله ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يذهب ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يطهّركم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يذهب.
(34) -: (الواو) conjunction, (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (يتلى) is a pronoun هو, the linking pronoun, (في بيوتكنّ) attached to (يتلى), (من آيات) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil, (خبيرا) a second khabar of the defective (nāqiṣ) verb.
The clause «اذكرن ...» is in the position of a jussive, conjoined to the clause أطعن.
The clause «يتلى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله كان ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption — or causal (taʿlīliyya) —.
The clause «كان لطيفا ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(32) لستنّ: it contains an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) like the iʿlāl in لستم ... (see verse 267 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(33) قرن: one of the two rāʾs was deleted in it for lightening; its proper form would be (اقررن), i.e. stay firm; its past is قرّ and its imperfect يقرّ — with fatḥa on the qāf — it was said it is of the category of فرح and it was said of the category of فتح ... When the imperative was built on the sukūn because of its being joined to the nūn of the feminine plural, two quiescent letters met, namely the doubled rāʾ; so the first was deleted for lightening and its original vowel, the fatḥa, was transferred to the qāf; then the hamzat al-waṣl was deleted because the qāf had become vowelled, so it became قرن; its pattern is فلن.
(تبرجن): one of the two tāʾs was deleted from it for lightening; its origin is تتبرجن; its pattern is تفعلن.
(تبرّج): an analogical (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the five-letter verb تبرّج; its pattern is تفعّل, on the pattern of the past with ḍamma on the letter before the last.
(تطهيرا): an analogical maṣdar of the quadriliteral طهّر; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
The reversed simile (al-tashbīh al-maqlūb): in His saying, the Exalted, «يا نِساءَ النَّبِيِّ لَسْتُنَّ كَأَحَدٍ مِنَ النِّساءِ».
The simile is reversed; the original is: no one among women is like you. But if the meaning is: you are not like any of the women in lowliness (al-nuzūl), then there is no reversal in the simile.

* Benefits:
- The former Jāhiliyya (al-jāhiliyya al-ūlā):
It was said: the former Jāhiliyya is what was between Jesus and Muḥammad, upon them both be blessing and peace. It was said: it was the time of David and Solomon, upon them both be blessing and peace, when a woman would wear a shift of pearls not sewn at the sides, so that her back could be seen through it. It was said: it was in the time of Nimrod the tyrant, when a woman would take a garment of pearls, put it on and walk in the middle of the road with nothing else on her, offering herself to men. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the former Jāhiliyya is what was between Noah and Idrīs, and it was a thousand years. It was said: the former Jāhiliyya is what was before Islam, and the other Jāhiliyya: a people who will do the like of their doings at the end of time.

safi-cedvel:35-36.t:
* I'rab:
(فروجهم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle الحافظين, and the object of الحافظات is omitted, (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi of الذاكرين, (كثيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), since it is its adjective; the object of الذاكرات was omitted because the first indicates it, (لهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعدّ), and the pronoun in it is masculine by way of predominance (taghlīb).
The clause «إنّ المسلمين ... أعدّ الله لهم..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أعدّ الله لهم ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
36- (الواو) conjunction, (ما) negative, (لمؤمن) attached to an omitted khabar of كان, (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation, (مؤمنة) conjoined to مؤمن by the wāw, genitive (majrūr), (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, (لهم) attached to the khabar of يكون, (من أمرهم) attached to الخيرة [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الخيرة.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون..) is in the position of a nominative as the postponed noun of كان.
(الواو) conjunction, (من) a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), (ضلالا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «ما كان ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قضى الله ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «يكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «من يعص ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ما كان.
The clause «يعص ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «قد ضلّ ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الصائمين): plural of الصائم, an active participle from the triliteral صام; its pattern is فاعل; it contains the change of the weak letter into a hamza after the alif of فاعل.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive, (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر, (للذي) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقول), (عليه) attached to (أنعم), and the second is attached to (أنعت) [Translator's note: so in the source (أنعت); the Quranic verb is أنعمت.], (عليك) attached to (أمسك) [Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of زوجك.], (في نفسك) attached to (تخفي), (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, (والله) the wāw is circumstantial, (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle..
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تخشاه) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (أحقّ), i.e. more deserving of being feared [Note: it may be in the position of a nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is (أحقّ), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله), i.e. Allah — fearing Him is more rightful than fearing anyone else.].
(الفاء) conjunction, (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (زوّجناكها), and it is in the position of an accusative, (منها) attached to (قضى), (كي) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle, (لا) negative, (على المؤمنين) attached to the khabar of يكون, (حرج) the noun of يكون, (في أزواج) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of حرج, (منهنّ) attached to (قضوا), (الواو) resumptive ...
The clause «(اذكر) إذ تقول ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تقول ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «أنعم الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أنعمت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أمسك ...» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اتّق الله ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «تخفي ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تقول.
The clause «الله مبديه» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «تخشى ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تخفي.
The clause «الله أحقّ ...» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تخشاه» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «قضى زيد ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «زوّجناكها ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لا يكون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (كي).
The clause «قضوا ...» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «كان أمر الله مفعولا» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مبديه): an active participle from the quadriliteral أبدى; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma [on the mīm] and kasra on the ʿayn.
(زيد): a masculine proper name; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn; it is originally the maṣdar of the triliteral زاد.
(وطرا): a noun meaning need; there is no verb in use from this root; the plural is أوطار on the measure أفعال, and the pattern of وطر is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Benefits:
- Abolishing the custom of adoption:
It is well known
that the Prophet ﷺ had married his freedman (mawlā) Zayd ibn Ḥāritha to Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and her family were displeased at that because of her standing in nobility, for the Arabs disliked marrying their daughters to freedmen. When His saying, the Exalted, in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb was revealed: وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْراً أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا مُبِيناً, her family saw no option but to accept her marriage to Zayd. When Zayd went in to her, she held herself above him because of her nobility and lineage, and he could not bear that, so he complained of her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who ordered him to bear with her and be patient with her, until he could bear it no longer and decided to divorce her. After the end of her waiting period (ʿidda), Allah ordered His Prophet ﷺ to marry Zaynab, to settle this discord and to preserve her honour. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ feared the blame of the Jews and the Arabs for marrying the wife of his adopted son, so he said to Zayd: keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah, and he concealed within himself what Allah was to reveal.
So Allah settled His ruling by abolishing this rule, namely the prohibition of [marrying] the wife of an adopted son, with His saying in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: فَلَمَّا قَضى زَيْدٌ مِنْها وَطَراً زَوَّجْناكَها لِكَيْ لا يَكُونَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ فِي أَزْواجِ أَدْعِيائِهِمْ إِذا قَضَوْا مِنْهُنَّ وَطَراً وَكانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا
. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade adoption to the Muslims, because of the harms in it, and revealed concerning it in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: ما كانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجالِكُمْ وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً. From that time Zayd's name became (Zayd ibn Ḥāritha) instead of (Zayd ibn Muḥammad). The doubters have tried to spit their poison around this story, saying: the Messenger ﷺ went one day to visit Zayd, and his eye fell on Zaynab and she fell into his heart, and he said: Glory be to Allah; when her husband came she mentioned that to him, and he saw it as his duty to part from her, so he went and told the Prophet ﷺ of that, and he forbade him from it. The falsehood of that appears from the fact that the Prophet ﷺ had known Zaynab since the days of Mecca, where she became Muslim — she was his paternal aunt's daughter — and he was the one who married her to Zayd; had he had any desire for her, he would have married her himself from the beginning. In any case, the true believer believes in the infallibility (ʿiṣma) of our master Muḥammad ﷺ, the purity of his character and the cleanness of his heart, and does not doubt that by a hair's breadth. As for the doubters, they give no weight to the prophets and observe no sanctity for religions; therefore they fabricate lies and interpret appearances according to their sick souls, and they are too contemptible to be paid attention to or answered.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative particle. (من رجالكم) attached (mutaʿalliq) to an adjective (naʿt) of أحد. (الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no grammatical effect. (رسول) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (أبا), accusative like it [Note: it is permissible that it be the predicate of an implied kāna together with its subject, the clause being conjoined to the resumptive clause ما كان محمد ...]. (خاتم) conjoined to رسول by the wāw, accusative. (بكلّ) attached to (عليما), the predicate (khabar) of كان.
The clause «ما كان محمّد أبا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان الله ... عليما» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما كان محمد.

* Morphology:
(خاتم): a rigid, non-derived noun denoting a thing; the instrument with which a document is sealed. It is used here by way of comparison. Its pattern (wazn) is فاعل, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
The device of "talfīf" (wrapping up): in the words of the Exalted «ما كانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجالِكُمْ», the verse.
In Muḥīṭ al-Muḥīṭ: talfīf among the masters of eloquence is proportionality (tanāsub). It consists in bringing out the speech as the teaching of a ruling or a point of etiquette which the speaker did not intend to mention; rather he intended to mention a ruling that falls within the generality of what is mentioned, whose teaching he stated explicitly. More clearly: it is a general answer concerning one kind among the kinds of a genus, all of which need to be explained, so the answerer turns away from the specific answer to what was asked, namely the clarification of that kind, to a general answer that includes the clarification of the ruling asked about and of other matters that need to be explained.
So his saying «ما كانَ مُحَمَّدٌ» is the answer to an implied question, namely someone's saying: Is Muḥammad not the father of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha? The answer came saying: Muḥammad was not the father of any of your men. The requirement of the answer was to say: Muḥammad was not the father of Zayd, and that alone would have sufficed. But it turned away from that to prepare the announcement that Muḥammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, and this preparation is complete only by denying his fatherhood of any man, for he can be the Seal of the Prophets only on the condition that he have no son who has reached maturity. So it is no objection that he had al-Ṭāhir, al-Ṭayyib and al-Qāsim, since they did not reach the age of men. Then it took further precaution for that with the words مِنْ رِجالِكُمْ, attaching the men to them and not to him. The specific meaning was thus wrapped up within the general meaning, and it yielded the denial of universal fatherhood of any of their men, and within that was folded the denial of fatherhood of Zayd. Then there is another wrapping up, namely his saying «وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ»: it turned from the word "nabī" (prophet) to the word "rasūl" (messenger) for additional praise, since every messenger is a prophet but not vice versa, according to one of the two views. So this is a wrapping up after a wrapping up.

* Benefits:
- Some rulings on لكن:
It is known that the lightened (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), and sometimes it comes as a conjunction. The grammarians differed about such a sentence as (ما قام زيد ولكن عمرو) in four views:
1- What Yūnus said: that لكن is not a conjunction, and the wāw is a conjunction joining a single word to a single word.
2- What Ibn Mālik said: that (لكن) is not a conjunction, and the wāw is a conjunction joining a clause partly omitted to a clause stated in full. He said: so the implied form in (ما قام زيد ولكن عمرو) is "ولكن قام عمرو", and in (وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ) it is "ولكن كان رسول الله". The reason is that the wāw does not join a single word to a single word that differs from it in affirmation and negation, unlike two conjoined clauses, in which a difference between them in that is permissible, as in: قام زيد ولم يقم عمرو.
3- Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: that (لكن) is a conjunction, and the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) and obligatory.
4- Ibn Kaysān said: that (لكن) is a conjunction, and the wāw is redundant and not obligatory.

safi-cedvel:41-44.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) a vocative, an indefinite noun that is specified (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative. (الذين) a substitute (badal) for أيّ, in the position of the accusative. (ذكرا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative.
The clause «يأيّها الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اذكروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
(42) (بكرة) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (سبّحوه).
The clause «سبّحوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اذكروا.
(43) (عليكم) attached to (يصلّي). (ملائكته) conjoined to the latent pronoun that is the agent (fāʿil) of يصلّي, nominative; it was not reinforced with a detached pronoun because of the separator (عليكم). (اللام) for purpose. (يخرجكم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām. (من الظلمات) attached to (يخرجكم), and likewise (إلى النور).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يخرجكم) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يصلّي).
(بالمؤمنين) attached to the predicate of كان, (رحيما).
The clause «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption - or a causal clause.
The clause «يصلّي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «يخرجكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle (أن) with its maṣdar.
The clause «كان ... رحيما» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يصلّي.
(44) (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to تحيّتهم. (سلام) a second mubtadaʾ (subject), its predicate omitted, its implied form being "عليكم" [Note: or it is the predicate of the mubtadaʾ تحيّتهم]. (الواو) conjunction. (لهم) attached to (أعدّ).
The clause «تحيّتهم ... سلام (عليكم)» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «سلام (عليكم)» is in the position of the nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (تحيّتهم).
The clause «أعد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تحيّتهم.

* Rhetoric:
1- Specification (takhṣīṣ): in the words of the Exalted «بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا».
Their being singled out for mention is not to restrict glorification to them to the exclusion of all other times, but to show their merit over the other times, because the angels of the night and of the day attend them and meet in them; likewise glorification is singled out from among the remembrances, though it is included in them, because it is the mainstay among them.
2- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in the words of the Exalted «هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلائِكَتُهُ».
Since it is characteristic of the one who prays (muṣallī) to bend in his bowing and prostration, the word was borrowed for one who bends toward another out of tenderness and compassion for him, like one visiting the sick in his bending over him, and the woman in her tenderness toward her child. Then it became frequent until it was used for mercy and compassion. From it comes their saying: ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayka, that is, may He have mercy on you and be compassionate toward you.

safi-cedvel:45-48.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها النبيّ) like يأيّها الذين [Note: in verse (41) of this sura.]. (شاهدا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the pronoun of address. (إلى الله) attached to (داعيا). (بإذنه) a ḥāl from the pronoun in (داعيا). (سراجا) conjoined to (شاهدا), so it is a ḥāl in meaning [Note: it is permissible for it to be so although it is a rigid noun because it has been qualified.]. (لهم) attached to the predicate of أنّ. (من الله) attached to a ḥāl from (فضلا), the subject of أنّ (ism anna). (الواو) conjunction. (لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle. (تطع) an imperfect verb, jussive, and it was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (على الله) attached to (توكّل). (كفى بالله وكيلا) like كفى بالله حسيبا [Note: in verse (39) of this sura.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم ... فضلا) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (بشّر).
The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّا أرسلناك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «أرسلناك ... » is in the position of the nominative, predicate of إنّ.
The clause «بشّر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, that is:
"observe the people and give glad tidings ...", the resumption being within the scope of the vocative.
The clause «لا تطع ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied resumption.
The clause «دع أذاهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied resumption.
The clause «توكّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied resumption.
The clause «كفى بالله وكيلا» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(دع): it has undergone weakening (iʿlāl) by elision because of the imperative; it is a wāw-initial verb (mithāl wāwī), its pattern (wazn) being عِل with kasra on the first letter and a quiescent second [Translator's note: the source text reads "بفتح فسكون" (with fatḥa then sukūn); translated as written].

safi-cedvel:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (41) of this sura.]. (من قبل) attached to (طلّقتموهنّ); the wāw in it is redundant, to lengthen the vowel of the mīm. (أن) a particle of maṣdar and accusative. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (ما) a negative particle, inoperative. (لكم) attached to an omitted word, the predicate of the mubtadaʾ عدّة, which is genitive in form and nominative in position. (عليهنّ) attached to the "being" (istiqrār) that is the predicate [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from عدة].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تمسّوهنّ) is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
(الفاء) the second, linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (سراحا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative.
The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «نكحتم ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «طلّقتموهنّ» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause نكحتم.
The clause «تمسّوهنّ» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle (أن) with its maṣdar.
The clause «ما لكم ... من عدّة» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تعتدّونها ... » is in the position of the genitive - or the nominative - an adjective (naʿt) of عدّة.
The clause «متّعوهنّ ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you have not set a dowry for them, then provide for them".
The clause «سرّحوهنّ» is conjoined to the clause متّعوهنّ.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metonymic synecdoche (majāz mursal): in the words of the Exalted «إِذا نَكَحْتُمُ الْمُؤْمِناتِ»:
Calling the contract "nikāḥ" is a majāz mursal whose relation is association (mulābasa), in that it is the way to it; its like is their calling wine "sin" (ithm), because it is a cause of committing sin.
2- Euphemism (kināya): in the words of the Exalted «تَمَسُّوهُنَّ».
Among the courtesies of the Qur'an is the euphemism for intercourse by the words: touching (mulāmasa), contact (mumāssa), approaching (qurbān), covering (taghashshī), and coming to (ityān).

* Benefits:
- No divorce and no waiting period before marriage:
The verse is evidence that divorce before marriage does not take effect, because Allah the Exalted made divorce consequent upon marriage, even if a man said to an unrelated woman: "If I marry you, you are divorced." This is the view of ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Ṭāwūs, Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda and most of the people of knowledge. Al-Shāfiʿī held, and it is reported from Ibn Masʿūd, that the divorce takes effect, and it is the view of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī and the people of personal opinion (aṣḥāb al-raʾy). The first view is the more preferable, because of the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās: Allah made divorce after marriage.
From another angle, the scholars agreed that if the divorce is before touching and seclusion there is no waiting period. Aḥmad held that seclusion makes the waiting period and the dowry obligatory.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها النبيّ) like يأيّها الذين [Note: in verse (41) of this sura.]. (لك) attached to (أحللنا). (اللاتي) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of أزواجك. (الواو) conjunction in all places. (ما) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, conjoined to أزواجك. (ممّا) attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun (ʿāʾid), that is: "what your right hand possesses (ملكتها)". (عليك) attached to (أفاء). The four words (بنات) are conjoined to أزواجك, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, for it is attached to the sound feminine plural. (اللاتي) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, an adjective (naʿt) of بنات. (معك) an adverb, accusative, attached to (هاجرن). (امرأة) conjoined to أزواجك, accusative. (وهبت) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (للنبيّ) attached to (وهبت). (أراد) like وهبت. (أن) a particle of maṣdar and accusative. (خالصة) a ḥāl, accusative [Note: it may be an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) standing in for the maṣdar, that is: "she gave herself as a pure gift".]. (لك) attached to خالصة. (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in خالصة ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستنكحها) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of which the governing word is أراد ...
(ما) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a direct object. (عليهم) attached to (فرضنا). (في أزواجهم) attached to (فرضنا). (ما) the second, a relative in the position of the genitive, conjoined to أزواجهم by the wāw. (اللام) a preposition. (كي) a particle of maṣdar and accusative. (لا) negative. (عليك) attached to the predicate of يكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (كي لا يكون ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أحللنا) [Note: or attached to خالصة because it contains the sense of making lawful and its coming about for him].
The vocative clause ... has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إنّا أحللنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «أحللنا ... » is in the position of the nominative, predicate of إنّ.
The clause «آتيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (اللاتي).
The clause «ملكت يمينك» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أفاء الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «هاجرن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (اللاتي).
The clause «وهبت ... » is in the position of the accusative, a second adjective (naʿt) of امرأة [Note: it may be a ḥāl from (امرأة) because it has been qualified.] .. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, that is: "then she is lawful for him".
The clause «أراد النبيّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical ... and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the preceding apodosis.
The clause «يستنكحها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle (أن) with its maṣdar.
The clause «علمنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
The clause «فرضنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative noun (ما).
The clause «ملكت أيمانهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (ما).
The clause «يكون عليك حرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle (كي) with its maṣdar.
The clause «كان الله غفورا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
The shift of person (iltifāt): in the words of the Exalted «نَفْسَها لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنْ أَرادَ النَّبِيُّ أَنْ يَسْتَنْكِحَها».
Here it turned from address to the third person, to signal that this is among the things he was singled out for and favoured with; its coming in the word "the Prophet" shows that the distinction is an honouring of him on account of prophethood; and its repetition is a magnification of him and an affirmation of his deserving honour because of his prophethood.

* Benefits:
- Marriage by gift (hiba):
This verse indicates that Allah the Mighty and Majestic made lawful for the Prophet ﷺ a believing woman who gave herself to him without a dowry; a non-believing woman, however, is not lawful for him in that. As for anyone other than the Prophet ﷺ among the rest of the Muslims, his marriage is not concluded with the word "gift"; rather the word "inkāḥ" or "tazwīj" is indispensable.
This is the view of most scholars, among them Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī. Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said: The Prophet ﷺ had no woman who gave herself to him, and he had no wife except by a marriage contract or by right of ownership, and the verse is by way of supposition and hypothesis. Others said: rather he did have a woman who gave herself to him. Al-Shaʿbī said: she is Zaynab bint Khuzayma. Qatāda said: she is Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith. ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil said she is: Umm Sharīk bint Jābir.
ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: she is: Khawla bint Ḥakīm.

safi-cedvel:51-51.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, a direct object. (منهنّ) attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun, that is: "whom you wish to postpone (irjāʾahu) of them". (إليك) attached to (تؤوي). (الواو) conjunction. (من) the third, in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the relative noun من تشاء [Note: it may be a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is the clause ابتغيت, or a fronted direct object whose governing word is ابتغيت, and the fāʾ is a linker]. (ممّن) attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun, that is: "whom you sought from among those you set aside". (الفاء) resumptive. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (عليك) attached to the predicate of لا. (ذلك) a mubtadaʾ, the pointing being to the giving of choice, and the predicate is أدنى. (أن) a particle of maṣdar and accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقرّ..) is in the position of the genitive by an implied (إلى), attached to أدنى, that is: "to their eyes being cooled".
(الواو) conjunction. (لا) negative. (يحزنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (تقرّ), and likewise (يرضين). (بما) attached to (يرضين). (كلّهنّ) tawkīd (emphasis) of the agent in (يرضين). (الواو) resumptive. (في قلوبكم) attached to an omitted word that is the ṣila of ما. (الواو) like the last one.
The clause «ترجي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (من).
The clause «تؤوي ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ترجي.
The clause «تشاء (the second) ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
The clause «ابتغيت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative noun (من).
The clause «عزلت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (من).
The clause «لا جناح عليك» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or it is the apodosis if (من) is made a conditional noun.. and it may be a predicate if (من) is made a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ, with the fāʾ redundant because of the resemblance of the relative to the condition.].
The clause «ذلك أدنى ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «تقرّ أعينهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle (أن).
The clause «لا يحزنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle with its maṣdar.
The clause «يرضين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle with its maṣdar.
The clause «آتيتهنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of the nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «كان الله عليما ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, containing the sense of giving a reason.

* Morphology:
(ترجي): lightened from ترجئ, meaning "you postpone".

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {بِغَيْظِهِمْ}: It is possible that the bāʾ is causal (sababiyya) — this is what Abū al-Baqāʾ expressed as "the object" (al-mafʿūl), meaning that it is a transitive-making bāʾ (muʿaddiya). The second possibility: that it is for accompaniment, in which case it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "enraged" (mughīẓīn).

His saying: {لَمْ يَنَالُواْ خَيْراً} is a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the first ḥāl, so that the two are nested (mutadākhila). It is also possible that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun that is genitive by iḍāfa. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be an explication (bayān) of the first ḥāl, or resumptive (mustaʾnafa). The explication is not evident except on the basis of badal (substitution), and the resumptive reading is remote.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {وَأَنزَلَ الذين}: that is, "and Allah sent down". And {مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب} is an explication (bayān) of the relative noun, and so is attached to an omitted element; it is also possible that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «مِنْ صَياصِيْهم» is attached to «أَنْزل», and «مِنْ» marks the starting point. The word «الصَّياصِي» is the plural of «صِيْصِيَة», meaning fortresses. Anything by which one defends oneself and fortifies oneself is called a «صِيْصِيَة»; from this the horn of the bull and the spur of the cock are called «صِيْصِيَة». «الصَّياصِي» also means the weaver's thorn (shawk al-ḥāka), which is made of iron. Duraid ibn al-Ṣimma said:

3690 - ... ... ... like the falling of the iron weaver's picks on stretched-out cloth (كوَقْعِ الصَّياصِيْ في النسيجِ المُمَدَّدِ)

His saying: «فريقاً تَقْتُلون»: «فريقاً» is accusative (manṣūb) by what follows it. Likewise the second «فريقاً» is accusative by what precedes it. The sentence explains and confirms Allah's casting terror into their hearts. The majority read both verbs in the second person. Ibn Dhakwān, in one transmission, read both in the third person. al-Yamānī read the first only in the third person. Abū Ḥaywa read «تَأْسرون» with ḍamma on the sīn.

His saying: «لم تَطؤُوْها»: the sentence is an adjective (ṣifa) of «أرضاً». The majority read it with a hamza carrying ḍamma, then a quiescent wāw, as the imperfect of waṭiʾa. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «تَطُوْها», with a wāw after a ṭāʾ carrying fatḥa. Its explanation is that he substituted an alif for the hamza, which is contrary to the regular rule, as in his saying:

3691 - Truly the lions are at ease in their lairs ... (إنَّ الأُسودَ لَتَهْدا في مَرابِضِها)

Then, when he attached it to the wāw, two quiescent letters met and the first of them was dropped, as in «لم يَرَوْها». This is better than saying that he then treated the alif substituted for the hamza as an original alif and dropped it for the jussive, because the better course there is not to drop it, out of regard for its origin. Some have cited as evidence for the dropping the saying of Zuhayr:

3692 - Bold: when he is wronged he punishes with his own wrong, swiftly; and if he is not begun upon with wrong, he does wrong (جَرِيْءٍ متى يُظْلَمْ يعاقِبْ بظلمِه ... سَريعاً وإن لا يُبْدَ بالظُّلمِ يَظْلِمِ)

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحْكُنَّ}: The majority read both as jussive (majzūm). There are two explanations. The first: that it is jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and what lies between the protasis and its apodosis is parenthetical (muʿtariḍ); the entry of the fāʾ upon a parenthetical sentence does no harm. Similar in the entry of the fāʾ is the poet's saying:

3693 - And know — for a man's knowledge benefits him — that everything that has been decreed will surely come (واعلَمْ فَعِلْمُ المَرْءِ يَنْفَعُه ... أَنْ سَوْفَ يَأْتيْ كلُّ ما قُدِرا)

He means: "and know that everything will surely come". The second: that the apodosis is «فَتَعالَيْنَ», and «وأُمَتِّعْكن» is the answer to this imperative.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «أُمْتِعْكُنَّ», with the tāʾ unshadded, from amtaʿahu. Ḥumayd al-Khazzāz read «أُمَتِّعُكُن وأُسَرِّحْكُن» in the nominative (marfūʿ) for both, as resumptive (istiʾnāf). And «سَراحاً» stands in the place of «التَّسْريح» (the verbal noun).

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ}: The majority read «يَأْتِ» with a yāʾ (with two dots below), construing it according to the form (lafẓ) of «مَنْ». Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Jaḥdarī and Yaʿqūb read it with a tāʾ (with two dots above), construing it according to its meaning, because the feminine sense is reinforced by the words «منكُنَّ»; and «منكنَّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَأْتِ». The reading of «مُبَينة» with respect to kasra or fatḥa of the yāʾ has already been given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

His saying: «يُضاعَفْ»: Abū ʿAmr read «يُضَعَّفْ» with a yāʾ (dots below) and a shadda on the ʿayn carrying fatḥa, in the passive; «العذابُ» is nominative because it stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil). Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «نُضَعِّفْ» with the nūn of majesty and a shadda on the ʿayn carrying kasra, in the active; his saying «العذابَ» is accusative as direct object (mafʿūl bihi). The rest read «يُضاعَفْ», from the form mufāʿala, in the passive; «العذابُ» is nominative because it stands in the place of the agent. The explanation of taḍʿīf and muḍāʿafa has already been given in Sūrat al-Baqara, which makes repeating it unnecessary.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {وَتَعْمَلْ صَالِحاً نُؤْتِهَآ}: The two (al-Akhawān, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «ويَعْمَلْ ويُؤْتِ» with a yāʾ (dots below) in both. The rest read «وتَعْمل» with a tāʾ (dots above) and «نُؤْتِها» with a nūn. As for the yāʾ in «ويَعْمَلْ», it is for construing according to the form of «مَنْ», which is the basic rule. The tāʾ is according to its meaning, since what is meant by it is feminine; this is reinforced by the preceding feminine word «مِنْكُنَّ». Similar is the saying:

3694 - And among women there is one who is a garden ... (وإنَّ مِن النِّسْوان مَنْ هي روضةٌ ...)

When "among women" came first, the sense was preferred, so he construed according to it. As for «يُؤْتِها» with a yāʾ (dots below), the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, because He was mentioned before in «لله ورسوله». With the nūn, it is the nūn of majesty, and there is in it a shift from the third person to the first.

al-Jaḥdarī, Yaʿqūb, Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «تَقْنُتْ» with a tāʾ (dots above), construing according to the meaning, and likewise «وتَعْمَل». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Some of them read «ومَنْ تَقْنُتْ» with the feminine, construing according to the meaning, and «يَعْمَلْ» with the masculine, construing according to the form." He said: "Some of the grammarians said: this is weak, because the masculine is the basic form, so it is not made to follow the feminine. But what they gave as their reason has a parallel in the Quran. The Exalted said: {خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا وَمُحَرَّمٌ على أَزْوَاجِنَا} [al-Anʿām: 139]."

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {مِنْ آيَاتِ الله}: an explication (bayān) of the relative noun, and so it is attached to «أعني» ("I mean"). It is also possible that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the relative noun or from its omitted returning pronoun, and then it is likewise attached to an omitted element.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {والحافظات}: its object is omitted because what indicates it has preceded. The implied form is "and the women who guard them (fully)". Likewise «والذاكراتِ». The omission is made pleasing by the verse-endings (fawāṣil). And the masculine is given precedence over the feminine in «لهم», and he did not say «ولَهُنَّ».

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {أَن يَكُونَ}: it is the subject (ism) of kāna, and the predicate (khabar), the preposition and its genitive noun, is advanced. His saying {إِذَا قَضَى الله} may be a pure adverb (ẓarf) governed by the "being established" (al-istiqrār) to which the predicate is attached, that is: "it was not established for any believing man or believing woman, at the time of Allah's decree, that they have a choice"; or it may be conditional, with its apodosis implied, indicated by the preceding negation.

The Kufans and Hishām read «يكونَ» with a yāʾ (dots below), because «الخِيَرَة» is feminine only figuratively (majāzī), and also because of the separation. The rest read it with a tāʾ (dots above), regarding its form. It has already been mentioned that «الخِيَرَة» is the verbal noun of takhayyara, like «الطِّيَرَة» from taṭayyara. ʿĪsā ibn Sulaymān reported that it was read «الخِيْرَة» with a quiescent yāʾ. And «مِنْ أمرِهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الخِيَرة»; it was also said that «مِن» means "in". The pronoun in «أمرِهم» and what follows is plural because what is meant by "believing man" and "believing woman" is the class (jins), and the masculine is given precedence over the feminine. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun by rights should have been singular, as you say: 'No man or woman came to me but that such-and-such was his affair.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "That is not correct, because the conjunction is with wāw, so that is not permissible except by interpreting an omission."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ}: Some grammarians stated explicitly that «على» in a construction like this is a noun. He said: "so that a verb acting on an attached pronoun does not pass over to its own attached pronoun, except in the chapter of ẓanna and in the two words faqada and ʿadima." And he counted among that:

3699 - Take it easy; for matters, their measures are in the hand of the Divine (هَوِّنْ عليكَ فإنَّ الأمورَ ... بكفِّ الإِلهِ مقاديرُها)

Likewise he ruled on «عَنْ» in his saying:

3700 - Leave aside the booty that was shouted about in its courtyards ... (دَعْ عنك نَهْباً صِيْحَ في حُجُراتِهِ ...)

You have already had this at length in al-Naḥl, in His saying {وَلَهُمْ مَّا يَشْتَهُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 57], and in His saying {وهزى إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ} [Maryam: 25] and {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 32].

His saying: «وتُخْفي»: there are several explanations. The first: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أَمْسِكْ», that is: "when you were combining your saying such-and-such with hiding such-and-such, and fearing the people." al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: that it is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "you say such-and-such in this state." al-Zamakhsharī said this too. There is a point to consider in it, since it is an affirmative imperfect, so how can the wāw come directly before it? Its analysis is like that of «قمتُ وأَصُكُّ عينَه» ("I rose and I strike his eye"), I mean by implying a subject (mubtadaʾ). The third: that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). al-Ḥawfī said this. As for His saying {والله أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَاهُ}, its like has already been given in Barāʾa.

His saying: «وَطَراً»: the object of «قَضَى». «الوَطَر» is desire and love; al-Mubarrad said this. And he recited:

3701 - How could my stay in Medina be, after Jamīl ibn Maʿmar had fulfilled his need of it (وكيف ثَوائي بالمدينةِ بعدَما ... قَضَى وَطَراً منها جميلُ بنُ مَعْمَرِ)

Abū ʿUbayda said: "«الوَطَر» is the need and the want." And he recited for al-Ḍubayʿ al-Fazārī:

3702 - He bade us farewell before we could bid him farewell, when he had fulfilled a need of our youth (ودَّعَنا قبلَ أَنْ نُوَدِّعَهْ ... لَمَّا قضى مِنْ شبابِنا وَطَراً)

The majority read «زوَّجْناكها». ʿAlī and his two sons al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased, read «زَوَّجْتُكَها» with the tāʾ of the first person singular.

And «لِكَيْلا» is attached to «زَوَّجْناكها», and here «كي» only governs the subjunctive, because the preposition has entered upon it. The two pronouns are attached to the verb because they differ in rank.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {سُنَّةَ الله}: accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like {صُنْعَ الله} [al-Naml: 88] and {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122]; or a noun put in the place of the maṣdar; or accusative by "He made" (jaʿala); or by ighrāʾ (urging), that is: "so upon him is the sunna of Allah." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected it, because the governor of ighrāʾ is not omitted, and because it would be urging a third person (ighrāʾ al-ghāʾib). What has occurred of it is interpreted as rare, such as: «عليه رجلاً لَيْسَني». I say: His saying, peace be upon him, has occurred: «وإلاَّ فعليه بالصوم» ("otherwise let him fast"). It was said: this is ighrāʾ. It was also said that it is not, but is rather a mubtadaʾ and khabar, with the bāʾ redundant in the mubtadaʾ. That is an analysis whose meaning is invalid, because fasting is not obligatory upon that person.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {الذين يُبَلِّغُونَ}: it is possible that it follows «الذين خَلَوْا» (as an adjective), and possible that it is cut off from it, in the nominative or the accusative, by implying "they" (hum), or "I mean" (aʿnī), or "I praise" (amdaḥu).

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {ولكن رَّسُولَ الله}: The majority read «لكن» with the shadda dropped, and «رسول» accusative. Its accusative case is either by implying "kāna", as the earlier "kāna" indicates it, that is "but he was", or by conjunction (ʿaṭf) to «أبا أَحَدٍ».

The first is more fitting, because «لكن» is not a conjunction, on account of the wāw; so it is more fitting that it enter upon sentences, like the one that is not a conjunction.

Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read it with the shadda, so that «رسولَ الله» is its subject (ism), and its predicate is omitted as indicated, that is: "but the Messenger of Allah is he", that is, Muḥammad. The omission of its predicate is common. And it was recited:

3707 - Had you been of Ḍabba you would have known my kinship, but (you are) a Zanjī with big lips (فلو كنتَ ضَبِّيَّاً عَرَفْتَ قَرابتي ... ولكنَّ زَنْجِيَّاً عظيمَ المَشافِرِ)

that is: "you". They also transmit this verse as «ولكنَّ زَنْجيٌّ» in the nominative, as evidence for the omission of its subject, that is: "but you".

Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it without the shadda and with «رسولُ» nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar implied, that is: "he"; or the reverse, that is: "but he is a messenger", like the saying:

3704 - I am not the vain poet among them, but a champion of the harsh war (ولَسْتُ الشاعرَ السَّفسافَ فيهمْ ... ولكنْ مِدْرَهُ الحربُ العَوانِ)

that is: "but I am the champion".

His saying: «وخاتم»: ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ, and the rest with kasra. The fatḥa is a noun for the instrument with which one seals, like «الطابَع» and «القالَب» for that with which one stamps and moulds; this is the well-known view. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned other possibilities for it, among them that it has the sense of a maṣdar. He said: "This is how it is mentioned in some works of iʿrāb." I say: this is an outright mistake; how could it be otherwise, when it requires figurative usage and an implied element? Had this been said of «خاتِم» with kasra it would have been nearer, because a maṣdar may come on the pattern fāʿil and fāʿila. That is coming shortly. Among them also: that it is a noun meaning "last". Among them: that it is a past verb like qātala, in which case «النبيين» is the direct object. I say: the reading of ʿAbd Allah, «خَتَم النبيين», supports this.

The kasra is on the basis that it is an active participle, and the reading of ʿAbd Allah mentioned above supports it. Some said: it has the same meaning as the fatḥa, that is, it means "the last of them".

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {وَمَلاَئِكَتُهُ}: it is either conjoined (ʿaṭf) to the agent of «يُصَلِّي», and the separation by the preposition and its genitive noun makes emphasis by a pronoun unnecessary. This is according to those who hold shared meaning (ishtirāk), or a common core meaning, or figurative usage, since the ṣalāh of Allah the Exalted is not the same as their ṣalāh; or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is: "and His angels pray". This is according to those who consider any of the preceding permissible; but there is a point of investigation in it, namely that they stated explicitly that when the meanings of the two predicates differ, it is not permissible to omit one because of the other, even if the wording is the same. So you do not say «زيد ضاربٌ وعمروٌ» meaning "and ʿAmr is striking in the land", that is, travelling.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {تَحِيَّتُهُمْ}: it may be a maṣdar annexed to its object, and it may be annexed to its agent and its object, in the sense that some of them greet others. So the pronoun may be for the agent and the object under two considerations, not that it is agent and object from a single aspect, as said by one who said, regarding {وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 78], that it is annexed to both the agent and the object.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying: {شَاهِداً}: an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl (circumstantial), or a concurrent one because of the nearness of the time.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {بِإِذْنِهِ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "accompanied by His facilitating"; he does not mean actual permission, because that is understood from «أَرْسلْناك».

His saying: «وسِراجاً»: it may be conjoined to what came before, either on the basis of comparison, or on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, that is: "possessor of a lamp". al-Farrāʾ allowed that the original was "and reciting a lamp" (tāliyan sirājan); by "lamp" he means the Quran. On this it would be a conjunction of attributes that belong to a single person, because the reciter is the one sent. al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be conjoined to the object of «أَرْسَلْنَاك». There is a point to consider in that, because the lamp is the Quran, and it is not described as being sent (irsāl) but as being sent down (inzāl); unless it is said that it was construed according to the meaning, as in:

3705 - I fed it chopped straw and cold water ... (عَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ...)

Also, in secondary elements things are tolerated that are not tolerated in primary ones.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {وَدَعْ أَذَاهُمْ}: it is possible that «أذاهم» is annexed to its object, that is: "leave your harming of them", meaning your punishing them; and it is possible that it is annexed to its agent, that is: "leave what they harmed you with, and do not take them to account until you are commanded."

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ}: If it is asked: what is the point of bringing «ثم», when the ruling for a woman divorced immediately after the contract is the same? The answer: it follows the usual case. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It removes the supposition from anyone who might suppose a difference of ruling between divorcing her when the marriage is recent and when the marriage is long past and the period has extended with her in the husband's care before he divorces her." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He used ʿasā as the ṣila of «مَنْ», and that is not permissible." I say: his statement can be analysed as the poet's saying is analysed:

3706 - I am one who casts a glance toward the one whom — perhaps, even if her abode is far — I shall visit (وإني لَرامٍ نَظْرَةً قِبَلَ التي ... لَعَلِّي وإنْ شَطَّتْ نَواها أَزورها)

and that is by implying "saying" (iḍmār al-qawl).

His saying: «تَعْتَدُّوْنَها» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «عِدَّة». «تَعْتَدُّونها» is on the form tafʿalūnahā (iftiʿāl): either from al-ʿadad (number) or from al-iʿtidād, that is: "you count it" or "you complete its number", from your saying "ʿadda the dirhams and iʿtaddahā", meaning he completed their number, like "I measured it (kiltuhu) and he measured it out (iktālahu)" and "I weighed it (wazantuhu) and he weighed it out (ittazanahu)". Ibn Kathīr, in one transmission, and the people of Mecca read it with the dāl unshadded. There are two explanations for it. The first: that it is from al-iʿtidād, and they disliked its doubling so they lightened it. al-Rāzī said this; he said: "Had it been from al-iʿtidāʾ, which is wrongdoing, it would be weak, because al-iʿtidāʾ takes «على»." It was said: it may be from al-iʿtidāʾ with the preposition omitted, that is: "you transgress against it", that is, against the ʿidda, figuratively, and then «تَعْتَدُوْنها», as in the saying:

3707 - She yearns and shows what is in her of longing, and I hide that which, but for grief, would have finished me (تَحِنُّ فَتُبْدِيْ ما بها مِنْ صَبابةٍ ... وأُخْفي الذي لولا الأسى لقَضاني)

that is, "would have finished me" (laqaḍā ʿalayya). al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was also read «تَعْتَدُونها» unshadded, that is: 'you transgress in it' (taʿtadūna fīhā)", as in the saying:

3708 - And many a day we witnessed ... ... ... (ويومٍ شَهِدْناه ...)

the verse. What is meant by al-iʿtidāʾ is what is in His saying: {وَلاَ تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِرَاراً لِّتَعْتَدُواْ} [al-Baqara: 231]. He means that he omitted the preposition, as it is omitted in his saying:

And many a day we witnessed, Sulaymā and ʿĀmir, few but for the thrust and the thirsty spears are its supererogatory gains (ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سُلَيْمى وعامِراً ... قليلٍ سوى الطَّعْنِ النِّهالِ نوافِلُهْ)

It was also said: the meaning of «تَعْتَدُونها» is "you transgress against them in it". Ibn ʿAṭiyya denied the reading as from Ibn Kathīr and said: "Ibn Abī Bazza made a mistake in transmitting it from him." It is not as he said. The second: that it is from al-ʿudwān and al-iʿtidāʾ, whose explanation has already been given; and the objection of Abū al-Faḍl to it, that it ought to take «على», whose answer has also been given. al-Ḥasan read «تَعْدُّونها» with a quiescent ʿayn and a shadda on the dāl, which combines two quiescent letters not in accordance with their two limits.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {مِمَّآ أَفَآءَ}: an explication (bayān) of «مَلَكَتْ»; this is not a restriction, for even if his right hand had acquired her by purchase the ruling would be the same; it came out following the usual case.

His saying: «وامرأةً»: the majority read it accusative. There are two explanations. The first: that it is conjoined to the object of «أَحْلَلْنا», that is: "and We made lawful for you a woman described by these two conditions." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "A group rejected this and said: «أَحْلَلْنا» is past, while «إنْ وَهَبَتْ», which is an adjective of the woman, is future; so «أَحْلَلْنا» is in the position of its apodosis, and the apodosis of a condition cannot be past in meaning." He said: "That is not correct, because the meaning of 'making lawful' here is informing of the lawfulness if the act occurs on that basis, as you say: 'I have permitted you to speak to so-and-so if he greets you.'" The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "and He makes lawful for you a woman."

His saying: «إنْ وَهَبَتْ ... إنْ أرادَ»: this is the interposing of a condition upon a condition, and the second is a restriction on the first; for that reason we parse it as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the ḥāl is a restriction. For this reason the jurists stipulated that the second must precede the first in existence. So if he said: "If you eat, if you ride, you are divorced", then the riding must precede the eating. This is so that the quality of being a ḥāl and the restriction are realised as I mentioned to you; for were it not to precede, some part of the eating would be left unrestricted by riding, and so they stipulated that the second precede. The verification of this has passed, and that it is on condition that there is no indication preventing the second from preceding the first, as in your saying: "If I marry you, if I divorce you, my slave is free": here the precedence of divorce over marriage cannot be conceived.

However, a difficulty has occurred to me concerning what the jurists said, on the basis of this verse. It is that the second condition here cannot precede in existence with respect to the ruling specific to the Prophet ﷺ — not that it is impossible rationally. For the exegetes interpreted His saying «إنْ أرادَ» as meaning "if he accepted the gift", because by his acceptance, peace be upon him, his marriage is completed; and its precedence over the gift cannot be conceived, since acceptance comes later. Moreover the story was as I mentioned, that his desire came after her gift, and this is mentioned in the exegesis. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), when he came to this place, made the second condition precede the first by the general rule and did not find any of what I mentioned problematic. I presented this difficulty to a number of the notables of our time and they acknowledged it, and no answer to it appeared, except what I stated earlier, that there is an indication preventing that, as I exemplified for you just now.

Abū Ḥaywa read «وامرأة» nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar implied, that is: "We have made her lawful for you also." In His saying {إِنْ أَرَادَ النبي} there is a shift (iltifāt) from the second person to the third using the overt noun, to alert that the reason for that is prophethood; then he returned to the second person and said: «خالصةً لك».

Ubayy, al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read «أَنْ» with fatḥa, and there are two explanations. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) of «امرأة», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. It is as if it were said: "and We made lawful for you a woman's giving herself to you." The second: that it is by omission of the lām of cause, that is: "because she gave." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إذ وَهَبَتْ», which has the sense of causation.

His saying: «خالصةً»: the majority read it accusative. There are several explanations. The first: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «وَهَبَتْ», that is: "in the state of her being exclusive to you, to the exclusion of others." The second: that it is a ḥāl from «امرأةٌ» because it was described and so became specified; it is the same as the first in meaning. al-Zajjāj took this view. The third: that it is an adjective of an implied maṣdar, that is: "an exclusive gift", and he made it accusative by «وَهَبَتْ». The fourth: that it is a confirmatory maṣdar like {وَعْدَ الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 122]. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fāʿil and fāʿila forms among maṣdars are not rare, such as «الخارِج», «القاعِد», «الكاذِبة» and «العافِية»." By «الخارج» he means what is in the saying of al-Farazdaq:

3709 - ... ... nor a false word coming out of my mouth (... ولا خارِجاً مِنْ فِيَّ زُوْرُ كَلامِ)

and by «القاعد» what is in their saying «أقاعِداً وقد سار الرَّكْبُ» ("sitting while the caravan has set out?"), and by «الكاذبة» what is in His saying the Exalted {لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ}. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected to his saying "not rare" and said: "Rather they are rare, and what has occurred is interpreted otherwise." It was also read «خالِصَةٌ» nominative. If «خالصةً» is a ḥāl, the mubtadaʾ «she» is implied, that is, the woman who gives herself; and if it is a maṣdar, it is implied: "that state is exclusive." And «لك» is an explication (bayān), that is: "I mean for you", like "may there be rain for you" (saqyan laka).

His saying: «لكيلا» is attached to «خالصةً», with what is between them parenthetical, and «مِنْ دون» is attached to «خالصةً», as you say: "it became free of such-and-such" (khalaṣa min kadhā).

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {وَمَنِ ابتغيت}: two explanations are possible for «مَنْ». The first: that it is conditional, in the position of accusative by what follows it. And His saying {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ} is its apodosis. The meaning: "whichever of the women you set aside you seek, then there is no blame upon you in that." The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ with its returning pronoun omitted. On this «مَنْ» may be a relative noun, or may be conditional, and {فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ} is the khabar or the apodosis, that is: "and the one you sought."
