And السَّرَاحُ is a noun for "releasing" (al-tasrīḥ), not the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَحْلَلْنَا لَكَ أَزْوَاجَكَ اللَّاتِي آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ مِمَّا أَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمِّكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمَّاتِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالَاتِكَ اللَّاتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً إِنْ وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنْ أَرَادَ النَّبِيُّ أَنْ يَسْتَنْكِحَهَا خَالِصَةً لَكَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا فَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِي أَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ لِكَيْلَا يَكُونَ عَلَيْكَ حَرَجٌ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا (٥٠))
His saying (وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً): there are two views on what puts it in the accusative. First: أَحْلَلْنَا at the beginning of the verse. Some rejected this, saying: أَحْلَلْنَا is past, while «إِنْ وَهَبَتْ», which is a qualification of the woman, is future, and «أَحْلَلْنَا» stands in the position of its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the apodosis cannot be past in meaning. This is not correct, because the meaning of "making lawful" here is the announcement of lawfulness if the act occurs in that way; as you say: "I have permitted you to speak to so-and-so if he greets you." The second view: that it is in the accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We make lawful for you a woman" (وَنُحِلُّ لَكَ امْرَأَةً).
It is also read «أَنْ وَهَبَتْ» with fatḥa on the hamza; it is then a badal (substitute) of امْرَأَةً, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). It is also said: the implied form is "because she gave" (لِأَنْ وَهَبَتْ).
And (خَالِصَةً) may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in وَهَبَتْ, and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "an exclusive gift" (هِبَةً خَالِصَةً).
It may also be a maṣdar, i.e. "she made that exclusively yours" (أَخْلَصَتْ ذَلِكَ لَكَ إِخْلَاصًا); the pattern fāʿila has occurred as a maṣdar, as in الْعَاقِبَةُ and الْعَافِيَةُ.
And (لِكَيْلَا) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَحْلَلْنَا.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ تَقَرَّ أَعْيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحْزَنَّ وَيَرْضَيْنَ بِمَا آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَلِيمًا (٥١))
(وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ): «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative, governed by ابْتَغَيْتَ; it is conditional, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ».
It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the referential pronoun omitted, i.e. "and the one whom you desired" (وَالَّتِي ابْتَغَيْتَهَا), and the khabar (predicate) is «فَلَا جُنَاحَ».
His saying (كُلُّهُنَّ): the nominative is as tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in (يَرْضَيْنَ), and the accusative (كُلَّهُنَّ) as tawkīd of the accusative pronoun in (آتَيْتَهُنَّ).

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّسَاءُ مِنْ بَعْدُ وَلَا أَنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكَ حُسْنُهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ رَقِيبًا (٥٢))
His saying (إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ): it may be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) of النِّسَاءُ, and it may be in the position of the accusative according to the basic rule of exception, it being of the same genus.
It may also be of a different genus.
And His saying (مِنْ أَزْوَاجٍ): it is in the position of the accusative, and (مِنْ) is redundant (zāʾida).
«إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ» may be in the position of the accusative as excepted from النِّسَاءُ, or in the position of the nominative as a badal; and it may be in the position of the accusative as a badal of أَزْوَاجٍ; and the exception may be disjoined (munqaṭiʿ).

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ وَلَكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَادْخُلُوا فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَانْتَشِرُوا وَلَا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ وَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَاعًا فَاسْأَلُوهُنَّ مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ ذَلِكُمْ أَطْهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمْ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَلَا أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا أَزْوَاجَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أَبَدًا إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمًا (٣٥)) [Translator's note: so numbered in the text; this is verse 53.]
His saying (إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "do not enter except with permission granted to you".
And (إِلَى) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُؤْذَنَ, because its meaning is "you are invited".
And (غَيْرَ) is in the accusative as a ḥāl of the agent in «تَدْخُلُوا», or of the genitive pronoun in «لَكُمْ».
It is also read in the genitive (غَيْرِ), as a naʿt (adjective) of طَعَامٍ. According to the Basrans this is an error, because it is applied to something other than what it belongs to; so the agent pronoun would have to be made overt, giving غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ أَنْتُمْ ("you not waiting").
His saying (وَلَا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نَاظِرِينَ.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِأَزْوَاجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَاءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ جَلَابِيبِهِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَنْ يُعْرَفْنَ فَلَا يُؤْذَيْنَ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا (٥٩))
His saying (يُدْنِينَ): it is like His saying, the Exalted: (قُلْ لِعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ) in [Sūrat] Ibrāhīm.

ukberi-tibyan:60-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْمُرْجِفُونَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ ثُمَّ لَا يُجَاوِرُونَكَ فِيهَا إِلَّا قَلِيلًا (٦٠) مَلْعُونِينَ أَيْنَمَا ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا وَقُتِّلُوا تَقْتِيلًا (٦١))
His saying (مَلْعُونِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent in «يُجَاوِرُونَكَ». It cannot be a ḥāl of what comes after «أَيْنَ», because it is conditional, and what comes after the condition does not govern what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا (٦٢))
His saying (سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ): it is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He established that as a practice" (سَنَّ ذَلِكَ سُنَّةً).

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ يَقُولُونَ يَا لَيْتَنَا أَطَعْنَا اللَّهَ وَأَطَعْنَا الرَّسُولَا (٦٦))
(يَوْمَ تُقَلَّبُ وُجُوهُهُمْ): it may be an adverb of time (ẓarf) for «لَا يَجِدُونَ» and for نَصِيرًا [in verse 65], or for «يَقُولُونَ».
And «يَقُولُونَ», on the first two views, is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الْوُجُوهُ, because what is meant is their owners. It is weak for it to be a ḥāl of the genitive pronoun, because it is a muḍāf ilayhi.
It is also read «تُقَلِّبُ» — meaning the Blaze (al-saʿīr) [is the agent] — with وُجُوهَهُمْ in the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:72-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا عَرَضْنَا الْأَمَانَةَ عَلَى السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَالْجِبَالِ فَأَبَيْنَ أَنْ يَحْمِلْنَهَا وَأَشْفَقْنَ مِنْهَا وَحَمَلَهَا الْإِنْسَانُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ ظَلُومًا جَهُولًا (٧٢) لِيُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكَاتِ وَيَتُوبَ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا (٧٣))
His saying (لِيُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَمَلَهَا. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His words: ﴿وَإذْ أخَذْنا مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِيثاقَهم ومِنكَ ومِن نُوحٍ وإبْراهِيمَ ومُوسى وعِيسى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ﴾: the position of ”إذْ“ is accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "Remember when We took". Allah mentioned him ﷺ in the taking of the covenant before Noah, and it has come in the exegesis: "I was created before the prophets and sent after them." On this view there is no fronting (taqdīm) and no postponement (taʾkhīr) in this speech; it runs in its natural order, and the covenant was taken when they were brought forth from the loins of Adam — Allah bless him — like tiny particles (al-dharr). The doctrine of the linguists is that the wāw means combination (al-ijtimāʿ), and there is no indication in it that what is mentioned first cannot have the meaning of coming later. So the meaning, according to the doctrine of the linguists, is: "and from Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus son of Mary, and from you". Similar to it is His words: ﴿واسْجُدِي وارْكَعِي مَعَ الرّاكِعِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 43].

zajjaj:8-8.t: His words: ﴿لِيَسْألَ الصّادِقِينَ عَنْ صِدْقِهِمْ﴾: its meaning is: "that He may ask those of the messengers who conveyed [the message] about their truthfulness in their conveying". The interpretation of questioning the messengers — while Allah knows that they are truthful — is the rebuking (al-tabkīt) of those who disbelieved in them, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116], and he answered, saying: ﴿سُبْحانَكَ ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ إنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116], then he said: ﴿ما قُلْتُ لَهم إلا ما أمَرْتَنِي بِهِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 117]. So its interpretation is the rebuking of those who deny. On this basis: ﴿لِيَسْألَ الصّادِقِينَ عَنْ صِدْقِهِمْ وأعَدَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾, that is: for those who disbelieve in the messengers.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His words: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم إذْ جاءَتْكم جُنُودٌ فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا وجُنُودًا لَمْ تَرَوْها﴾: these hosts are the Confederates (al-aḥzāb). The hosts that came were Quraysh — with Abū Sufyān —, Ghaṭafān and Banū Qurayẓa; they formed a confederacy and backed one another in making war on the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So Allah sent against them a wind that overturned (kafaʾat) their cooking pots, that is, turned them upside down, uprooted their tents and drove them away from their place. The hosts that they did not see are the angels.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿إذْ جاءُوكم مِن فَوْقِكم ومِن أسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾: Qurayẓa came from above them, and Quraysh and Ghaṭafān came from the direction of Mecca, from below them.
His words: ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ الظُّنُونا﴾: the readers differed over it. Some read it retaining the alif both in pause and in continuous recitation; some read: ”اَلظُّنُونَ“ without an alif in continuous recitation and with an alif in pause; and Abū ʿAmr read: ”اَلظُّنُونَ“ without an alif in both continuous recitation and pause. What the skilled grammarians hold — and those of them who follow the Sunna — is that they read: ”اَلظُّنُونا“, pausing on the alif and not joining [it to what follows]. They did this only because the ends of verses are, in their view, fawāṣil (verse endings), and at their ends in pause they retain what may be omitted in continuous recitation. These follow the Muṣḥaf, and they dislike joining while retaining the alif, because then they would not have paused on the end so as to treat it the way verse endings are treated. Like this in the speech of the Arabs, in rhymes:
أقِلِّي اللَّوْمَ عاذِلَ والعِتابا
(Lessen the blame, O censuring woman, and the reproach.)
So he retained the alif, because it is in the position of a verse ending, namely the rhyme.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُنالِكَ ابْتُلِيَ المُؤْمِنُونَ وزُلْزِلُوا زِلْزالا شَدِيدًا﴾: ”زَلْزالًا“ with fatḥa on the zāy is also permissible. The maṣdar (verbal noun) of the doubled (muḍāʿaf) [quadriliteral] comes in two patterns: ”فَعْلالٌ“ and ”فِعْلالٌ“, as in ”قَلْقَلَهُ، قَلْقالًا، وقِلْقالًا“ and ”زَلْزَلْتُهُ، زَلْزالًا، وزِلْزالًا“. The kasra is more common and better, because the non-doubled verbs of this class have kasra on the first letter, as in ”دَحْرَجْتُهُ دِحْراجًا“, in which nothing but kasra is permitted. The meaning of ”هُنالِكَ ابْتُلِيَ المُؤْمِنُونَ“ is: "in that situation the believers were tested", and the meaning of ”زُلْزِلُوا زِلْزالًا شَدِيدًا“ is: "they were severely alarmed and shaken".

zajjaj:12-12.t: His words: ﴿وَإذْ يَقُولُ المُنافِقُونَ والَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ ما وعَدَنا اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ إلا غُرُورًا﴾: the position of ”إذْ“ is accusative (naṣb); the meaning is: "Remember when the hypocrites say". The meaning of the verse is that the hypocrites said: "Muḥammad ﷺ promised us that Persia and Byzantium would be conquered for us, while here we are in this place of ours, and not one of us is able to go out to relieve himself; so this is a promise of delusion."

zajjaj:13-13.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذْ قالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنهم يا أهْلَ يَثْرِبَ لا مُقامَ لَكم فارْجِعُوا﴾: it is also read: ”لا مَقامَ لَكم“ with fatḥa on the mīm. Whoever reads the mīm with ḍamma, the meaning is: "there is no staying for you"; you say: ”أقَمْتُ في البَلَدِ إقامَةً ومُقامًا“ (I stayed in the town, a staying). Whoever reads: ”لا مَقامَ لَكم“ with fatḥa on the mīm, the meaning is: "there is no place for you in which you may stay". These were holding the believers back from the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿وَيَسْتَأْذِنُ فَرِيقٌ مِنهُمُ النَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إنَّ بُيُوتَنا عَوْرَةٌ﴾, that is: ”مُعَوَّرَةٌ“ (exposed); that is because they said: "Our houses are among those adjoining the enemy, and we will be robbed from them." So Allah the Exalted declared them liars and made known that their aim was flight and running away, saying: ﴿وَما هي بِعَوْرَةٍ﴾. It is also read: ”وَما هي بِعَوِرَةٍ“. One says: ”عَوِرَ المَكانُ، يَعْوَرُ، عَوَرًا، وهو عَوِرٌ“ (the place became exposed … and it is exposed), and ”بُيُوتٌ عَوِرَةٌ“ and ”بُيُوتٌ عَوْرَةٌ“, on two accounts: on the basis of making ”عَوْرَةٌ“ quiescent (taskīn), and on the meaning "possessing exposure" (dhātu ʿawra). ﴿إنْ يُرِيدُونَ إلا فِرارًا﴾, that is: they do not want protection from theft; rather, the hypocrites want to flee from supporting the Prophet — upon him be peace.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَلَوْ دُخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن أقْطارِها﴾, that is: and if the houses were entered from their sides, ﴿ثُمَّ سُئِلُوا الفِتْنَةَ لآتَوْها﴾. It is also read with shortening (qaṣr): ”لَأتَوْها“. Whoever reads: ”لَآتَوْها“ with lengthening (madd), the meaning is: "they would have given it", that is: "if it were said to them: 'Be against the Muslims, openly displaying sedition (al-fitna)', they would have done so". ﴿وَما تَلَبَّثُوا بِها إلا يَسِيرًا﴾. And whoever reads: لَأتَوْها with shortening, the meaning is: "they would have gone for it".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ المُعَوِّقِينَ مِنكم والقائِلِينَ لإخْوانِهِمْ هَلُمَّ إلَيْنا﴾, that is: those who hold back the Prophet's ﷺ helpers from him. That is because they said to the helpers of the Prophet ﷺ: "Muḥammad and his companions are nothing but a handful who could be fed on one head [of livestock] (akalatu raʾs); if they were meat, Abū Sufyān and his companions would gobble them up. So leave them and come over to us."
His words: ﴿وَلا يَأْتُونَ البَأْسَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾, that is: they do not come to battle with the companions of the Prophet ﷺ except as a feigned excuse (taʿdhīr), making them imagine that they are with them.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿أشِحَّةً عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: ”أشِحَّةً“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is: "They come to battle being stingy towards you with victory and booty; when fear comes they are the most cowardly of people, and when booty comes they are the most grasping of people and the most quarrelsome of them." ﴿فَإذا جاءَ الخَوْفُ رَأيْتَهم يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أعْيُنُهم كالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾, because they attend with no intention of good, only an intention of evil. ﴿فَإذا ذَهَبَ الخَوْفُ سَلَقُوكم بِألْسِنَةٍ حِدادٍ﴾: the meaning of “ سَلَقُوكم ” is: they addressed you in the harshest of address and the most eloquent of it regarding the booty. One says: “ خَطِيبٌ مِسْلاقٌ، وسَلّاقٌ " (a sharp-tongued orator) when he is eloquent in his speech. ﴿أشِحَّةً عَلى الخَيْرِ﴾, that is: they addressed you while being grasping for wealth and booty.
His words: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا فَأحْبَطَ اللَّهُ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾, that is: even though they displayed faith and acted hypocritically, they are not believers.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His words: ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ الأحْزابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا﴾, that is: they reckon that the Confederates, after their defeat and departure, have not gone, out of their cowardice and their fear of them. ﴿وَإنْ يَأْتِ الأحْزابُ يَوَدُّوا لَوْ أنَّهم بادُونَ في الأعْرابِ﴾, that is: when the hosts and the Confederates come, they wish that they were in the desert.

zajjaj:22-22.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَمّا رَأى المُؤْمِنُونَ الأحْزابَ قالُوا هَذا ما وعَدَنا اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ﴾: Allah described the state of the hypocrites in the war against the disbelievers and the state of the believers in the war against the disbelievers. He described the hypocrites with faintheartedness, cowardice, evasion, hastening to sedition and increase in disbelief, and He described the believers with steadfastness — at the time of fear — in faith, saying: ﴿وَلَمّا رَأى المُؤْمِنُونَ الأحْزابَ﴾, the verse. The promise is that Allah said to them: ﴿أمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أنْ تَدْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ ولَمّا يَأْتِكم مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلِكم مَسَّتْهُمُ البَأْساءُ والضَّرّاءُ وزُلْزِلُوا حَتّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ مَتى نَصْرُ اللَّهِ ألا إنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 214]. So likewise, when the companions of the Prophet ﷺ were tested and severely shaken, they knew that Paradise and victory had become due to them.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ رِجالٌ صَدَقُوا ما عاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: the meaning is that they made a covenant in Islam and remained true to their covenant. The position of ”ما“ is accusative through ”صَدَقُوا“. ﴿فَمِنهم مَن قَضى نَحْبَهُ﴾, that is: his term, and he did not change; that is His words: ﴿وَما بَدَّلُوا تَبْدِيلا﴾. So the meaning is that he died upon his religion without changing.

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ اللَّهُ الصّادِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ ويُعَذِّبَ المُنافِقِينَ﴾, that is: that He may reward those who were true to their covenant; and the hypocrites were false to their covenant, because they displayed Islam and concealed disbelief. His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَيُعَذِّبَ المُنافِقِينَ إنْ شاءَ أوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, that is: or that He may move them from hypocrisy to faith.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His words: ﴿وَرَدَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنالُوا خَيْرًا﴾: by this He means here Abū Sufyān and his companions, the Confederates. ”﴿لَمْ يَنالُوا خَيْرًا﴾“, that is: they did not gain victory over the Muslims, and that would have been "good" in their eyes, so they were addressed according to their own usage.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His words: ﴿وَأنْـزَلَ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوهم مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ مِن صَياصِيهِمْ﴾: by this are meant Banū Qurayẓa. The meaning of ظاهَرُوهُمْ is: they aided them against the Prophet ﷺ. So Allah cast terror into their hearts and brought them down to the judgement of Saʿd, and Saʿd judged concerning them that their fighting men be killed and their offspring taken captive.

zajjaj:27-27.t: ﴿وَأوْرَثَكم أرْضَهم ودِيارَهم وأمْوالَهُمْ﴾: the Prophet ﷺ gave their land, their dwellings and their wealth to the Emigrants (al-muhājirūn), because they did not own real estate. The meaning of ”اَلصَّياصِي“ is: anything by which one protects oneself; ”اَلصَّياصِي“ here are the fortresses, and it is said: the palaces, and palaces may be used as strongholds. ”اَلصَّياصِي“ are also the horns of cattle and gazelles, and every horn is a ”صَيْصَيَةٌ“, because horned animals protect themselves with their horns and defend themselves with them. And ”صِيصَةُ الدِّيكِ“ is the cock's spur, because it too protects itself with it.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His words: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لأزْواجِكَ إنْ كُنْتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وزِينَتَها فَتَعالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعْكُنَّ وأُسَرِّحْكُنَّ سَراحًا جَمِيلا﴾: they had wanted something of the affairs of this world, so Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to give his wives the choice between staying with him in seeking what is with Allah, or release, if they wanted the life of this world and its adornment. They chose the Hereafter over this world, and Paradise over adornment.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His words: ﴿وَإنْ كُنْتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ والدّارَ الآخِرَةَ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ أعَدَّ لِلْمُحْسِناتِ مِنكُنَّ أجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾, that is: whoever of you prefers the Hereafter, her reward is a great reward.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾ — it is also read: ”مُبَيَّنَةٍ“ — ﴿يُضاعَفْ لَها العَذابُ ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾: the reading is ”يُضاعَفْ“ with an alif, and Abū ʿAmr alone read: ”يُضَعِّفْ“; both are good. Abū ʿUbayda said: she would be punished with three punishments. He said: she was liable to be punished once, and when that once is doubled twofold, the punishment becomes three punishments. This view is worth nothing, because the meaning of ”يُضاعَفْ لَها العَذابُ ضِعْفَيْنِ“ is: "the punishment of her crime is made like the two punishments of two crimes". The proof of this is: ﴿نُؤْتِها أجْرَها مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 31]; it cannot be that she is given two rewards for obedience and three punishments for disobedience. The meaning of ”ضِعْفُ الشَّيْءِ“ is: its like, because the ḍiʿf of a thing that doubles it is in the position of the equal weight (mithqāl) of the thing. The meaning of ”يَقْنُتْ“ is: he persists in obedience. ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لَها رِزْقًا كَرِيمًا﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 31]: it has come in the exegesis that it is Paradise.
His words: ﴿إنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أهْلَ البَيْتِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 33]: ”أهْلَ البَيْتِ“ is accusative by way of praise (ʿalā l-madḥ). Had it been read ”أهْلِ البَيْتِ“ in the genitive, or read ”أهْلُ البَيْتِ“ in the nominative, that would have been permissible, but the reading is the accusative, and it is on two accounts: on the meaning "I mean the people of the house", and as a vocative (al-nidāʾ), on the meaning: "O people of the house". ”اَلرِّجْسُ“ in the language is anything found objectionable and filthy, whether food, deed or indecency. It is said that ”أهْلَ البَيْتِ“ here means "the wives of the Prophet ﷺ", and it is said: the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and the men who are his family. The language indicates that it is for the women and the men together, because of His saying ”عَنْكم“ with the mīm, and ”وَيُطَهِّرَكم“; had it been for the women, only ”عَنْكُنَّ“ and ”وَيُطَهِّرَكُنَّ“ would be permissible. The proof of this is His words: ﴿واذْكُرْنَ ما يُتْلى في بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 34], where He singled out the women in the address.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَن يَقْنُتْ مِنكُنَّ لِلَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾ with the yāʾ, ﴿وَتَعْمَلْ﴾ with the tāʾ: the first is construed according to the wording (al-lafẓ), and ”تَعْمَلْ“ according to the meaning (al-maʿnā). Whoever reads both with the tāʾ construes according to the meaning, intending: "and she of you who is devoutly obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does". Whoever reads the first with the tāʾ, it is ugly (qabīḥ) for him to read ”وَيَعْمَلْ“, because he has already construed according to the meaning and made clear that the relative (al-mawṣūl) is feminine, so construing according to the wording becomes ugly.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
His words: ﴿يا نِساءَ النَّبِيِّ لَسْتُنَّ كَأحَدٍ مِنَ النِّساءِ﴾: He did not say ”كَواحِدَةٍ مِنَ النِّساءِ“, because ”أحَدٌ“ is a general negation covering masculine and feminine, singular and plural.
His words: ﴿إنِ اتَّقَيْتُنَّ فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ بِالقَوْلِ فَيَطْمَعَ الَّذِي في قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ﴾, that is: do not say words by which a hypocrite finds a way to hope that you will comply with him. ﴿وَقُلْنَ قَوْلا مَعْرُوفًا﴾, that is: say what religion and Islam require, without softness in it, but rather with plainness and clarity. ”فَيَطْمَعَ“ is in the accusative, and that is the reading; the answer (jawāb) to ”فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ“ is ”فَيَطْمَعَ“. It is also read: ”فَيَطْمَعِ الَّذِي في قَلْبِهِ مَرَضٌ“ with the ʿayn made quiescent, conjoined (nasaq) to ”فَلا تَخْضَعْنَ فَيَطْمَعْ“.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقَرْنَ في بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾: it is also read: ”وَقِرْنَ“ with kasra on the qāf. Whoever reads with fatḥa, it is from ”قَرِرْتُ بِالمَكانِ، أقَرُّ“ (I stayed in the place), so the meaning is: ”واقْرَرْنَ“; when it is lightened it becomes ”وَقَرْنَ“: the alif is dropped because of the heaviness of the doubling in the rāʾ, and its vowel is thrown onto the qāf. The better is: ”وَقِرْنَ في بُيُوتِكُنَّ“ with kasra on the qāf, and it is from ”اَلْوَقارُ“ (dignity); you say: ”وَقَرَ، يَقِرُّ في المَكانِ“. It may also be from ”قَرَرْتُ في المَكانِ، أقِرُّهُ“, so that it is shortened on the basis that it comes from ”واقْرِرْنَ“ with kasra on the first rāʾ. So the kasra is from two directions together: from its being from ”اَلْوَقارُ“ and from its being from ”اَلْقَرارُ“.
His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَلا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ الجاهِلِيَّةِ الأُولى﴾: ”اَلتَّبَرُّجُ“ is displaying adornment and that by which a man's desire is invited. It is said that they used to walk with a swaying gait and strut. It is said that the first Jāhiliyya is those from the time of Adam to the time of Noah; it is said: from the time of Noah to the time of Idrīs; and it is said: from the time of Jesus to the time of the Prophet ﷺ. The most likely is that it is from the time of Jesus to the time of the Prophet ﷺ, because they are the well-known people of the Jāhiliyya, for it is related that they used to keep prostitutes (al-baghāyā) — they are the immoral women — who brought them earnings. If it is asked: why was it called ”اَلْأُولى“ (the first)? It is answered: everything preceding, masculine or feminine, is called ”أُولى“ and ”أوَّلٌ“; so its interpretation is that they preceded the community of Muḥammad ﷺ, so they are ”أُولى“ and ”أوَّلٌ“ relative to the community of Muḥammad ﷺ.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ المُسْلِمِينَ والمُسْلِماتِ﴾ up to His words: ﴿وَأجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾: when what was revealed about the wives of the Prophet ﷺ was revealed, the Muslim women said: "Has nothing then been revealed about us?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that women and men are recompensed for their deeds with forgiveness and a great reward.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والحافِظِينَ فُرُوجَهم والحافِظاتِ والذّاكِرِينَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا والذّاكِراتِ﴾: the meaning is: "and the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them (al-ḥāfiẓātihā), and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him (al-dhākirātihi)". The mention of the hāʾ was dispensed with because of what preceded, which indicated what was omitted. Similar to it is: ”وَنَخْلَعُ ونَتْرُكُ مَن يَفْجُرُكَ“ (and we cast off and leave whoever disobeys You); the meaning is: "and we cast off whoever disobeys You and leave him". Similar to it from poetry:
وَكُمْتًا مُدَمّاةً كَأنَّ مُتُونَها ∗∗∗ جَرى فَوْقَها واسْتَشْعَرَتْ لَوْنُ مُذْهَبِ
(And bay [horses], blood-red, as though over their backs there ran — and they took it as an undergarment — the colour of gilding.)
with ”لَوْنُ“ in the nominative; the meaning is: "the colour of gilding ran over them, and they took it as an undergarment".

zajjaj:36-36.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما كانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ ولا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إذا قَضى اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ أمْرًا أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الخِيَرَةُ مِن أمْرِهِمْ﴾: ”اَلْخِيَرَةُ“ is choosing. «This verse was revealed because of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh — she was the daughter of the paternal aunt of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — and Zayd ibn Ḥāritha. Zayd was the freedman (mawlā) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and his standing with him, in his love for him, was like the standing of a son. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to Zaynab in order to marry her to Zayd, and she thought that he had proposed to her for himself — upon him be peace. When she learned that he wanted her for Zayd, she disliked that. Allah, Majestic and Exalted, made known that there is no choice against what Allah and His Messenger have decreed, and he married her to Zayd.»

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وأنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ واتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾: the meaning of ”أنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ“ is: He guided him to Islam; and ”أنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ“: you freed him from slavery. Zayd had complained to the Prophet — upon him be peace — about the matter of Zaynab, and he commanded him to hold on to her. He — upon him be peace — would have loved to marry her, except that he — upon him be peace — preferred what he loved of enjoining what is right, so he said: ”أمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ واتَّقِ اللَّهَ“. ﴿وَتُخْفِي في نَفْسِكَ ما اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ وتَخْشى النّاسَ واللَّهُ أحَقُّ أنْ تَخْشاهُ﴾, that is: you dislike what people would say. ﴿فَلَمّا قَضى زَيْدٌ مِنها وطَرًا زَوَّجْناكَها﴾, that is: when Zayd divorced her. ”اَلْوَطَرُ“ and ”اَلْأرَبُ“ in the language have one meaning. Al-Khalīl said: the meaning of ”اَلْوَطَرُ“ is every need in which you have a concern; when one attains it, it is said: ”قَدْ قَضى وطَرَهُ، وأرَبَهُ“, that is: "he has attained what he wanted of it".
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِكَيْ لا يَكُونَ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَجٌ في أزْواجِ أدْعِيائِهِمْ إذا قَضَوْا مِنهُنَّ وطَرًا﴾, that is: We married you to Zaynab, who was the wife of Zayd whom you had adopted, so that it would not be thought that whoever adopts a man, his wife is not lawful for the adopter.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما كانَ عَلى النَّبِيِّ مِن حَرَجٍ فِيما فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَهُ سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ في الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ﴾: ”سُنَّةَ“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because its meaning is: "There is no blame on the Prophet in what Allah has ordained; Allah has laid down a good, ample way (sunna) in which there is no ḥaraj", that is: no constraint in it. ”اَلسُّنَّةُ“ is the way (al-ṭarīqa), and ”اَلسَّنَنُ“ (course) is from all of this.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِي الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ﴾: its meaning is: among the prophets who were before Muḥammad — Allah bless them and grant them peace —, that is: Allah's way in making things ample for Muḥammad ﷺ in what Allah ordained for him is like His way with the past prophets.
His words, the Exalted: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 39]: ”اَلَّذِينَ“ is in the position of the genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of His words: ”في الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ“. It may also be nominative by way of praise, on [the implied form] ”هَمُ الَّذِينَ يُبَلِّغُونَ رِسالاتِ اللَّهِ“, and it may be accusative on the meaning: "I mean those who convey".

zajjaj:40-40.t: His words, the Exalted: ﴿ما كانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أبا أحَدٍ مِن رِجالِكُمْ﴾, that is: Zayd was not the son of Muḥammad ﷺ; he did not beget him. Male children were indeed born to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Ibrāhīm, al-Ṭayyib, al-Qāsim and al-Muṭahhar. Its interpretation is only: "What is forbidden to a father was not forbidden to him regarding the one he adopted." The Prophet ﷺ is the father of the believers in veneration and reverence. It has been read: “ وخاتِمَ النَّبِيِّينَ ” and “ وخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ ”. Whoever reads the tāʾ with kasra, its meaning is: “ he sealed the prophets ”; and whoever reads: “ وخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ ” with fatḥa on the tāʾ, its meaning is: “ the last of the prophets ”; there is no prophet after him ﷺ. It is also permissible: “ ولَكِنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وخاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينَ ”. Whoever reads the accusative, the meaning is: “ but he was the Messenger of Allah and was the seal of the prophets ”; and whoever reads the nominative, the meaning is: “ but he is the seal of the prophets ".

zajjaj:43-43.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكم ومَلائِكَتُهُ﴾: Allah's ṣalāt upon His creation is His mercy and His guiding them.

zajjaj:44-44.t: His words: ﴿تَحِيَّتُهم يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ سَلامٌ﴾: the greeting of the people of Paradise is ”سَلامٌ“; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿تَحِيَّتُهم يَوْمَ يَلْقَوْنَهُ سَلامٌ﴾

zajjaj:45-45.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إنّا أرْسَلْناكَ شاهِدًا ومُبَشِّرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾, that is: a witness over your community by conveying — conveying the message —, a bearer of good tidings of Paradise, and a warner against the Fire. All of this is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: " We sent you in the state of witnessing, giving good tidings and warning.

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿وَداعِيًا إلى اللَّهِ بِإذْنِهِ﴾, that is: calling to the oneness of Allah and what brings near to Him; and بِإذْنِهِ, that is: by His command. ﴿وَسِراجًا مُنِيرًا﴾, that is: and a clear Book. The meaning is: “We sent you as a witness, and possessor of a light-giving lamp, and possessor of a clear Book. Or, if you wish, “ وسِراجًا ” is accusative on the meaning: “ calling to Allah and reciting a clear Book ".

zajjaj:48-48.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَدَعْ أذاهُمْ﴾: its meaning is: leave the harm of the hypocrites. The interpretation of ”وَدَعْ أذاهم“ is: leave them; do not requite them for it until you are given a command concerning them.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا نَكَحْتُمُ المُؤْمِناتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾: the meaning of ”تَمَسُّوهُنَّ“ is: you approach them [sexually]. ﴿فَما لَكم عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن عِدَّةٍ تَعْتَدُّونَها فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ وسَرِّحُوهُنَّ سَراحًا جَمِيلا﴾: some said: ”فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ“ was abrogated by His words, the Exalted: ﴿وَإنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ ما فَرَضْتُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 237], and the half takes the place of the provision (al-tamtīʿ), unless he had not named a dower for her, in which case she has half the dower of her peers. Allah removed the waiting period (al-ʿidda) from the woman with whom marriage has not been consummated, because the ʿidda is in origin [a means of] ascertaining that the womb is free (istibrāʾ).

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إنّا أحْلَلْنا لَكَ أزْواجَكَ اللاتِي آتَيْتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾: ”أُجُورَهُنَّ“ is their dowers. ﴿وَما مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ مِمّا أفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ﴾: the basis of ownership of slave women and slaves is what may lawfully be taken captive and gained as fayʾ (spoils). As for a wrongful captive (sabyu l-khabītha), intercourse with her and ownership of her are not permissible. One says: ”هَذا سَبْيُ طَيِّبَةٍ، وسَبْيُ خِبْثَةٍ“ (this is a lawful captivity, and an unlawful captivity). The lawful captivity is the captivity of those of the people of disbelief whom it is permissible to fight; as for whoever has a covenant, it is not permissible to take him captive, nor to own any slave or slave woman from them.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وامْرَأةً مُؤْمِنَةً إنْ وهَبَتْ نَفْسَها لِلنَّبِيِّ إنْ أرادَ النَّبِيُّ أنْ يَسْتَنْكِحَها خالِصَةً لَكَ مِن دُونِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: it is also read: “ أنْ وهَبَتْ ” with fatḥa, that is: “ if she gives herself to the Prophet ﷺ she is lawful for him ” «[Translator's note: the gloss given here fits the reading with kasra (إنْ, "if"); the source as printed has «أنْ … with fatḥa» at this point, which is translated as written.]». And whoever reads: “ أنْ وهَبَتْ ” with fatḥa, the meaning is: “ We made her lawful because she gave herself ”. “ خالِصَةً ” is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: “ We have made lawful for you these, and We have made lawful for you whoever gives herself to you ”. It was only said “ لِلنَّبِيِّ ” here because, had it been said “ إنْ وهَبَتْ نَفْسَها لَكَ ", it might have been imagined that there is an indication in the speech that this is permissible for other than the Prophet — upon him be peace —, as it is permissible in His words: ﴿وَبَناتِ عَمِّكَ وبَناتِ عَمّاتِكَ﴾, since the daughters of the paternal uncle and the daughters of the maternal uncle are lawful for people.
His words: ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما فَرَضْنا عَلَيْهِمْ في أزْواجِهِمْ وما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُمْ﴾, that is: marriage is not contracted except with a guardian (walī) and two witnesses, and ownership by the right hand is only of those whom it is lawful to take captive.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His words: ﴿تُرْجِي مَن تَشاءُ مِنهُنَّ وتُؤْوِي إلَيْكَ مَن تَشاءُ﴾: ”تُرْجِي“ is read with hamza and without hamza, and the hamza is more common and better. The meaning of ”تُرْجِي“ is: you postpone; with hamza or without hamza the meaning is one. This is among the things with which Allah singled out the Prophet — upon him be peace —: it was for him to postpone whichever of his wives he wished and to take to himself whichever of his wives he wished, and that is not for anyone else of his community; and he could return to his bed — upon him be peace — the one he had postponed. ﴿وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكَ﴾, that is: if you wish to take to yourself one of those you set aside, there is no blame on you. ﴿ذَلِكَ أدْنى أنْ تَقَرَّ أعْيُنُهُنَّ ولا يَحْزَنَّ ويَرْضَيْنَ بِما آتَيْتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّ﴾, that is: and that they all be content with what you give them, of drawing near or postponing. The accusative in ”كُلُّهُنَّ“ is also permissible, as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ and nūn.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّساءُ مِن بَعْدُ﴾: it is also read: ”لا تَحِلُّ لَكَ النِّساءُ“ with the tāʾ. Whoever reads with the yāʾ, it is because the yāʾ is in the sense of the plural of women «[Translator's note: so in the source; the argument seems to be that ”اَلنِّساءُ“ is a plural (jamʿ), hence the masculine verb is allowed]», and ”اَلنِّساءُ“ indicates the feminine, so the feminine marking of ”يَحِلُّ“ can be dispensed with. ”لا تَحِلُّ“ with the tāʾ is also permissible, on the meaning "the group of women is not lawful for you".
His words: ﴿وَلا أنْ تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِن أزْواجٍ ولَوْ أعْجَبَكَ حُسْنُهُنَّ إلا ما مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ﴾: the position of ”ما“ is nominative; the meaning is: "nothing is lawful for you except what your right hand possesses"; he made ”ما“ a badal (substitute) for ”اَلنَّساءُ“. The position of ”ما“ may also be accusative, on the meaning: "women are not lawful for you; I except what your right hand possesses".

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ﴾ with ḍamma on the bāʾ. ”بِيُوتَ“ with kasra on the bāʾ has been related from ʿĀṣim and from a group of the people of Kufa. The Basrans do not relate ”بِيُوتَ“ with kasra on the bāʾ; rather, they say that a ḍamma after a kasra does not exist in the speech of the Arabs nor in their poetry. Those who read the kasra seem to have aimed at harmonizing it with the yāʾ. The preferred reading among the Kufans is the ḍamma in ”بُيُوتَ“.
His words: ﴿إلا أنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكم إلى طَعامٍ﴾ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: "except by its being permitted to you", or "because it is permitted to you".
His words: ﴿إلى طَعامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إناهُ﴾: ”إناهُ“ is its being cooked and its being ready. One says: ”أنى، يَأْنِي، إناءً“ when it is cooked and ready. ”غَيْرَ“ is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "except that permission be given to you, not waiting [for it]". The genitive in ”غَيْرَ“ is not permissible, because if it were a naʿt (adjective) of the food, the agent would have to be made overt; only ”غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إناهُ أنْتُمْ“ would be permissible.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إنَّ ذَلِكم كانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنكُمْ﴾: ”فَيَسْتَحِي مِنكم“ with a single yāʾ is also permissible, and likewise His words: ﴿واللَّهُ لا يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾, and ”يَسْتَحِي“ with lightening, on [the pattern of] ”اِسْتَحْيَيْتُ“ and ”اِسْتَحَيْتُ“; the omission is because of the heaviness of the two yāʾs. The Prophet ﷺ used to bear their lingering out of his generosity and endure the annoyance in that, so Allah taught those who attended him good manners, and it became a code of manners for them and for those after them.
His words: ﴿وَإذا سَألْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتاعًا فاسْألُوهُنَّ مِن وراءِ حِجابٍ﴾, that is: when you want to address the wives of the Prophet ﷺ about a matter, address them from behind a screen. So the command to be screened was revealed.
His words: ﴿وَما كانَ لَكم أنْ تُؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: it is not for you to harm him in any matter whatsoever. ﴿وَلا أنْ تَنْكِحُوا أزْواجَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ أبَدًا﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is nominative; the meaning is: "and it is not for you to marry his wives after him". That is because it was mentioned that a man said: "When Muḥammad dies, I will marry his wife so-and-so." So Allah made known that this is forbidden, by His words: ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكم كانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمًا﴾, that is: it is a grave sin.

zajjaj:55-55.t: His words: ﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ في آبائِهِنَّ ولا أبْنائِهِنَّ﴾: their paternal uncles and maternal uncles are not mentioned in this passage. It has come in the exegesis that He did not mention the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle because each of them is lawful for the woman's daughter, so she is lawful for her paternal cousin and her maternal cousin; so it is said: that was disliked because the two of them would describe her to their sons. This verse was revealed about the veil (al-ḥijāb), concerning those before whom it is lawful for the woman to appear. So the father and the son were mentioned, to the end of the verse; the meaning is: "there is no blame on them in their fathers' seeing them". He did not mention the paternal uncle and the maternal uncle because they are treated like the parents as regards seeing. The naming of the paternal uncle as a father has come in the Quran, in His words: ﴿قالُوا نَعْبُدُ إلَهَكَ وإلَهَ آبائِكَ إبْراهِيمَ وإسْماعِيلَ وإسْحاقَ إلَهًا واحِدًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 133], where He made the paternal uncle a father.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ المُنافِقُونَ والَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ والمُرْجِفُونَ في المَدِينَةِ لَنُغْرِيَنَّكَ بِهِمْ﴾: the meaning is: "We shall surely give you power over them". ﴿ثُمَّ لا يُجاوِرُونَكَ فِيها إلا قَلِيلا﴾ ﴿مَلْعُونِينَ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 61] is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "they will not be your neighbours except while they are accursed".
His words: ﴿أيْنَما ثُقِفُوا أُخِذُوا﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 61]: it is not permissible for ”مَلْعُونِينَ“ to be made accusative by what comes after ”أيْنَما“; you may not say: ”مَلْعُونًا أيْنَما ثُقِفَ أُخِذَ زَيْدٌ يُضْرَبُ“, because what comes after the conditional particles does not govern what precedes them.

zajjaj:62-62.t: His words: ﴿سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ في الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلُ﴾: ”سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ“ is accusative through the sense of His words: ”أُخِذُوا وقُتِّلُوا“. So the meaning is: "Allah has laid down as His way, concerning those who act hypocritically towards the prophets and spread alarming rumours about them, that they be slain wherever they are found".

zajjaj:67-67.t: His words: ﴿إنّا أطَعْنا سادَتَنا وكُبَراءَنا فَأضَلُّونا السَّبِيلا﴾: the preferred reading is ”اَلسَّبِيلا“ with an alif, pausing on it, because at the ends of verses and their fawāṣil (verse endings) the same is done as is done at the ends of lines of poetry and at rhymed endings, since the Arabs were addressed with what they understand in composed speech. So pausing in these things and adding letters in them, as in ”اَلظَّنُونا“, ”اَلسَّبِيلا“ and ”اَلرَّسُولا“, indicates that the speech is complete and has ended, and that what follows it is a new start.

zajjaj:68-68.t: His words: ﴿والعَنْهم لَعْنًا كَبِيرًا﴾: it is also read: ”كَثِيرًا“, and their meanings are close.

zajjaj:69-69.t: His words: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ آذَوْا مُوسى﴾, that is: do not harm the Prophet — upon him be peace — as the companions of Moses harmed Moses — upon him be peace —, lest there befall you what befell them. Their harming Moses — according to what has come in the exegesis — was that they found fault with him over something in his body. One day he bathed and put his garment on a stone, and the stone went off with his garment; Moses followed it, and the Children of Israel saw him and did not see that defect by the mention of which they had harmed him. ﴿وَكانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وجِيهًا﴾: Allah spoke to him directly, and cleared him of the defect they had accused him of by a miraculous sign.

zajjaj:72-72.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا عَرَضْنا الأمانَةَ عَلى السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ والجِبالِ فَأبَيْنَ أنْ يَحْمِلْنَها وأشْفَقْنَ مِنها وحَمَلَها الإنْسانُ إنَّهُ كانَ ظَلُومًا جَهُولا﴾: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that they both said: ”اَلْأمانَةُ“ (the trust) here is the obligations that Allah has imposed on His servants. Ibn ʿUmar said: "Obedience and disobedience were presented to Adam, and he knew the reward of obedience and the punishment of disobedience." The true sense of this verse — and Allah knows best — and it agrees with the exegesis, is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, entrusted the children of Adam with the obedience to Him that He imposed on them, and entrusted the heavens, the earth and the mountains with obedience to Him and submission to Him. Allah informed us that He said: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إلى السَّماءِ وهي دُخانٌ فَقالَ لَها ولِلأرْضِ ائْتِيا طَوْعًا أوْ كَرْهًا قالَتا أتَيْنا طائِعِينَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 11], and He informed us that among stones there are those that fall down for fear of Allah, and that the sun, the moon, the stars, the angels and many people prostrate to Allah. So Allah informed us that the heavens, the earth and the mountains did not bear (lam taḥtamil) the trust, that is: they discharged it. Everyone who betrays the trust has borne it, and likewise everyone who sins has borne the sin; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أثْقالَهم وأثْقالا مَعَ أثْقالِهِمْ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 13]. So Allah made known that whoever incurs sin is called a bearer of sin. Thus the heavens, the earth and the mountains refused to bear the trust and discharged it — and discharging it is obedience to Allah in what He commanded, acting upon it, and abandoning disobedience — and man bore it. Al-Ḥasan said: the disbeliever and the hypocrite bore the trust and did not obey. This is the meaning — and Allah knows best. As for those who obeyed, of the prophets, the truthful and the believers, it is not said [of them]: ”كانَ ظَلُومًا جَهُولًا“. The confirmation of that is what follows this verse, His words: ﴿لِيُعَذِّبَ اللَّهُ المُنافِقِينَ والمُنافِقاتِ والمُشْرِكِينَ والمُشْرِكاتِ ويَتُوبَ اللَّهُ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ والمُؤْمِناتِ وكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 73]

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Aḥzāb
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾ — its meaning is: stand firm in the fear of Allah and continue in it.
His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾ — i.e. "He was knowing of what will be before it comes to be, wise in what He creates before His creating it."

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿واتَّبِعْ ما يُوحى إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ — He means by it the Qur'an.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وكِيلا﴾ — its meaning is "Allah suffices as a guardian." The bāʾ entered with the sense of a command, even though its wording is the wording of a statement; the meaning is: "Be content with Allah as a guardian."

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن قَلْبَيْنِ في جَوْفِهِ﴾ — «Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed, and he became absent-minded as men become absent-minded in their prayer, and a word occurred to his mind; so the hypocrites said: "He has two hearts: a heart with you and a heart with his companions."» Most of what has come in the tafsīr is that Quraysh used to call ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khaṭal "the one with two hearts," and it is related that he said: "I have two hearts, with each of which I understand more than Muḥammad understands." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave him the lie and said: ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن قَلْبَيْنِ في جَوْفِهِ﴾. Then He joined to this speech what other idolaters say that has no reality, and He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أزْواجَكُمُ اللائِي تُظاهِرُونَ مِنهُنَّ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾ — and it is read ”تَظّاهَرُونَ مِنهُنَّ“. Whoever reads ”تُظاهِرُونَ“, without doubling, it is according to your saying ”ظاهَرَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ امْرَأتِهِ“; and whoever reads ”تَظّاهَرُونَ“, with doubling, it is according to ”تَظاهَرَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ امْرَأتِهِ“. Its meaning is that he said to her: "You are to me like my mother's back." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that a wife does not become a mother. The people of the Jāhiliyya used to divorce with these words, so Allah sent down the expiation for ẓihār in Sūrat al-Mujādala.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أدْعِياءَكم أبْناءَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. He has not made the one whom you call a son, though he is not in reality a child [of yours], a son. They used to inherit from one another on the basis of the Hijra, and the Bedouin did not inherit from the Emigrant, even if kinship made inheritance due to him. So Allah made known that blood relatives are nearer to one another, and He abolished inheritance by the Hijra.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكم قَوْلُكم بِأفْواهِكُمْ﴾ — i.e. your claiming the lineage of someone whose lineage has no reality is a saying with the mouth, with no reality of meaning beneath it. ﴿واللَّهُ يَقُولُ الحَقَّ وهو يَهْدِي السَّبِيلَ﴾ — i.e. Allah does not make one who is not a son a son; and He guides to the way, i.e. He guides to the straight way, like His saying: ”فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ“.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿ادْعُوهم لآبائِهِمْ هو أقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ — i.e. it is more just. ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا آباءَهُمْ﴾ — i.e. if you do not know that the one so called is the son of so-and-so, then he is your brother in religion, if he is a believer; i.e. then say: "O my brother." ﴿وَمَوالِيكُمْ﴾ — i.e. your cousins; and it is possible that ”وَمَوالِيكم“ means your allies in religion. ﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ فِيما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ ولَكِنْ ما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ — there are two aspects in this. One of them: "There is no blame on you for what you erred in of what you did before you were forbidden this, but [there is] in what your hearts intended," i.e. but the sin is in what your hearts intended. ”ما“ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined onto the first ”ما“; the meaning is: "There is no blame on you in that in which you erred, but in that which your hearts intended." And it may be: "There is no blame on you in saying to him 'O my son', without your intending to treat him as a child in inheritance."

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿النَّبِيُّ أوْلى بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ وأزْواجُهُ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ﴾ — in one reading: ”اَلنَّبِيُّ أوْلى بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ وهو أبٌ لَهم“ (and he is a father to them), but it is not permissible to recite it, because it is not in the muṣḥaf agreed upon. The Prophet, upon him be peace, is the father of the community in reality. The meaning of ﴿وَأزْواجُهُ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ﴾ is: the wife of the Prophet ﷺ is not lawful for anyone after him, since she is in the position of a mother.
His saying: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحامِ بَعْضُهم أوْلى بِبَعْضٍ في كِتابِ اللَّهِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ والمُهاجِرِينَ﴾ — i.e. a blood relative is nearer to his blood relative than the Emigrant, if [the Emigrant] is not one of his blood relatives.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إلا أنْ تَفْعَلُوا إلى أوْلِيائِكم مَعْرُوفًا﴾ — ”إلّا أنْ“ is an exception not from the first [i.e. a disconnected exception]; the meaning is: "but your doing a kindness to your allies is permissible," which is that a man bequeaths to someone with whom he has a bond of alliance whatever he wishes of his third, if that person is not an heir, because there is no bequest for an heir. ﴿كانَ ذَلِكَ في الكِتابِ مَسْطُورًا﴾ — i.e. that was inscribed in the Book in which the obligation was prescribed; i.e. written.
